# ═══ 2026-08-28 · BLUE LIGHT — PHASE 3: ENGINEER GUIDED SERVICE + CALIBRATION WIZARD · testing_agent 100% ═══
Phase 3 of the Blue Light epic — the on-site engineer wizard. Reuses svc_cases for faults (reactive case, NO
new fault type), crm2_contract_assets for the register, crm2_station_visits as the visit state. Mobile-first.

  • BACKEND routes/crm_contracts.py (appended ~L1881+), CRM v2 router (get_crm_user, testable):
    - GET  /crm/v2/visits/{id} — full wizard state via _visit_state(): pack, per-asset audit+service merge,
      calibrations, faults, progress counters, completion_blockers (plain English §22), can_complete, steps.
    - POST /visits/{id}/start (§6 confirm_on_site → in_progress + started_at + optional gps).
    - POST /visits/{id}/assets/{key}/audit (§8: present|update|not_found|replaced|add). update/replace writes
      changes to crm2_contract_assets + audit trail crm2_asset_changes (§36); add inserts new asset flagged
      office_review; not_found sets status+reason. Stored in crm2_asset_verifications (upsert per asset).
    - POST /visits/{id}/assets/{key}/service (§11 outcome enum + notes + optional check_sheet_id).
    - POST /visits/{id}/treadmills/{key}/calibration (§14-§19): _calc_calibration() grades each speed/incline
      point pass/review/fail — FAILURE = |measured-target|/target*100 > tolerance_pct(5); target incline 0 uses
      abs band (0.5). overall=fail/review/pass/incomplete. Keeps original + retest in history[] (§17/§20) and
      pushes calibration_history onto the asset. Returns last_calibration.
    - POST /visits/{id}/faults (§12/§44): creates a reactive svc_case (next_reference/compute_sla_targets,
      source=blue_light_visit) prefilled station/asset/engineer/visit; increments visit.faults_raised; out_of_
      service flags the asset.
    - POST /visits/{id}/complete (§22-§24): blocks unless can_complete or override_reason; requires signature;
      computes next_service_due (+freq months); sets certificate_status = awaiting_review (office_review default)
      else pending_generation; marks station completed + svc_case repaired. Audit logged.
    - POST /visits/{id}/partial (§39): status follow_up_required, no certificate. _station_rows now returns
      visit_id so the matrix can deep-link.
  • FRONTEND pages/CRM/Contracts/BlueLightVisitWizard.js (NEW) — route /blue-light/visit/:visitId (AppRoutes.js),
    reads localStorage crm_token. Start screen (confirm-on-site gate) → 6-step progress bar (Asset Check, Service,
    Calibration, Faults, Review, Sign) → completion screen. Bottom-sheets for audit/add/service/calibration/fault;
    large buttons + NumPad for calibration; signature canvas. Dummy-proof Sign step lists blockers with 'Go to'.
    Matrix (BlueLightTab.js) station name deep-links to the wizard for open visits (bl-open-visit-<site_id>).
    data-testids: start-visit-btn, step-tab-*, asset-row-*, audit-present/-update/-notfound, add-asset-*,
    service-outcome-*, calib-asset-*, calib-numpad/numpad-*, calib-target/-measured/-result/-fail-action/-retest,
    raise-fault-btn/fault-*, review-panel, sign-blocked/blocker-goto-*, sign-panel/sign-name/sign-canvas/
    complete-visit-btn, save-partial-btn, visit-completed.
  • VERIFIED: backend curl full flow (audit→service→calibration 12mph=13→8.33%>5%→FAIL→retest PASS, history
    [fail,pass]→fault SVC-00009→complete next_due +6mo, cert awaiting_review; blocked while treadmill uncalib).
    testing_agent frontend 85%→ fixed 2 HIGH (calibration onSubmit swallowed response; Retest didn't clear

# ═══ 2026-08-10 · SECURITY · Abuse Auto-Response escalation ladder (§33) — behaviour-based (tests 26/26) ═══
Built deterministic abuse auto-response driven by the denial signals the authorisation engine already emits (no AI fingerprinting).
  • NEW utils/abuse_guard.py: record_denial(user, request, reason) counts denials per actor (email, else IP) in a rolling window
    (ABUSE_WINDOW_SECONDS=300) and escalates: throttle@8 → force step-up@15 → suspend writes@25; suspension cooldown 900s. Every
    escalation → security_events (abuse_detected critical/warning). check_abuse(user, action) enforces on WRITE actions only.
  • SAFEGUARDS (no legit lock-outs): only DENIED attempts count; READS never blocked; master/pulse admins exempt; all time-boxed
    with auto-cooldown; enforcement gated by ABUSE_GUARD_ENFORCED (default true, conservative thresholds).
  • RESPONSES: SUSPEND → 429 + Retry-After; STEP_UP → 403 step_up_required {reason:'unusual_activity'} (reuses existing step-up FE
    dialog — the App.js interceptor already retries after re-auth).
  • WIRED into utils/authz.py authorize_resource: check_abuse at top (writes, non-admin) + record_denial on cross_tenant/cross_owner/
    cross_site denial branches. Index registered at boot (server.py). Config env: ABUSE_THROTTLE_AT/STEPUP_AT/SUSPEND_AT.
  • ALERT CENTRE: added 'abuse' category (abuse_detected/abuse_action_blocked/abuse_stepup_required) to backend EVENT_CATEGORIES +
    frontend chip 'Abuse / auto-response'.
  • TESTS: NEW tests/test_abuse_guard.py (4) — escalate+block writes but allow reads, step-up band forces reauth, admin exempt,
    disabled no-op. Added to CI gate (pre-deploy.sh §0c, ci.yml security-gate, Makefile security). Full suite 26/26 PASS.
    Backend /api/health=200; SecurityAlertCentre babel OK; bash -n + ci.yml YAML validated.
  ⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — REDEPLOY (Save to GitHub for the workflow/Makefile/pre-deploy changes). Behaviour: an actor that trips 25 authz
    denials in 5 min has WRITE actions paused for 15 min (reads unaffected, admins exempt).
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Closed the contract skip-approval holes. Two existed: (1) sign_contract activated from ANY status (draft→active); (2) send

    rejected/sent/signed/active/expired/terminated/cancelled). draft/negotiation/amended CANNOT reach sent/signed/active/approved —
    only pending_approval→approved, then approved→sent/signed/active.

    pending_approval), sign (→active/signed, blocks unapproved draft).

    rejected) with a security event; public customer sign defensively asserts current→active is legal. Re-sending an approved/
    active contract still works (precise guard, not a blanket transition).
  • tests/test_security_authz_matrix.py: +test_contract_workflow_lock → 13/13 PASS. Backend /api/health=200; modules import clean.

# ═══ 2026-06 · Rate-limit + account-lockout moved to a SHARED MongoDB store (survives restarts, spans all pods) — verified ═══
The per-IP throttle, login/reset limiters and account-lockout lived in per-process dicts in utils/security.py, so a restart
wiped every counter and each pod enforced its OWN allowance (N pods = N× the limit; an attacker throttled on one pod was
free on the next).
  • Migrated all of them to the shared `rate_buckets` collection in MongoDB (the same store the async middleware limiter in
    utils/security_plus.py already uses). Function signatures are UNCHANGED (still sync) — ZERO call-site edits across the
    ~20 callers in auth.py / security_document.py / security_manifest.py / public_demo_request.py / signup_journeys.py /
    service_provider.py / master_admin_users.py — so there was no risk of a missed `await` silently disabling a control.
  • NEW in utils/security.py: a LAZY sync pymongo handle `_rl_col()` (built on first use, never at import, 1.5s timeouts →
    can't hang an Atlas SRV boot) + `_sliding_window_hit()` (atomic `$pull` stale + count + `$push`, mirrors the async
    limiter). `rate_limit` / `rate_limit_by_ip` / `rate_limit_login` / `rate_limit_password_reset` now delegate to it.
    Account lockout rewritten to Mongo: `record_failed_login` pushes to `faillogin:<email>` + sets `lock:<email>.lock_until`
    at threshold; `check_account_lockout` reads the lock doc; `clear_failed_logins` deletes both; `clear_login_rate_limits`
    (Master-Admin unlock) `delete_many` on `^(login|ip):`; `get_failed_login_count` reads the window. `updated_at` stored as
    a BSON **date** so the existing 24h TTL index actually sweeps abandoned buckets.
  • FAIL-OPEN (logged) if the store is briefly unreachable, so a DB blip degrades gracefully instead of causing a total auth
    outage. Buckets are keyed by the SEC-002 spoof-resistant client IP.
  • VERIFIED — unit: sliding window blocks the 6th of 5; lockout after 6 fails; **still locked after a simulated restart**
    (durability); unlock after clear. LIVE via the real ingress: 5×401 → **429**, and the bucket is present in Mongo
    (`login:104.198.214.223`, `updated_at` = BSON date). No refs to the removed in-memory globals remain.

# ═══ 2026-06 · SEC-002 FIX — X-Forwarded-For spoofing locked down (per-IP throttle + admin IP allow-list) — live-verified ═══
The client-IP derivation trusted the LEFT-most X-Forwarded-For value, which is fully client-controlled → an attacker could
rotate a fake XFF to mint a fresh rate-limit bucket per request (bypassing the 5/5min login throttle) and could forge an
allow-listed source IP for the master-admin IP allow-list.
  • MEASURED the real proxy chain (temp debug log on the external endpoint): honest XFF =
    `<client>, <cloudflare>, <gcp-lb>` (3 entries); an injected XFF lands to the LEFT of `<client>`, i.e. the trusted infra
    ALWAYS appends exactly 2 entries (Cloudflare + GCP LB) to the right of the real client. So the real client is at index
    `-3` (`-(hops+1)`, hops=2).
  • NEW canonical utils/security.py `client_ip(request)`: reads XFF from the RIGHT and skips `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` (env,
    default **2**) trusted appenders → returns the entry the trusted chain recorded for the client; anything a client injects
    is further left and ignored. Falls back to X-Real-IP / socket peer when there's no full chain (dev/local). `_client_ip`
    kept as a thin alias.
  • ROUTED ALL five duplicate derivations through it: utils/security.py (rate_limit_by_ip / login / password-reset +
    account-lockout via auth.py), utils/hardening.py `_extract_client_ip` (master-admin IP allow-list),
    utils/security_plus.py `client_rate_key` (middleware limiter), routes/staffing_orgchart.py `_oc_client_ip`,
    routes/widget_embed.py `_client_ip`.
  • VERIFIED — unit: honest user → own IP (no throttle breakage); 1-fake & 2-fake spoofs → still resolves the true client at
    `-3`; dev single / no-XFF fallbacks correct. LIVE (through the real ingress): 7 login attempts each with a DIFFERENT
    spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` left-most → 5×401 then **429** (throttle keyed on the true IP, not the rotating spoof). Temp
    debug logging removed; grep confirms zero remaining left-most-XFF security parsing.
  • CONFIG: `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` defaults to 2 in code (not added to .env to avoid touching secrets) — set it in the prod
    env only if the deployment's trusted proxy count differs.
  ⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION needs a REDEPLOY. If prod sits behind a different number of trusted proxies, set
    TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS accordingly (re-measure the same way).
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


# ═══ 2026-06 · CSP hardening (P2/P3) — dropped script-src 'unsafe-inline' in production; prod-build validated 0 violations ═══
Removed the XSS-relevant `'unsafe-inline'` from the PRODUCTION script-src by externalising every inline executable script.
  • EXTERNALISED inline <script>s from frontend/public/index.html → NEW public/pwa-brand.js (PWA brand/manifest swap),
    perf-error-suppressor.js (PerformanceServerTiming DataCloneError suppressor), posthog-init.js (PostHog bootstrap).
    index.html now references them via <script src="%PUBLIC_URL%/…">. Only type="application/ld+json" DATA blocks remain
    inline (not executed → not subject to script-src).
  • frontend/.env: added INLINE_RUNTIME_CHUNK=false so CRA no longer inlines the webpack runtime chunk (it becomes an
    external /static/js file). Confirmed in a prod build: 0 inline executable <script> blocks.
  • CSP (PRODUCTION) — backend/server.py + frontend/public/_headers: script-src dropped 'unsafe-inline' (now only 'self' +
    the allow-listed CDNs: challenges.cloudflare/js.hcaptcha/js.stripe/assets.emergent.sh/*.posthog.com/
    *.i.posthog.com/static.cloudflareinsights.com). ADDED `worker-src 'self' blob:` (a blob: Web Worker was falling back to
    script-src and getting blocked — the tight fix is worker-src, not re-loosening script-src). style-src KEEPS 'unsafe-inline'
    (Tailwind/emotion inject runtime inline styles — removing breaks the app; nonce/hash infeasible for a static CRA build).
    'unsafe-eval' was already removed in a prior iteration.
  • DEV/PREVIEW — frontend/craco.config.js (webpack-dev-server, the CSP the PREVIEW actually enforces): KEEPS 'unsafe-inline'
    + 'unsafe-eval' (HMR/React refresh need them in dev — do NOT remove or preview breaks). Added the same external
    allow-list (assets.emergent.sh/posthog/cloudflareinsights) + worker-src to clean up pre-existing preview console
    violations (those domains were never on the dev allow-list, so emergent-main.js/PostHog/CF-beacon were being blocked in
    preview — harmless telemetry, now allowed). /docs+/redoc still exempt from the backend CSP (swagger needs inline+eval).
  • VALIDATED: ran a real `yarn build`, served build/ under the EXACT hardened production CSP, loaded headless →
    / , /login , /MODService , /pulse all render (React mounts, root innerHTML 6k–110k) with **0 CSP violations**. Live
    preview /login re-screenshotted clean after aligning the craco CSP (dev-server warmup showed a transient 'Loading…').
  ⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY for code; the _headers CSP takes effect on the next Cloudflare Pages deploy, server.py CSP on backend
    redeploy. No behavioural/UX change. Test artifacts (build/, temp servers) removed.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    explicit ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=1 override is set. Fail-safe: remote/managed prod Mongo host → refuses before connecting.

    connection or write. seed_pulse_equipment_demo.py (pymongo, writes at module level) guarded before MongoClient().

    seed_site_isolation_demo.py with MONGO_URL=remote host → exit 1 with guard message, NO writes). All 12 scripts
    ast-parse clean. Preview seeds still work (local DB) with zero config; no .env change needed.

    used a localhost sidecar Mongo the host heuristic would need revisiting.

# ═══ 2026-08-06 · SECURITY AUDIT — FIX SEC-001 credentialed CORS origin reflection (HIGH) — verified ═══
security_audit_agent flagged ONE HIGH (SEC-001): with allow_credentials=True the CORS allow-list resolved to ["*"]
whenever APP_ENV/ENVIRONMENT were unset (they are unset in preview AND prod), so Starlette reflected ANY request
origin + ACAC:true → any website a logged-in user visited could read their (cross-tenant) data. Confirmed live.
FIX (utils/security_plus.py — env-agnostic, no reliance on APP_ENV):
  • resolve_cors_origins() NEVER returns "*" anymore (unsafe with credentials). It always returns an explicit
    allow-list: _BRAND_DEFAULT_ORIGINS (pulsefitness.ai, www, fitness-ai-migrate.emergent.host) + localhost in non-prod.
    A literal CORS_ORIGINS='*' is now ignored in EVERY environment (logged), not just prod.
  • resolve_cors_origin_regex() now ALWAYS returns the Emergent platform regex (preview.emergentagent.com|emergent.host)
    so preview redeploys + the deployed host keep working without a wildcard.
VERIFIED (curl direct to :8001 = app CORS layer): attacker origin → NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (was
  reflected before); prod host + preview subdomain → exact-origin echoed + ACAC:true (allowed). Login 200 + health ok
  (same-origin app flow unaffected). Backend log: "CORS_ORIGINS='*' ignored (unsafe with credentials)".
  NOTE: the preview/prod INGRESS separately returns ACAO:* (without exact-origin reflection) on OPTIONS — that variant
  is NOT browser-exploitable for credentialed reads (browsers reject '*'+credentials); it's a platform-layer header
  outside our code.
STILL OPEN (lower priority, flagged to user — NOT changed):
  • SEC-002 (LOW/P3): _client_ip() trusts left-most X-Forwarded-For (utils/security.py:18) → per-IP throttle +
    master-admin IP allow-list spoofable. Correct fix needs the trusted proxy hop count (CF→ingress); a blind change
    risks breaking rate-limits, so left as a recommendation. Per-account lockout (5/15min) still applies.
  • Hardening (P3): in-memory rate-limit resets per deploy; SameSite=None cookie w/o CSRF tokens; plaintext
    onboarding password at rest; MasterAdmin123! fallback when env unset; CSP script-src 'unsafe-inline' (CRA build).
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION still has the CORS hole until a REDEPLOY ships this fix.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ═══ 2026-08-06 · EQUIPMENT FACTORY-BARCODE SCANNER (gym staff + engineers) — E2E verified ═══
Machines leave the Pulse factory with LINEAR barcodes (numeric serial e.g. 17150704760 = unique per-machine
identifier, already stored as equipment.serial_number; model code e.g. 510H-AAA = the model). Phones auto-open the
app from a QR but NOT from linear barcodes, so gym staff needed an in-app scanner that lands on the SAME options page
the QR opens (/scan/{id} → Complete Maintenance Check / Report a Fault / Update Equipment Photo).
BACKEND:
  • NEW GET /api/equipment/scan/resolve?code=&site_id= (routes/equipment.py, authed get_current_user, org-scoped via
    get_organization_filter + apply_site_lock for site-locked staff). Match order: (1) exact unique
    serial_number/asset_tag/sticker_code/barcode/id → {match:"exact",equipment}; (2) model / model_code case-insensitive
    exact → single = exact, several = {match:"multiple",options[]} (the '510H-AAA can hit multiple machines, pick one'
    case); (3) fuzzy contains fallback. 404 when nothing matches.
  • Engineer lookup routes/svc/engineer_equipment.py GET /svc/engineer/equipment/by-code/{code} EXTENDED to also match
    `barcode` + `model`/`model_code` (returns multiple options on a model hit) so both factory labels work for engineers
    (history / log parts flows already hang off the resolved machine).
FRONTEND:
  • NEW components/equipment/EquipmentScanModal.js — camera scanner via native BarcodeDetector
    (qr_code, code_128, code_39, ean_13/8, upc_a/e, itf, codabar) + manual-entry fallback (iOS Safari). A scanned QR
    (/scan/{id} URL) jumps straight in; a linear code calls the resolver → exact navigates to /scan/{id}, multiple shows
    a 1-tap chooser, 404 shows a friendly retry. Uses react-router navigate.
  • pages/EquipmentInfoTab.js (Operations → Equipment): NEW MOBILE-ONLY "Scan barcode" button (data-testid
    scan-barcode-btn, class sm:hidden so it only shows on phones) in the search/filters row; renders <EquipmentScanModal
    siteId={user.active_site_id}>.
  data-testids: scan-barcode-btn, equipment-scan-modal, equipment-scan-video, equipment-scan-manual-input/-submit,
    equipment-scan-switch-manual, equipment-scan-error, equipment-scan-options, equipment-scan-option-<id>, equipment-scan-close.
VERIFIED: curl (serial PF-TM-260-01 → exact 1 machine; model 260G → multiple=2; unknown → 404) + mobile-viewport
  screenshot E2E (owner@isodemo.com): Scan button present in DOM & correctly hidden at desktop width; modal opens;
  manual lookup 'PF-TM-260-01' → navigated to /scan/2bcb45df-… → the SAME options page (Maintenance Check / Report Fault /
  Update Photo). Camera path not headless-testable but mirrors the production BarcodeScanModal. Babel + webpack clean.

# ═══ 2026-07-31 · SECURITY — FEATURE LOCKDOWN AUDIT (Pulse-only features cross-tenant sweep) — READ-ONLY, NO CODE CHANGE ═══
Follow-up to the MOD Quote Writer leak fix. Swept the other Pulse-only / cross-org features for the SAME class of bug
(an intentionally cross-org read exposed on ordinary user/CRM auth with no operator/admin gate). RESULT: the MOD Quote
Writer was the ONLY instance; everything else is correctly isolated. No code changes required.
Findings (all SAFE):
  • Tenders (crm_v2.py /tenders*) — org-scoped via _of(user) (organization_id = caller's org); nav is feature-flag
    gated (crm_tenders). A customer sees only its OWN tenders, never the operator's.
  • MOD Estate (master_admin_mod_estate.py) — all 22 admin endpoints call require_master_admin. The 3 UNGUARDED
    endpoints are the PUBLIC /public/mod-capture/{token}(/submit) equipment-capture forms — no-auth BY DESIGN,
    gated by a secure random token + IP rate-limit (same pattern as booking forms).
  • Estate modules rollup (master_admin_estate_rollup.py) — local _require_master (is_master_admin/is_pulse_admin).
  • Sicon (sicon.py) — config is per-org (get_sicon_config(org_id)=caller's org), owner/manager gated; every
    sync-by-id endpoint re-checks the issue/contract belongs to the caller's org via get_organization_filter.
  • MOD visits/booking (svc/mod_visits.py) — list/booking-link org-scoped; public booking forms secure-token gated.
  • MOD drill (mod_portal.py /master-admin/mod/sites/{id}/drill/*) — require_master_admin + equipment ownership check.
  • CAPEX cross-org (capex.py /capex/master-admin/overview) — is_master_admin check before the broad org read.
  • Admin analytics (admin_analytics.py) — local require_admin (is_master_admin) in all 5 endpoints.
  • Platform integrity (platform_integrity.py) — admin-gated (10 guards / 6 endpoints).
Method: grep for (a) db.organizations enumeration (find({}) / account_type mod filters) and (b) equipment/data reads
by an arbitrary request-param org/site id, on non-admin auth; then read each hit's guard. No new leak found.

Reported (PRODUCTION): a customer org ("Penkridge") could see Pulse Fitness's MOD customers via CRM "MOD Auto Quote".
ROOT CAUSE (NOT a master-admin flaw — master admin cross-org visibility is by-design for the platform owner):
  the MOD Quote Writer (routes/crm_mod_quote.py) is a Pulse-internal, deliberately cross-tenant tool (it reads across
  MOD *site* orgs so Pulse can quote the whole estate) but every endpoint was gated only by get_crm_user (ANY CRM
  login) with NO operator-org check. GET /crm/mod-quote/mod-sites enumerated ALL orgs with account_type mod_site/mod_org
  platform-wide; GET /crm/mod-quote/equipment?site_id= returned ANY site's equipment (no ownership check). Frontend
  showed the "MOD Auto Quote" button to every CRM user. → cross-tenant exposure of MOD customer + equipment data.
FIX:
  • BACKEND crm_mod_quote.py: new dependency require_operator_crm_user — allows ONLY Pulse platform admins
    (is_master_admin / is_pulse_admin / role pulse_master_admin) OR a caller whose org has the authoritative
    is_operator_company flag (Pulse Fitness Ltd, id 3ece2d0c-57ea-4acd-a6b4-d748478ed117). Applied to ALL 9
    authenticated router endpoints (rate-card get/put/reseed, mod-sites, equipment, ai-match, generate, contracts,
    send-esign). Public token e-sign router unchanged. Uses is_operator_company (not a name/brand heuristic) for the
    security boundary.
  • FRONTEND CRMCPQ.js: "MOD Auto Quote" button (data-testid mod-quote-btn) now renders only when
    canModQuote = crm.user.is_pulse_internal || is_master_admin (UX layer; backend 403 is the real guard).
VERIFIED (curl): owner@isodemo.com (non-operator org) → 403 "MOD quoting is restricted to Pulse Fitness." on
  /mod-sites, /equipment, /rate-card. admin@pulsefitness.com (operator/master) → 200, 7 MOD sites returned. Frontend
  babel-parse OK.
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — the leak is LIVE on PRODUCTION (fitness-ai-migrate.emergent.host); a REDEPLOY is required to close it
  there. Only 1 org carries is_operator_company=true (Pulse Fitness Ltd) — confirm the same on production before/after
  redeploy.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ═══ 2026-07-29 · MASTER-ADMIN STAFF INVISIBLE IN OPERATIONS > STAFF > HR (FIXED, verified) ═══
Reported: a staff member added to "Pulse Fitness Ltd" via Master Admin didn't appear in the end-user portal's
Operations → Staff → HR list.
RCA: `_create_org_user` (master_admin.py) routes a new user to `db.users` AND/OR `db.crm_users` based on the org's
portal_type / enabled modules. For a CRM-primary org (Pulse Fitness Ltd historically had portal_type='crm'), staff
land ONLY in `crm_users`. But Operations HR's auto-backfill `_ensure_staff_for_org_users` (staffing.py) read ONLY
`db.users` → CRM-collection staff never got a `staff_members` row → invisible in HR (same collection-split family as
the CRM territories bug).
FIX: `_ensure_staff_for_org_users` now UNIONs `db.crm_users` with `db.users` (dedup by user_id + email) before
backfilling, so every internal team member surfaces in Operations HR regardless of which collection they were written
to. Idempotent; existing manual HR overrides (primary_role_source='manual') preserved.
VERIFIED (preview, direct call): seeded a crm_users-only staff for Pulse Fitness Ltd → after backfill a matching
staff_members row exists (active, user_id bound, primary_role mapped). Preview state restored (test rows removed).
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION needs a REDEPLOY. Note: on first HR open post-deploy, ALL existing internal crm_users for
an org will be surfaced into staff_members (intended unification).

# ═══ 2026-07-29 · CRM DURING IMPERSONATION — "Invalid CRM token" 401 LOOP + empty Territories reps (FIXED) ═══
Reported (recurring): impersonating an org → CRM shows "Invalid CRM token" (top-right), Territories shows "No CRM
users yet" despite Engineers/Sales Managers added in Operations>HR, and some Territories toolbar buttons render blank.

RCA (reproduced via master-admin → org-portal impersonate "Pulse Fitness Ltd" → /crm, network capture):
  • ROOT: infinite CRM cross-login loop. crm/auth/cross-login returned 200 repeatedly (dozens/render) but
    localStorage.crm_token was NEVER persisted → every CRM call 401'd. Cause: cross-login bound the CRM identity to
    the ambient MASTER-ADMIN ga_session COOKIE (privileged) instead of the impersonation/portal BEARER token (whose
    `impersonated_by` claim was dropped by a token refresh). So identity.crm.org (admin's org) ≠ identity.main.org
    (impersonated org) → the frontend UnifiedAuthProvider org-mismatch guard stripped the freshly-minted token every
    render → re-mint → loop → 401 storm → "Invalid CRM token" + empty CRM data.
  • Territories reps: /crm/territories/team/tree read db.crm_users but never synced Operations Staffing (HR) field
    staff into crm_users — while the /users endpoint did. So even with a good token, engineers/sales managers didn't
    appear as assignable reps.

FIX (2 parts):
  1) BACKEND crm_auth.py cross-login: prefer the EXPLICIT bearer identity over ambient ga_session cookies when it can
     reach CRM (new bearer_user tracked at candidate index 0; selected right after impersonation_user, before the
     privileged-cookie loop). Binds CRM to the org the SPA is acting as → no org mismatch → no strip/re-mint loop.
     Stale-bearer fix preserved (a deleted/invalid bearer resolves to no user → still falls through to cookie).
  2) BACKEND crm_territories.py team_tree: now calls sync_staffing_to_crm_users(org) before reading crm_users
     (idempotent, best-effort) so HR engineers/sales managers appear as territory reps.

VERIFIED (impersonation → /crm, network capture): crm_token PERSISTS; cross-login calls 0 (was dozens); total /api
401s = 0 (was 8+); no "Invalid CRM token" / no "No CRM users" text; CRM dashboard renders with visible labels.
team_tree curl: seeded HR Engineer + Sales Manager now returned as reps (were absent). Regression-safe: normal user
& master-admin DIRECT CRM login still bind to their own org (bearer = their token).
OUTSTANDING: Issue-1 "blank Territories toolbar buttons" could NOT be directly reproduced — the Territories MAP is
feature-gated for the synthetic portal impersonation user, so my repro path can't open it. Strong likelihood it was a
downstream symptom of the 401 loop (toolbar rendered in a broken state); --color-brand-blue / seg-active CSS vars are
defined globally so it's not an undefined-var issue. → Ask user to re-verify after redeploy; if it persists, get a
fresh screenshot from their real (Pulse-internal) session.
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION needs a REDEPLOY (the user hit this on production).
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ═══ 2026-07-29 · BACKEND GUARD (belt-and-braces) FOR THE IMPERSONATION SITE-SCOPE BUG (VERIFIED) ═══
Follow-up to the frontend site-scope fix. Root of the "data disappears" behaviour on the backend:
utils/site_scope.build_site_filter() does NOT verify org-membership for an UNRESTRICTED user — it returns
{"site_id": X} for ANY id, so a stale/foreign/cross-org site_id (leaked from a master-admin impersonation switch)
produced an empty result set (HTTP 200, zero rows) rather than an error → equipment & faults silently vanished.
FIX: utils/mod_scope.resolve_mod_query_filter() non-MOD branch now, for an UNRESTRICTED user, checks the requested
site_id against db.sites for the caller's org; if it doesn't belong, the site filter is dropped → treated as
ALL SITES (org-wide) instead of an empty set. Restricted users are untouched — build_site_filter still 403s them for
a disallowed site and we never widen their scope. Covers BOTH /equipment and /issues (both route through this helper),
and any other caller of resolve_mod_query_filter. File: backend/utils/mod_scope.py (+ import get_request_site_scope).
VERIFIED via curl: owner@isodemo — /equipment?site_id=ghost-foreign-999 → 20 items (== org-wide, was 0); valid
site-a → 18 (correctly scoped); /issues?site_id=ghost → 25 (== org-wide). manager@isodemo (restricted to site-a):
ghost → 403, disallowed site-b → 403, allowed site-a → 200 (RBAC intact).
Net: the impersonation "equipment/faults disappeared" bug is now fixed at BOTH layers (frontend no longer sends a
leaked site_id; backend ignores a foreign site_id for owners instead of returning empty).
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION still needs a REDEPLOY for both the frontend and backend fixes to land.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────



# ═══ 2026-07-29 · PROD BUG FIX — EQUIPMENT/FAULTS "DISAPPEAR" AFTER LOGGING A FAULT WHILE IMPERSONATING (VERIFIED) ═══
Report: on PRODUCTION, master admin impersonating "Penkridge leisure centre" logged an engineer-callout fault →
all equipment & faults vanished; exiting + returning restored them. RCA (code-trace): NOT data loss — a client-side
SITE-SCOPE bug. useDashboardData.loadData() builds ?site_id= by reading `active_site_cache` from localStorage
directly (SSoT divergence). Impersonation start (App.js ?impersonation_token=) did NOT reset site scope, and
loadSites() auto-reset a stale/foreign activeSite to siteList[0] AND persisted it to active_site_cache. First paint
raced ahead (no filter → all shown); the engineer-callout path (useIssueWorkflow.handleCreatePOAndLog → loadData())
then refetched WITH the now-populated site_id → /equipment & /issues returned 200-empty for that (equipment-less)
site → everything vanished. Logout wipes active_site_cache → reappeared on return.
FIX (frontend-only, 3 parts):
  1) App.js impersonation-start block: on ?impersonation_token=, clear active_site_cache/active_site_all/sites_cache
     + setActiveSite(null)/setAllSitesMode(false) → impersonated org ALWAYS starts org-wide.
  2) useDashboardData.loadData(): only apply ?site_id= when the cached site's id is present in the current user's
     sites_cache (ignores a stale/cross-org/auto-defaulted site silently filtering out everything).
  3) App.js loadSites() reset branch: when `current` site isn't in the org's list (stale/impersonation leak), RESET
     TO ORG-WIDE (remove active_site_cache/active_site_all) instead of persisting siteList[0] — protects the
     page-reload-mid-impersonation variant too.
VERIFIED via impersonation + network inspection (screenshot script): (a) impersonate Iso Demo w/ pre-injected stale
foreign site → active_site_cache=None, 0 stale site_id on /equipment|/issues, equipment loads; (b) inject leaked
ghost site then RELOAD → active_site_cache cleared to None, /api/equipment sent with NO site_id (fully org-wide),
0 ghost hits, dashboard intact. Files: frontend/src/App.js, frontend/src/pages/Dashboard/hooks/useDashboardData.js.
⚠️ PREVIEW ONLY — PRODUCTION (pulsefitness.ai / fitness-ai-migrate.emergent.host) NEEDS A REDEPLOY for the fix to land.

# ═══ 2026-06 (this session) · BUGFIX · "Logged fault not showing" + AI triage portal-awareness ═══
Two production-reported issues (pulsefitness.ai; impersonating somerslee@hotmail.com, Pulse Fitness Pro,
Penkridge Leisure Centre HO). Fixed in PREVIEW code — REQUIRES REDEPLOY to reach production.

1) FAULT LOGGED BUT NOT SHOWING in the Faults screen (shows "No faults logged"). ROOT CAUSE: asymmetry
   between the equipment and issues per-site queries. `GET /equipment?site_id=X` HEALS the view with an
   `$or` that also returns site-less rows (routes/equipment.py:183-188), but `GET /issues?site_id=X`
   (routes/issues.py:1075) did an EXACT `{"site_id": X}` match via build_site_filter — no heal. A fault
   logged against site-less equipment is stamped site-less (create_issue only inherits the equipment's
   site_id, and falls back to the reporter site which is null for a privileged/owner user with no
   allowed_site_ids), so the exact per-site filter dropped the just-logged fault. FIX: mirrored the
   equipment `$or` heal in `GET /issues` — when a specific site is requested (non-MOD path), also surface
   `{site_id:{$exists:false}}` / `{site_id:null}` rows. VERIFIED via preview API: a site-less issue now
   appears in `?site_id=iso-demo-site-a` (contains new? True; previously excluded).

2) AI TRIAGE told staff to "Log a service call with Pulse Fitness" — the triage LLM didn't know it runs
   INSIDE the PulseFitness.ai portal where submitting the fault already dispatches the engineer. FIX: added
   a "PLATFORM CONTEXT" block to `_TRIAGE_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` (routes/issue_helpers.py) instructing the model
   not to tell users to log a call / contact Pulse / raise a ticket / book an engineer as a separate action,
   and to phrase engineer hand-off as "this fault will be sent to the assigned engineer via the portal".
   VERIFIED via a live triage call (treadmill belt tear): step 4 now reads "…will be sent to the assigned
   engineer via the portal", no forbidden external-call phrases.

Both backend-only; self-tested via curl (small targeted fix, no testing_agent needed).

# ═══ 2026-07-21 · MODAL FOOTER CUT-OFF FIX (all consoles) ═══
User reported the Memberships "Add member" and "New ad" modals cut off the last field/text behind the
Save footer (couldn't scroll far enough). Root cause: footers used `sticky bottom-0` INSIDE the scroll
container, so the pinned footer floated over the last content at max scroll.
Fix pattern applied everywhere: flex-column card → header (fixed) → body `flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0`
→ footer `flex-shrink-0` (footer pulled OUT of the scroll area). No more overlap.
Files: Memberships/_shared.js (ModalShell/ModalActions — covers Add member ✅ verified, New ad, Record
payment + all Memberships modals), Memberships/FamilyTab.js, CRM/LeadConversionModal.js,
CRM/CRMProductDrawer.js, ServiceOps/Engineer/EngineerCustomers.js, MasterAdmin/PartnerApplicationDrawer.js,
MasterAdmin/SiteDetailDrawer.js. All compile clean; zero `sticky bottom-0` footers remain.

CRM Documents cross-org leak (2026-07-20): confirmed a stale-token DISPLAY bug (docs correctly org-stamped);
user confirmed docs were uploaded by orgs' own users → NO backfill required. Both fixes ship on next redeploy.

Follow-up (2026-07-21): Extracted a canonical shared modal primitive `components/shared/Modal.jsx`
(`Modal` + `ModalFooter`) — the single source of truth for the header / scroll-body / fixed-footer
structure that prevents footer cut-off by construction. Memberships `_shared.js` `ModalShell` now delegates
to it (public API + `ModalActions` unchanged; verified Add member still renders + scrolls clear). New modals
should use `<Modal … footer={<ModalFooter …/>}>` rather than hand-rolling a scroll container.

Guard script (2026-07-21): `frontend/scripts/check-modal-footers.js` (run `yarn lint:modals`) fails CI if any
`sticky bottom-0` footer is reintroduced (the cut-off anti-pattern). Opt out with a `sticky-footer-ok`
comment. Mirrors the existing `lint:overlays` guard. Currently PASSES (zero offenders).

A11y hardening (2026-07-21): the shared `Modal` primitive now includes a focus trap (Tab/Shift+Tab cycle
within the dialog), initial focus into the dialog on open, focus restore to the trigger on close, ESC-to-close
and body scroll-lock. Verified on Add member (focus lands inside dialog; ESC closes; trigger re-focused).
Every modal using the primitive (Memberships + future) inherits this automatically.

NOTE on migrating the 6 remaining bespoke modals/drawers (CRM/ServiceOps/MasterAdmin): NOT done as a batch —
they are structurally different (right-side DRAWERS vs centered modals), independently themed (prop-based
`c`/`isDark` or explicit light/dark rather than the primitive's `--theme-*` CSS vars), and one uses
framer-motion. They are already cut-off-fixed. Migrating them wholesale would risk visual regressions for
little functional gain; recommend migrating individually with before/after visual checks if desired, or first
extending the primitive with a `variant="drawer"` + theme passthrough.

Drawer variant + first migration (2026-07-21): extended `Modal` primitive with `variant="center|drawer"`
(right-side sheet), custom `header` node, `bodyClassName`, `panelClassName`/`panelStyle` (theme passthrough),
and `zClassName` (drawers over modals, e.g. z-[260]). `size` now accepts a raw Tailwind width (e.g. "max-w-xl").
Migrated `CRM/CRMProductDrawer.js` onto it — VERIFIED visually (right sheet, light theme, header/scroll-body/
Archive+Save footer intact, no regression) + a11y (focus trap/ESC/restore/scroll-lock) inherited. All other
markup/data-testids preserved. Remaining drawers (PartnerApplicationDrawer, SiteDetailDrawer, EngineerCustomers,
LeadConversionModal, PulseUpgradeRequestModal) can now follow the same pattern one-by-one with visual checks.

MasterAdmin drawer migration (2026-07-21): migrated `MasterAdmin/PartnerApplicationDrawer.js` onto the
`Modal` primitive (variant=drawer, custom header/footer nodes, dark-mode passthrough via panelClassName,
new `panelTestId` prop to preserve the panel's test id, z-50). VERIFIED visually (right sheet, pills, scroll
body, fixed Approve/Reject footer, no regression). `SiteDetailDrawer.js` was NOT migrated — its tabbed layout
has TWO per-tab footers inside one scroll body, which doesn't map to the primitive's single `footer` slot
without restructuring the tabs; left as-is (already cut-off-fixed). Remaining un-migrated: SiteDetailDrawer,
EngineerCustomers (3-step wizard), LeadConversionModal (success state), PulseUpgradeRequestModal (framer-motion).

OPS NOTE (2026-07-21): the `/app` volume (9.8G) hit 100% — cause was `frontend/node_modules/.cache`
(webpack persistent cache) ballooning to 6.2G. Cleared it (safe, regenerates). If `/app` fills again,
`rm -rf /app/frontend/node_modules/.cache` frees it.

Modal migrations round 2 (2026-07-22): migrated `CRM/LeadConversionModal.js` onto the primitive
(center variant + `panelStyle` theme override + `backdropClassName="bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-sm"` +
`zClassName="z-[90]"`). VERIFIED visually (header, all sections, fixed Cancel/Convert footer, blurred
backdrop, no cut-off). Added primitive props: `panelTestId`, `backdropClassName`. Success-state sub-modal
left as-is (no scroll/footer, no cut-off risk).
Still un-migrated (optional, already cut-off-fixed): SiteDetailDrawer (tabbed dual-footer),
EngineerCustomers (3-step wizard), PulseUpgradeRequestModal (framer-motion).

BUILD/RESOURCES (2026-07-22): cold webpack builds were extremely slow (CPU-throttled ~1.25 cores) after the
cache wipe, and a gzip cache-compression experiment caused an OOM — reverted that craco tweak (known-good).
Added `GENERATE_SOURCEMAP=false` to frontend/.env (faster preview builds; ESLint plugin already disabled).
User UPGRADED Emergent resources to 16 cores / 64GB RAM → frontend now cold-builds & serves in ~15s. All
services healthy (frontend/backend 200), `/app` at 48%.

Pre-deploy guard (2026-07-22): added `frontend/scripts/check-cache-size.js` (auto-prunes the webpack cache
if it exceeds 3 GB, protecting the /app volume) and a single `yarn predeploy` script that chains
`lint:overlays && lint:modals && check:cache`. Verified: all three pass (cache 1105 MB). Recommend wiring
`yarn predeploy` into CI / the redeploy step so modal-cut-off regressions and disk-bloat are caught automatically.

# ═══ 2026-07-07 · ONBOARDING → PORTAL EQUIPMENT VISIBILITY (P0, VERIFIED frontend 100%) ═══
BUG: After onboarding a customer, equipment showed at ORG level (Master Admin "18 equip") but the end-user
portal Equipment tab showed "No equipment found". Two chained root causes, both fixed:

1) MISSING site_id ON IMPORTED/ONBOARDED EQUIPMENT. The portal per-site Equipment query is
   {organization_id, site_id} (build_site_filter → site_scope), but onboarded equipment had NO site_id, so it
   was excluded from every per-site view (only visible under "All sites"). Fixes:
   - master_admin_pulse.py: onboard_pulse_site now threads the created site_id into _create_onboard_equipment /
     _create_kit_equipment / _create_manual_equipment (equipment docs carry site_id).
   - equipment_import.py: new helper _resolve_import_site_id(org_id, explicit) — confirm_import &
     confirm_bulk_import now default site_id to the org's PRIMARY/first site (old code only inferred when the
     org had EXACTLY one site, so multi-site/head-office imports got none).
   - equipment.py GET /equipment: per-site view now also includes site-LESS equipment of the same org
     ($or: site_id==requested / absent / null) — non-destructive heal so existing/legacy broken data (e.g. the
     production "18 equip" org) surfaces immediately after deploy without a migration.

2) PORTAL DEFAULTED TO AN EMPTY AUTO-HEAD-OFFICE. GET /sites (sites.py) auto-creates a "Head Office" site when
   an org has sites but none flagged is_head_office, and sorts HO first → the portal defaulted to the empty HO
   (0 eq) so the owner still saw "No equipment found" on first load (found by testing agent after fix #1). FIX:
   onboard_pulse_site now inserts its single site with is_head_office=True → no empty HO is auto-created, the
   switcher shows ONE site (the one holding the equipment) as default. Later branches attach under it.

VERIFIED: backend E2E via external URL (new-site onboarding → owner sees 3/3 equipment per-site; confirm import
→ primary site assigned; legacy site-less row surfaces). Frontend E2E (testing agent, 100%,
iteration_onboarding_equipment_default_site_retest_jan2026.json): brand-new owner logs in → Equipment tab shows
all items on FIRST load, single Head-Office site, no empty HO chip. Head-office branch mode already passed
site_id explicitly (unaffected). Reports: iteration_onboarding_equipment_portal_visibility_jan2026.json (+retest).

# ═══ 2026-07-03 · P0 DEPLOY FIX · Prod crash-loop — litellm loaded at import scope (VERIFIED 15/15) ═══
SYMPTOM: Production k8s deploy failed repeatedly — backend never bound :8001, nginx GET /health →
"connection refused", readiness probe timed out → crash-loop. Prod logs showed the startup banner
(captcha + python-magic) then NOTHING (no "Started server process"), i.e. a hang DURING module import.
Preview was fine (open egress + local mongodb://).

ROOT CAUSE: 13 route/util modules imported `emergentintegrations.llm.chat` (→ transitively loads the
heavy `litellm` package) at MODULE-IMPORT scope. uvicorn imports `server` (→ all routers) BEFORE binding
the port, so litellm loaded — and could attempt network — before :8001 opened. In the egress-restricted
prod rollout container this hung/over-ran the readiness window. Import measured 9.94s locally; litellm
was ~2.7s of it plus network risk.

FIX: converted every module-scope `emergentintegrations.llm` / `litellm` import to lazy function-local
imports (TYPE_CHECKING guards for the few type-annotation-only uses; added `from __future__ import
annotations` to routes/svc/ai.py). Files: routes/{gym_layouts,equipment,ai_diagnosis,qr_codes,files,
admin_documents,issues,issue_helpers,crm_v2,risk_assessments,capex,svc/ai}.py + utils/incident_ai.py.
RESULT: `import server` no longer loads litellm; import 9.94s→5.42s, time-to-/health 9s→6s.
GUARD: new `test_no_heavy_llm_imports_at_module_scope` in tests/test_no_blocking_imports.py (AST scan of
routes/route_registry/utils/bootstrap top-level statements; TYPE_CHECKING/function-local exempt). Both
guard tests pass.

VERIFIED (testing agent, backend 15/15 @ external URL): health 200; live LLM endpoints /api/chat/diagnose,
/api/svc/ai/triage, /api/capex/generate-justifications, /api/risk-assessments/ai-generate all 200 (lazy
imports resolve at request time); issues-triage import path reached without error; test-data purge tool
200 (auth) / 401 (anon). NO ImportError/NameError 500s anywhere. Regression suite:
tests/test_ai_lazy_import_regression_jan2026.py. Report:
/app/test_reports/iteration_lazy_llm_import_regression_jan2026.json.
ACTION: SAFE TO REDEPLOY pulsefitness.ai. Non-blocking pre-existing quirks noted (predictive-maintenance
& ai-scan-duplicates 404 route/id mismatch — unrelated to this fix).

# ═══ 2026-07-02 · DEPLOY FIX · File uploads HTTP 415 in Prod (missing libmagic) ═══
SYMPTOM: file/image uploads (equipment photos, fault attachments, CSV imports, CRM docs) returned HTTP 415 in
PRODUCTION. Root cause: the prod container has no `libmagic` → `python-magic` fails to import, and
`utils/file_validation.py::validate_upload()` guards every upload endpoint. (Confirmed: `import magic` also fails
in PREVIEW — the pure-Python fallback sniffer is what keeps preview working.)

FIX (two layers, both belt-and-suspenders):
1. Added `libmagic1` + `file` to `backend/packages.txt` (the deployment apt-package manifest — previously only
   `poppler-utils`). On next redeploy the prod container gets libmagic, restoring it as the PRIMARY MIME sniffer.
2. Verified the existing pure-Python fallback (`_sniff_mime_fallback`, already in the current code) correctly
   classifies every accepted type WITHOUT libmagic — tested PNG→image/png, JPEG→image/jpeg, PDF→application/pdf,
   CSV→text/csv, XLSX→…spreadsheetml.sheet. So uploads succeed even if libmagic is ever missing again.

ACTION (production): REDEPLOY pulsefitness.ai. The redeploy (a) installs libmagic1 via packages.txt and (b) ships
the current fallback validator — either alone fixes the 415, together they're resilient. Backend health = 200 in preview.

# ═══ 2026-06-30 · DEPLOY BLOCKER FIXED · weak JWT_SECRET aborted production startup ═══
SYMPTOM: production redeploy of "fitness-ai-migrate" (pulsefitness.ai) FAILED — k8s never became ready,
nginx /health → "connection refused". Because the deploy failed, production kept running the OLD build, so
(a) Lee still landed on the Master Dashboard and (b) the role dropdown still showed "Owner" — none of this
session's code fixes were live.

ROOT CAUSE: backend aborted on startup. `utils/secrets_audit.py::run_startup_audit(abort_on_critical_in_prod=
True)` calls sys.exit(2) in production (APP_ENV=production) when JWT_SECRET is <32 chars or contains a known-
weak substring. backend/.env had `JWT_SECRET=gymaxis-ai-secret-key-2026` (26 chars, weak) → CRITICAL → exit(2)
→ /health never served → deploy timeout. (Preview has APP_ENV unset, so it never aborted there.)

FIX: set a strong JWT_SECRET in backend/.env (64-char secrets.token_hex(32), no 'gymaxis'). Verified by
simulating the production audit (APP_ENV=production): 0 CRITICAL findings (only 1 HIGH: CORS '*', which does
NOT abort). Backend reboots clean, /health=200, login works with the new secret.
deployment_agent scan: compilation passes, no other blockers (1 WARN: .gitignore blocks .env — not the actual
blocker since the deploy snapshot already carried env values; primary blocker was the weak value).

⚠️ JWT_SECRET rotation invalidates ALL existing tokens → everyone re-logs in (expected; also explains the
"session expired" toast Lee saw).

USER ACTIONS:
1. REDEPLOY pulsefitness.ai — should now succeed.
2. After deploy: re-set lee.somers@pulsefitness.com to "Master Admin" in Pulse Fitness Ltd → People. Since
   Pulse Fitness Ltd is Pulse-branded, role becomes pulse_master_admin → dropdown shows "Master Admin (Pulse)".
3. Lee re-logs in → lands on the Pulse Fitness Ltd platform (org_is_operator routing) with Master Admin in the
   profile menu.
NOTE: if production uses a separate deployment env-var config (not the snapshotted backend/.env), the strong
JWT_SECRET must be set there too (≥32 random chars). If the redeploy still fails, contact Emergent Support.

# ═══ 2026-06-29 · ANALYSIS + FEATURE · Sicon import-readiness audit + Phase-1 import gaps closed ═══
Founder asked: is pulsefitness.ai ready to auto-import customers/equipment/contracts from Sicon once
credentials are entered, and where are the gaps? Scale: 5,000+ customers, 300,000 equipment.

AUDIT (grounded in the 3 real Sicon OpenAPI specs — stored in memory/SICON_API_AUDIT_2026-06.md):
- Customers/contacts: ✅ auto-pullable via CRM.R221200c `GET /api/CRM/Companies` + `/People` (paginated).
- Contracts: 🔴 Contracts.R260200c is PUSH-ONLY (4 POST endpoints, no GET/list) — cannot pull from Sicon.
- Equipment (300k): 🔴 no installed-asset list in Service/CRM specs (StockItems = product catalogue, not
  serial assets). Service embeds `Equipment` only on cases; a generic paged `TEntity` reader exists but no
  documented equipment route. User confirmed equipment lives in Sicon Service + needs ongoing two-way sync
  → BLOCKED pending a Sicon equipment/asset API doc or Sage 200 API access (Sage KB link provided, gated).
- The existing Sicon integration is an OPERATIONAL case/contract SYNC engine, not a bulk onboarding importer.

PHASE-1 BUILD (no API dependency — option C, VERIFIED):
- NEW Contracts CSV importer: `GET /api/master-admin/bulk-import/templates/contracts` +
  `POST /api/master-admin/bulk-import/contracts` → `crm2_contracts`. Idempotent on `contract_number` per org,
  batched insert_many (500), 200MB cap, links CRM company by name, captures `sicon_contract_id`/`sage_reference`.
  (routes/master_admin_bulk_import.py). Tested: 2 imported, idempotent re-run skipped 2, sicon_contract_id stored.
- Equipment bulk import now captures `sicon_equipment_id` + `sage_item_id` (template + doc builder) so migrated
  assets carry Sicon linkage for the ongoing sync. (Already batched + idempotent on serial — good for 300k.)
- Master Admin → Bulk Imports UI: added a 4th "Bulk import contracts" card + updated equipment columns.

NEXT (Phase 2, when user supplies docs/decision):
- Build "Import customers from Sicon" auto-pull (CRM API, paginated, idempotent on Sage ref) — feasible now.
- Equipment + contract auto-sync BLOCKED — need Sicon equipment/asset API doc OR Sage 200 WebAPI access.

# ═══ 2026-06-25 · BUGFIX (PRODUCTION) · Onboarding invoice upload → Cloudflare 520 (VERIFIED) ═══
Report (production pulsefitness.ai, Master Admin onboarding): invoice uploads failed with
"The origin web server sent a response that Cloudflare could not process" (Cloudflare 520).
URGENT — onboarding hundreds of customers next week, need 100% reliability.

ROOT CAUSE: small invoices (≤1.5MB) used a SINGLE synchronous POST to
`/api/equipment-import/parse-invoice` where the (slow) AI extraction ran INSIDE the request.
When extraction exceeded the production gateway/Cloudflare ~100s timeout the connection was
dropped → Cloudflare 520. Large files already used a decoupled background job, so only
small-but-slow invoices were affected.

FIX:
- `frontend/src/lib/uploadInvoice.js` `uploadInvoiceSmart` now ALWAYS chunks (even a tiny file =
  one chunk) → finalize → decoupled background job → poll `/status`. No invoice upload ever holds
  a synchronous request open during extraction, so the gateway timeout / 520 can't happen.
- `backend/routes/equipment_import.py`: chunk storage moved from local `/tmp` to MongoDB
  (`db.invoice_upload_chunks`, one doc per chunk, deleted on finalize) so reassembly works
  regardless of which production REPLICA handles each chunk vs the finalize call (the /tmp approach
  would break across pods). finalize returns a job_id immediately; the asyncio worker extracts and
  writes the result to `db.invoice_parse_jobs` (shared, so any pod can serve the status poll).

VERIFIED: testing agent 6/6 pytest @ external URL — single-chunk done (equipment_count/supplier/
import_id), multi-chunk reassembly of a ~3.2MB PDF, bogus upload_id → 404 (no hang), corrupt file →
clean job error (not 520), chunk docs cleaned up, finalize returns <10s. Frontend compiles clean;
UI couldn't be auto-driven (documented master-admin CSP harness limitation, not a regression).

ACTION (production): preview-only code fix — **redeploy pulsefitness.ai** to push it live.

# ═══ 2026-06-25 · BUGFIX · Master-admin module disable was bypassable via the trial CTA (VERIFIED) ═══
Report: "When modules are switched off for customers in Master Admin they are still showing when that
customer logs in." Root cause (NOT the ModuleSwitcher — that correctly hides disabled modules, and the
backend `resolve_module_access` correctly returns the module as off): when a customer hit a disabled
module's route, `ModuleAccessGate` showed the **"Start 3-day free trial"** upgrade screen because an
explicit master-admin disable was indistinguishable from "never opted in". The customer could click the
trial and self-re-enable a module the admin had turned off (POST /me/module-trials/start flipped
`modules.<key>.enabled=true`).

FIX:
- `utils/module_access.trial_status()` now returns per-module `admin_disabled` = (`modules.<key>.enabled is False`
  AND `source != "trial"`) — i.e. an explicit admin/seed disable, not an expired trial.
- Admin write paths stamp `modules.<key>.source = "admin"` so future toggles are unambiguous:
  `routes/master_admin_orgs.update_org_features` (Feature Control matrix) + `update_org_details` (Modules picker sync).
- `routes/module_trials.start_module_trial` returns **403** ("disabled by your administrator") when
  `admin_disabled`; `upgrade_to_pro` skips admin-disabled modules in its auto-trial loop.
- Frontend `ModuleAccessGate` renders a "{Module} is turned off — contact your administrator" screen
  (no trial CTA) when `trials.<module>.admin_disabled` (non-Lite orgs).

VERIFIED end-to-end (preview, owner@isodemo with Marketing disabled): /me/module-trials → admin_disabled:true;
POST trial start → 403; /marketing route → "Marketing is turned off" screen. ModuleSwitcher already hides
the pill. Backend logic unit-checked (admin-disabled vs trial-revoked vs enabled). ESLint clean.

# ═══ 2026-06-24 · BUGFIXES · Large invoice upload + Org add-site false 401 (both VERIFIED) ═══
Two production bugs reported by Master Admin:
1. **Large invoice upload "Network Error"** — the platform proxy enforces a 2MB request-body limit
   (413 'Request body exceeds 2097152 bytes' → browser Network Error). A 9.3MB invoice failed.
   FIX: chunked uploads. New backend endpoints in `routes/equipment_import.py`:
   `POST /api/equipment-import/parse-invoice/chunk` (≤2MB slices) → `POST …/parse-invoice/finalize`
   (returns a job_id, runs extraction in a DECOUPLED asyncio background task so a client disconnect /
   gateway timeout can't cancel it) → `GET …/parse-invoice/status/{job_id}` (poll). Frontend helper
   `src/lib/uploadInvoice.js` (`uploadInvoiceSmart`) auto-chunks files >1.5MB then polls; wired into
   `PulseOnboardingWizard.js` and `InvoiceImportWizard.js`. VERIFIED: 9.3MB PDF → 6 chunks all 200,
   finalize 200+job_id, background job done in ~105s, equipment_count=176.
2. **Org add-site "Save failed (401)" but it saved** — `OrgSitesPanel.submitNewSite` ran the POST and
   the follow-up refresh GET in the SAME try/catch; a transient 401 on the refresh surfaced as a false
   'Failed to create site'. FIX: only the POST is in the try/catch (success toast + optimistic
   `setSites` from the POST response); the refresh `loadSites()` is in its own isolated try/catch that
   swallows errors. VERIFIED end-to-end via Playwright (POST 200, success toast, new row, no false error).

Both were reported on PRODUCTION (pulsefitness.ai) — fixes are in PREVIEW and need a redeploy to go live.

ENHANCEMENT (2026-06-24): live invoice-parse progress. The background job now publishes
`phase` ('queued'→'extracting'→'done') and the real `page_count` (computed instantly via fitz). The
`uploadInvoiceSmart` helper fires an `onStatus` callback each poll + ramps the bar 85→97% during
extraction; `InvoiceImportWizard` and `PulseOnboardingWizard` feed it into the existing
`InvoiceParseProgress` component, which now animates "Reading page X of {N} with AI…" with the true
page count instead of a blank spinner. Verified end-to-end via curl (mid-extraction: phase=extracting,
page_count=26 for the 26-page Carshalton invoice).

Tier reference (asked by user): Pulse Fitness AI — Starter (CRM+Memberships+basic ops), Professional
(+Service Desk+AI triage+Sage outbox), Enterprise (multi-site, audit, SSO, custom SLA). Pulse — Lite
(equipment+faults+docs), Pro (full platform+AI+reports).

STILL OUTSTANDING (feature requests, not yet built): (a) CSV/spreadsheet import + template download in
the Onboard-Site wizard (note: OrgSitesPanel already has CSV import+template); (b) option to attach a
new onboarded site to a Head Office org.

# ═══ 2026-06-24 · BUGFIX · Onboarding "errors everywhere" = overlay click-interception ═══
Master Admin reported errors throughout the Onboarding hub (buttons/downloads/uploads). Backend was
100% healthy (all endpoints 200) — the real cause was UI overlay click-interception: `CookieConsent.js`
(`fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0`) and `PWAInstallPrompt.js` (`fixed bottom-4 left-4 right-4`) rendered
FULL-WIDTH transparent fixed wrappers whose empty padding sat on top of the Onboarding action buttons,
silently swallowing clicks (no network call, no toast → looked like "errors").
FIX: `pointer-events-none` on each banner wrapper + `pointer-events-auto` on the inner visible card.
Also hardened blob downloads (OnboardingReports.exportReport + AdminBulkImports.downloadTemplate) to
surface JSON error responses instead of saving a broken file. VERIFIED by testing agent: with the banner
physically overlapping a button, the click now fires (200) without force; banner's own buttons still work.

## Comms — Open/click tracking + conversion pipeline (Jun 23, 2026) ✅

Verified end-to-end (curl + UI): open pixel → opened+1; click → clicked+1, redirect, click-map populated; conversion logged → attributed → analytics shows count/rate/£revenue/by-type.
- **Open/click tracker on the new send path**: the dispatcher now injects a tracking pixel + rewrites every link through the tracker per recipient (message ids are clean uuids). Unauthenticated endpoints `GET /api/comms/t/o/{message_id}` (1×1 PNG → records open, increments `metrics.opened` once) and `GET /api/comms/t/c/{message_id}?u=<b64url>` (records click + URL, increments `metrics.clicked`, 302-redirects to the original link). Click URLs feed the campaign analytics **click map**.
- **Conversion pipeline** (`utils/comms_conversions.py`): `record_conversion(org, email, type, value_gbp, …)` attributes an outcome to the most recent campaign that reached that email within a 30-day window (clicked > opened > sent), stored in `comms_conversions`, and rolls `metrics.converted` + `metrics.revenue_gbp` onto the campaign. Authenticated `POST /api/comms/conversions` for integrations. Campaign analytics now computes real conversions (count, by_type, revenue, conversion_rate) and the analytics modal surfaces them + the click map.
- **Real hooks wired** (fire-and-forget, never break the flow): CRM quote sign/accept (`crm_v2.sign_quote` → `quote_accepted` + value) and member class booking (`bookings.py` → `class_booking`).


## Comms Phase 2 — Batch/timezone dispatch + AI-suggested segments (Jun 23, 2026) ✅

Tested: backend 7/7 pytest (100%), frontend Playwright green, full send loop verified (immediate → sending → sent via worker).
- **Batch + timezone SEND DISPATCH worker** (`utils/comms_dispatch.py`, registered in `server.py`, 30s loop, `COMMS_DISPATCH_INTERVAL_SEC`): activation resolves the campaign audience (segment_id or audience_inline) into one queued `marketing_messages` row per recipient, each stamped with a `scheduled_for` that bakes in the **batch offset** (size + interval pacing) and the **timezone strategy** (fixed tz, or each recipient's local hour via zoneinfo). The loop drains due rows in capped cycles (50/cycle), personalises merge tags per recipient, sends via Resend, bumps metrics, and flips the campaign to `sent` when the queue empties.
- **Send/schedule API** (`routes/comms.py`): `POST /campaigns/{id}/schedule` (strategy immediate|scheduled, send_at, batch_size, batch_interval_minutes, timezone_mode, tz, local_hour — validates content + audience), `pause-send`, `resume-send`, `GET .../dispatch` (progress).
- **Send UI** in the EmailBuilder: "Send" button → modal with segment picker, Send-now/Schedule, recipient-local timezone + hour, batch size/interval.
- **AI-suggested segments** (potential improvement): `POST /api/comms/segments/ai-suggest` (`comms_ai.suggest_segment`) turns plain English into a rule tree, **validated against the field catalogue**, with a live preview count; UI "AI suggest" button → pre-fills the SegmentEditor for review & save. ## Iter 279b — DEFINITIVE FIX: CRM lock-out was a STALE-TOKEN / wrong-identity auth bug ✅ (Jun 15, 2026)

**Report (production, CRITICAL):** Lee Somers AND Craig Henshall (both `pulse_master_admin`) still hit "CRM is not enabled for your account" at gymaxisai.com/crm after 4 iterations + 2 redeploys. Every Master Admin screen (GymAxis + Pulse) confirms they should have access.

**Why every previous fix failed (the real root cause — finally):** the CRM cross-login (`POST /crm/auth/cross-login`) authenticated using **ONLY the `Authorization: Bearer` header**, which the frontend fills from `localStorage['token']`. The app moved to httpOnly **cookie sessions** (`ga_session`) back in iter 227–232 (which has a whole saga about stale/duplicate cookies shadowing the fresh session). Long-lived accounts like Lee/Craig — who survived multiple re-registrations (the iter-272 stale-`user_id` saga) — carry a **STALE `localStorage['token']`** whose `user_id` points at an old/deleted record, while their **cookie session** holds the real, current `pulse_master_admin` login. So the cross-login kept resolving the **WRONG user** → `has_module()` False / user-not-found → 401/403 → lock-out. **No amount of fixing the entitlement resolver (`module_access.py`) mattered, because the wrong identity was being authenticated in the first place.** The People-drawer diagnostic looked correct because it reads the *current* directory record, not the stale token.

**Fix (`routes/crm_auth.py` cross-login):** authenticate against the CURRENT session, not just the bearer. The endpoint now (a) accepts an **optional** bearer + the **httpOnly cookie** (`request` + `_cookie_token_candidates`, handling the iter-231 multi-cookie case), (b) decodes **every** candidate token and resolves each to a live `users` row, and (c) picks the **CRM-capable identity** — a privileged admin first, else any CRM-entitled record — so a genuine Pulse/Platform admin can never be locked out by a stale bearer. Retains the iter-279 direct Pulse-admin recognition + duplicate-record safety net, and still 403s real no-access users. Frontend already sends the cookie (`axios.defaults.withCredentials = true`).

**Verified:** `tests/test_iter279_crm_crosslogin_pulse_admin.py` 5/5 — incl. **`test_stale_bearer_falls_back_to_current_cookie_session`** (bogus/stale bearer + valid Pulse-admin cookie → **200**, the exact prod bug), cookie-only → 200, pulse-admin in CRM-disabled org → 200, regular staff → 403, no creds → 401. Real-account curl: `pulse.admin.test`, `admin@gymaxisai.com`, `desk@pulsefitness.com` cross-login all **200**. iter278e 7/7, iter278f 1/1 (13 total green). In Makefile.

**ACTION (production):** preview-only code fix — **redeploy gymaxisai.com**. This time the cause is the cross-login authenticating a stale identity, now fixed at the source; Lee & Craig's CRM access no longer depends on which token their browser happens to send.

## Iter 279 — BUGFIX: Pulse Master Admin STILL locked out of CRM (recurring P0, root cause found) ✅ (Jun 15, 2026)

**Report (production gymaxisai.com, after the 278e/f redeploy):** Lee Somers (`lee.somers@pulsefitness.com`, role `pulse_master_admin`) STILL hits "CRM is not enabled for your account" at `/crm`. The Master Admin People-drawer diagnostic for Lee shows CRM ORG ✅ + USER ✅, "Full access — Pulse Master Admin", and the org's CRM module toggle is ON.

**Why 278e didn't actually fix it (the trap):** the People-drawer diagnostic (`master_admin_users._module_access_payload`) computes `privileged` with its OWN inline check and then forces `user_access = user_on or privileged` + `reason = "Full access — Pulse Master Admin"`. So Lee's green ticks are driven purely by the privilege flag — they do **not** prove the entitlement *resolver* (`resolve_module_access`, used by `has_module`) returns True. The previous agent read the green diagnostic as proof the resolver worked and kept editing `module_access.py`.

**Actual root cause (cross-login gate, not the resolver):** `POST /api/crm/auth/cross-login` computed `is_master = is_master_admin OR email==MASTER_ADMIN_EMAIL` — it did **NOT** recognise Pulse Master Admins (`role==pulse_master_admin` / `is_pulse_admin`, `is_master_admin=False`). So a Pulse admin fell through to `has_module()`, making the cross-login entirely dependent on the resolver in `utils/module_access._is_platform_admin`. Any deployment skew (prod `module_access.py` not carrying the 278e edit) or resolver edge case re-locked the admin out. The diagnostic stayed green the whole time, masking it.

**Fix (`routes/crm_auth.py` cross-login):** recognise Pulse Master Admins **directly in the gate** via a local `_is_priv()` (master/pulse-admin/role), so the exchange never depends on the module resolver for them — even when the org's CRM module is toggled OFF. Added a duplicate/mismatched-record safety net (email-based sibling lookup → grant + adopt that identity's org) for robustness, though `users.email` is unique so it's a belt-and-braces path. Ordinary staff in a CRM-disabled org are still denied (403).

**Verified:** new `tests/test_iter279_crm_crosslogin_pulse_admin.py` (2/2, real-HTTP integration): a Pulse Master Admin in a **CRM-disabled** org now gets a CRM token (200, was 403); a plain manager in the same org still gets 403. Curl regression: `pulse.admin.test` → 200, `admin@gymaxisai.com` → 200. `test_iter278e` 7/7, `test_iter278f` 1/1. Added to Makefile `regression:`.

**ACTION (production):** preview-only code fix — **redeploy gymaxisai.com**. After redeploy, Lee's cross-login no longer depends on the resolver, so the lock-out is gone regardless of any prod data/deploy skew.

## Iter 278e — BUGFIX: Pulse Master Admin locked out of CRM (recurring) ✅ (Jun 14, 2026)

**Report (production gymaxisai.com):** Lee Somers, a **Pulse Master Admin**, hits "CRM is not enabled for your account" at `/crm` even though his profile shows the CRM badge and his role has the CRM module ticked. Recurring.

**Root cause:** A Pulse Master Admin is stored as `role="pulse_master_admin"` with **`is_master_admin=False`** (that flag is reserved for the GymAxis operator). The People role editor markets the role as "platform-wide Master Admin access", but `utils/module_access.py` only treated `is_master_admin` or `role=="owner"` as privileged. So a Pulse Master Admin was gated like ordinary staff: if the org's CRM entitlement resolved to off (pulse_pro default is off, or his cross-org `organization_id` didn't point at the CRM-enabled org), `has_module(user, org, "crm")` returned False → the CRM cross-login (`POST /api/crm/auth/cross-login`) replied 403 → frontend `crmExchangeStatus = 'unavailable'` → the lock-out screen.

**Fix (central, one source of truth):** added `_is_platform_admin(user)` in `module_access.py` (True for `is_master_admin` OR `is_pulse_admin` OR `role=="pulse_master_admin"`) and used it in `_org_module_access`, `resolve_module_access`, and `crm_modes`. ## Iter 274b — Engineer App "Sign out" didn't sign out ✅ (Jun 14, 2026)

**Bug:** Engineer App sign-out (`EngineerAccountSettings.handleSignOut`) only did `localStorage.removeItem('token') + navigate('/login')`. The app now uses httpOnly cookie sessions (`ga_session`/`ga_refresh`) + an in-memory auth context, so the cookie survived → `LoginRedirectPage` saw the still-authenticated user and bounced the engineer straight back in.

**Fix:** `handleSignOut` now calls the shared `useAuth().logout()` (revokes the cookie via `POST /auth/logout`, clears all cached tokens, resets in-memory state, hard-navigates). Verified e2e: after sign-out URL = `/`, localStorage token = null, `/api/auth/me` = 401 (cookie revoked). Backend logout confirmed via curl.

**Reported (production):** pressing **Sign in** lands a partner engineer on the empty `/partner-engineer` "Become a Partner Engineer / Apply now" screen instead of their dashboard. (Previously misdiagnosed in iter 270 as a "stale production cache" — it was a real backend bug.)

**Root cause (reproduced):** the login claim hook (`utils/partner_claim.claim_pending_partner_for_user`) flagged the user `is_partner_engineer=True` by **email** match (→ frontend routes them to `/partner-engineer`), but the dashboard (`GET /partners/me` → `_get_partner_by_user`) resolves the partner row by **`user_id` ONLY**. When a `partner_engineers` row pointed at a stale/placeholder `user_id` (engineer's original account removed → re-registered with same email; `user_id` unique-indexed, email→row is 1:1), the two disagreed → flagged but empty dashboard. The claim hook only relinked `pending:` rows, not stale ones.

**Fix:**
- `utils/partner_claim.py` — claim hook now **self-heals**: finds the email's partner row (approved-first), and if it isn't already linked to the current user, relinks its `user_id` to the logged-in user (guards the unique-index edge). Runs on every login/register.
- `routes/partners.py` `GET /partners/me` — when the partner resolves to null, re-runs the claim hook then retries, so a stuck engineer heals on the dashboard request itself (no re-login needed).

**Verified:** seeded stale-link scenario → before: `/partners/me` partner=null (Apply screen); after login: relinked + partner returned. Happy path (engineer.smoke) still loads; non-partner users are NOT flagged. New regression `tests/test_iter272_partner_relink_selfheal.py` (2/2) added to Makefile `regression:`. Backend healthy, login 200.

**ACTION (production):** preview-only fix — **redeploy gymaxisai.com** to push it live.

**Proactive backfill (added):** `utils/partner_claim.backfill_partner_relink()` + standalone `scripts/backfill_partner_relink.py` (`--dry-run`/`--commit`) relink ALL stale/placeholder `partner_engineers.user_id` to their owning user in one pass (conservative: only relinks placeholders or dead ids, never steals a row from another live user). Wired as a marker-guarded one-time startup migration (`run_partner_relink_migration_once`, marker `partner_relink_backfill_v1` in `db.migrations`) so production auto-heals stranded engineers on the next redeploy without manual script runs. Verified: dry-run/commit relink a seeded stale row + flag the user; startup migration runs once then no-ops. Regression `test_iter272` now 3/3 (self-heal, non-partner no-op, backfill relink + don't-steal guard).

## Iter 267-HOTFIX — Production login 502 (refresh-token write crashed login) ✅ (Jun 13, 2026)

**Reported (production):** after deploying iter 267, Master Admin login at gymaxisai.com returned a Cloudflare **502** ("origin returned an invalid/incomplete response"). A wrong-password account returned a clean **401** — proving the backend was up and only the login **SUCCESS path** crashed.

**Root cause (high confidence):** iter 267 added `issue_refresh_token()` on the login success path (`_finalise_successful_login`), which does `db.refresh_tokens.create_index()` + `insert_one()` on a brand-new collection. In the **production** DB environment this write failed (most likely a restricted Mongo user lacking createCollection/createIndex/insert on the new collection, or an index-build/write issue) and the **unhandled exception crashed the login request → 502**. Preview (local Mongo, full perms) worked fine, which is why iter 267 passed all preview tests.

**Fix:** made the refresh-token feature **fully non-fatal** — `issue_refresh_token` and `renew_access_from_refresh` now wrap everything in try/except, log, and return `None` on any failure. The refresh cookie is a pure enhancement: if its DB write fails, **login still succeeds** and the session behaves exactly as pre-267 (access token + iter-266 proactive refresh). 

**Verified (preview):** login 200 (x3); `tests/test_iter267_refresh_token.py` **5/5**, including a new `test_issue_refresh_token_is_non_fatal` that forces `insert_one`/`create_index` to raise ("not authorized…") and asserts login proceeds with no cookie set.

**ACTION (production outage):** fix is in **preview**. Restore production by EITHER (a) **redeploy** gymaxisai.com with this hotfix, OR (b) **Rollback** to the checkpoint before iter 267 for instant recovery. Note: after redeploy, if the prod Mongo user can't write `refresh_tokens`, login works but the refresh-cookie feature silently no-ops (graceful degradation) — to make it active, grant the prod app DB user insert/createIndex on `refresh_tokens` (optional, not required for login).

## Iter 267 — Permanent session longevity: long-lived refresh token ✅ (Jun 13, 2026)

**Why:** follow-up hardening to iter 266. The single-token model meant any missed proactive refresh (frozen/slept tab past the access-token TTL) ended the session. Added a proper short-access + long-refresh split so sessions survive idle gaps, without weakening the hourly admin rotation.

**Design (deliberately conservative / additive / backward-compatible):**
- New **`ga_refresh`** HttpOnly cookie issued **only on real login/register** (NOT impersonation/CRM cross-login). Scoped to **`path=/api/auth`** (least privilege — only sent to auth endpoints), Secure, SameSite=lax, **30-day** TTL (`REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS`).
- **`POST /api/auth/refresh`** now uses `optional_current_user`: happy path (valid access token) behaves exactly as before; if the access token is **gone/expired**, it falls back to `renew_access_from_refresh()` to mint a fresh `ga_session` from the refresh cookie → session resumes with no re-login.
- **Non-rotating but revocable**: avoids refresh-rotation concurrency races (bursty parallel refreshes). Revoked on **logout** (`revoke_refresh_cookie`) and invalidated by the existing per-user **`tokens_revoked_before`** cutoff (password change / sign-out-everywhere). Rotation + reuse/theft detection noted as future hardening.
- **Logout** is now idempotent: revokes access jti + refresh token, clears both cookies, tolerates an already-expired access token.
- **Frontend `App.js`**: `bootAuthMe` tries `/auth/refresh` once on a 401 before logging out (idle-resume); proactive 15-min refresh + tab-refocus refresh from iter 266 retained.

**Files:** `backend/utils/refresh_tokens.py` (new), `backend/utils/auth.py` (`optional_current_user`), `backend/routes/auth.py` (login/register issue, refresh recovery, logout), `frontend/src/App.js`.

**Verified:** curl flow (login sets both cookies → drop access → `/auth/me` 401 → `/auth/refresh` recovers → `/auth/me` 200 → logout → replay refresh = 401). pytest `tests/test_iter267_refresh_token.py` 4/4 + iter227 8/8 (in Makefile regression). Testing agent frontend regression **5/5** (login/dashboards/logout/navigation, both cookies, no session-expired banner). Confirmed the 2 incidental auth-suite failures are **pre-existing on clean HEAD** (60s grace test + bulk-import org-state), not from this change.

**ACTION:** production-only — fix is in **preview**; user must **redeploy** gymaxisai.com.
**Minor backlog:** logout click could hard-redirect to /login immediately (cosmetic; session is already revoked server-side). Refresh-token rotation + reuse/theft detection (future security hardening). Per-device "revoke session" panel could also revoke that device's refresh token.

## Iter 266 — Fix recurring "Your session has expired" for Master Admins ✅ (Jun 13, 2026)

**Reported (production):** logging in as Master Admin, the dashboard shows a "Your session has expired" banner ~1h into a session. Recurring; prior cookie-focused fixes (iters 227/231/232) didn't resolve it.

**Root cause (reproduced + code-confirmed):** master/Pulse admins are issued a **1-HOUR** access token (`auth_guards.access_token_ttl_hours` → 1h; everyone else 24h) for security, and the HttpOnly `ga_session` cookie max-age matches. But the frontend **proactive token refresh ran on a 12-HOUR `setInterval`** (`App.js`) — it fired once on load, then not again for 12h. So an admin's 1h token expired with no proactive renewal; the next API call 401'd, the reactive refresh had no valid cookie → 401 → session-expired banner. 24h users were unaffected (12h interval refreshes them twice per token life), which is why it only hit admins and recurred ~hourly.

**Fix (`frontend/src/App.js`, no backend change):** refresh **every 15 minutes** (comfortably inside the 1h floor, with the backend's existing 60s rotation grace) + refresh **on tab refocus** (`visibilitychange`, throttled to once/min) to cover background-timer throttling / laptop sleep. The existing single-flight `__refreshInflight` guard prevents concurrent-refresh storms. Token still rotates hourly (security posture preserved).

**Verified:** login → 4 consecutive `/auth/refresh` rotations each followed by `/auth/me` = all 200 (chain stable, no self-revocation). `withCredentials=true` global so the cookie is sent. Frontend compiles clean. The long-idle-overnight banner remains by design (SessionResumedBanner).

**ACTION:** production-only fix made in **preview** — user must **redeploy** to push to gymaxisai.com.
