## Iter 227 — P3 security backlog: SEC-006 (libmagic) + localStorage→HttpOnly cookie (main session) ✅ (Jun 10, 2026)

**SEC-006 — strict upload validation.** Installed `libmagic1` so `python-magic` resolves; `utils.file_validation.selftest()` reports `enabled:true` and the startup health check surfaces it. A pure-Python signature-sniff fallback keeps uploads safe even where libmagic is absent (e.g. a prod image without the apt pkg). Tests: `tests/test_iter227_file_validation.py` (5/5). **Prod note:** the deploy image should include `libmagic1` for full detection; fallback covers it otherwise.

**localStorage JWT → HttpOnly cookie (Option B, scoped to the MAIN session).** The backend already set the HttpOnly `ga_session` cookie + `axios.defaults.withCredentials=true`; the remaining XSS gap was the JWT duplicated in `localStorage` and sent as a Bearer header across ~300 call-sites. Implemented with a **non-credential sentinel** approach (least-invasive, no rewrite of the 300 sites):
- **Backend** (`utils/auth.py`): `_extract_token` + `try_get_current_user` now ignore a literal `Bearer null` / `undefined` / `cookie` header and fall through to the `ga_session` cookie (a REAL header token still wins → impersonation/CRM/member unaffected). `routes/auth.py` `/auth/refresh` rotates the cookie **only** for cookie/sentinel sessions (NOT for a real header token — protects impersonation from cookie overwrite).
- **Frontend** (`App.js` + 3 edge login pages): the real JWT is never written to `localStorage`/React state for the main session; instead `localStorage['token']` holds the sentinel `'cookie'` (truthy → satisfies all `if (!token)` guards; produces a `Bearer cookie` header the backend ignores). `login()`, bootstrap, the 401-refresh interceptor, cross-tab sync, and `logout()` (now POSTs `/auth/logout` to clear the cookie) all updated. Impersonation keeps its real header token (deliberate override).
- **Tested:** `tests/test_iter227_cookie_session.py` (login sets cookie, cookie-only auth, sentinel fall-through, main-refresh rotates cookie, impersonation-refresh does NOT, logout clears). Backend pytest **12/12**. Testing agent verified frontend end-to-end (login→dashboard, no JWT in localStorage, HttpOnly cookie, reload persistence, module nav, logout, owner regression, Pulse engineer picker) — **no issues**.
- **Residual:** login email input is `type=text` (minor a11y/UX, optional). Full removal of the sentinel/header contract across all surfaces remains a future cleanup if ever desired.

## Iter 220 P1 (slice 4) — Master Price List secure backup + manual exports ✅ (Jun 4, 2026)

**User choices:** link expiry 7d; retention 90d; email = secure LINK (not raw file); owners/admins configure backup + include cost/margin (managers get cost/margin-free manual exports).

**Shipped (`routes/crm_price_backup.py`, prefix `/crm/price-list`):**
- **Manual export** `POST /export` {format csv|xlsx, scope live|archived|all|category, include_cost, include_margin} → CSV (UTF-8 BOM) or XLSX; **cost/margin columns gated** (forced off for non-approvers); stored base64 + secure token + 7d expiry.
- **Token-gated download** `GET /export/download/{id}?token=` — UNAUTHENTICATED by design (32-byte secret + expiry, 410 when expired, 404 on wrong token); no public listing. `GET /export/{id}/link` (auth) returns a fresh link; `GET /exports` lists history meta (no content/token).
- **Weekly backup** `GET/PUT /backup/config` (approver PUT) {enabled, day_of_week, time, recipients[], file_format, include_cost, include_margin, retention_days} → computes next_run (next matching weekday/time). `POST /backup/run` (approver) generates backup + emails recipients a secure link (Resend, best-effort try/except so it never blocks the backup).
- **Scheduler** `run_weekly_backup_loop` (server.py, hourly, `PRICE_BACKUP_SWEEP_MIN`) runs due backups + `purge_expired_exports` (retention cleanup).
- **Frontend** `CRMPriceExportModal.js` (Export/Backup button in CRMProductsSection): manual export + download link, weekly backup config + run-now, export history with per-row download + 🔒 on sensitive exports.

**Tested:** pytest 55/55 (added `test_iter_220p1_price_backup.py` 5; also fixed a brittle ambient-data fixture in the agent-authored `test_iter_220p1_quote_sage_api.py` → self-seeds products). testing_agent `iteration_220p1_slice4.json`: backend 100% (10 E2E + 5 unit), frontend 100% (all 17 testids, generate→link, save→next-run, run-now→history). Added env-overridable per-category Reply-To so customer replies land in the right inbox:
- billing → `billing@gymaxisai.com`, support → `support@gymaxisai.com`, service → `service@gymaxisai.com` (env: `REPLY_TO_BILLING|SUPPORT|SERVICE`).

**Goal:** Platform now has 4 verified Resend domains (`gymaxisai.com`, `billing.`, `support.`, `service.`). Route each outbound email from the domain matching its purpose.

**Core (`utils/email.py`):**

## Iter 220x — Membership member payments route to the gym's connected Stripe account (Connect destination charges) ✅ (Jun, 2026)

**Goal (user picked option a):** Member invoice + subscription + pay-all payments should land in the gym's OWN connected Stripe account (minus a platform fee), gated on `charges_enabled`, with graceful fallback to the platform account when the gym isn't connected.

**Implementation (destination charges — platform stays merchant of record so existing webhooks keep working):**
- New `utils/stripe_connect_routing.py`:
  - `resolve_org_connect_routing(org)` → `{destination, fee_pct}` only when the org's Express account is retrievable AND `charges_enabled` AND `capabilities.transfers == "active"`; else `None` (→ platform). Caches `stripe_charges_enabled` on the org.
  - `payment_intent_connect_kwargs(routing, amount_cents)` → `{transfer_data.destination, application_fee_amount}` (fee capped < amount) for mode=payment.
  - `subscription_connect_kwargs(routing)` → `{transfer_data.destination, application_fee_percent}` for mode=subscription.
  - Fee: `MEMBERSHIP_PLATFORM_FEE_PCT` env, default **1.0%**.
- Wired into: `memberships_payments.py::create_checkout` (subscription + one-time, fee computed on post-promo net), `memberships/studio_billing.py::_build_invoice_checkout_url` (resolves org by `invoice.organization_id` — projection-safe) and the member `pay-all` bundle.

**Validation:**
- 5 unit tests (`tests/test_iter_220x_membership_connect_routing.py`) — kwargs shape, fee cap, zero-fee omit, subscription percent. All pass.
- Live Stripe accepted the destination-charge param shape (`stripe.checkout.Session.create` with `payment_intent_data.transfer_data.destination` + `application_fee_amount`) — only rejected with `insufficient_capabilities_for_transfer` because no test gym has finished KYC yet, which is exactly the gated condition.
- Gating verified live: connected gym with `charges_enabled=false` → routing returns `None` → platform fallback. `_build_invoice_checkout_url` still returns a valid `cs_live` session on fallback (no regression).

**Status:** Money will flow to the gym's account automatically once each gym completes Stripe KYC (transfers capability active). Until then, payments collect into the platform account as before. Engineer invoices already use Direct Charges (unchanged).

## Iter 220u — Member app fixes: Check-in QR not generating + sign-up form layout ✅ (Jun, 2026)

Two member-app (`/m/{slug}`) bugs reported with screenshots (preview).

1. **Check-in pass QR never rendered ("Failed to generate pass", spinner + only the numeric code).** Root cause: `tabs/PassTab.js` passed **CSS variables** to `QRCode.toDataURL` colours (`dark: 'var(--color-surface-darker)'`, `light: 'var(--color-white)'`) — the `qrcode` lib needs real hex, so it threw. Fixed to `dark: '#0A0C10', light: '#FFFFFF'`. Verified live: scannable QR renders with the rotating code + countdown (`/member/qr` endpoint was always fine — confirmed via curl, payload `GXM|…|code`).

2. **Sign-up form layout — emergency-contact fields mismatched.** `portalShared.js` `LabelledInput` (a) rendered a stray `' *'` when `label={null}` + `required` (the floating asterisk on the empty phone field) and (b) ignored the `placeholder` prop entirely, so all placeholder hints were invisible and empty labels collapsed → fields misaligned. Fixes: only show `*` when there's a label; wire the `placeholder` prop to the input. Gave the Emergency-contact fields proper **Name** / **Phone** labels (MemberPortal.js). Verified live: aligned labelled fields, placeholders visible across the form.

Lint clean. Files: `tabs/PassTab.js`, `portalShared.js`, `MemberPortal.js`.

## Iter 220k — FIX: signup "stuck on Companies House" + Escape killed the whole signup ✅ (Jun, 2026)

**Bug (user testing signup):** on step-2 "Tell us about your gym", the Companies House typeahead box couldn't be dismissed, and pressing Escape (to close the dropdown) closed the ENTIRE signup.

**Root cause:** `TrialSignupModal.js` registers a global `window` keydown listener that closes the modal on Escape. The CH typeahead (`ProfileCompletionFields.js` -> `CompaniesHouseSearch`) had no Escape handler and no click-outside-to-close, so the keystroke bubbled to the modal's listener and nuked the flow.

**Fix (`components/shared/ProfileCompletionFields.js`):** added (1) `wrapRef` + a mousedown click-outside `useEffect` (gated on `open`) so clicking away dismisses the dropdown; (2) an input `onKeyDown` that, when the dropdown is open, calls `preventDefault + stopPropagation + nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation` and only `setOpen(false)` — so Escape closes just the dropdown and never reaches the modal's global listener. When the dropdown is closed, Escape still closes the modal as normal.

**Verified:** frontend testing agent 100% (3/3) on `/complete-profile` (same component; signup step-1 is captcha-gated) with the CH search mocked (preview CH API key is rejected) — Escape closes dropdown only + URL unchanged; click-outside dismisses; re-type re-opens; no console errors. Lint clean.

## Iter 220ea·48 — iOS Safari "logged out on resume" bug FIXED ✅ (Feb, 2026)

**Bug (PRODUCTION, Daniel — iOS Safari browser tab, not installed, logs out within seconds of switching apps).**

**Root cause:** `App.js` `if (loading)` gate only shows the auth "Loading…" splash for a hardcoded allowlist of protected routes — **`/partner-engineer` was missing**. iOS Safari reloads backgrounded tabs on resume; the app re-boots with `user=null` while `/auth/me` is in flight, and because `/partner-engineer` wasn't gated, its route guard (`user ? <PartnerDashboard/> : <Navigate to="/login"/>`) rendered immediately and bounced the returning user to `/login` = "logged out".

**Fix (`App.js`, render-timing only — no auth/token logic touched):** (1) added `/partner-engineer` + `/partners` to `protectedPrefixes`; (2) more robustly, while `loading`, now also show the splash whenever a **session token exists in localStorage** (`hasSessionToken`) — so route guards never render for ANY route until `/auth/me` resolves. Genuinely-invalid tokens are still cleared by boot → routed to `/login` (no lock-out); public marketing routes (no token) still render instantly.

**Verified:** frontend testing agent 5/5 — 3× reload on `/partner-engineer` stays put; `/dashboard` + `/svc/engineer` reload persist; no-token still redirects to `/login`; public root renders logged-out. **Production:** ships on redeploy.

After grace, the DBS/RTW gate re-applies. `grace` added to `/api/partners/me/compliance-docs`. ## Iter 220ea·39 — Faults auto-dispatch to the machine's supplier on submit ✅ (Feb, 2026)

**Request (option C):** when an operator submits a fault, automatically create the supplier "card to log the job" and **email it to the supplier** — resolving the supplier set against *that machine* first, with fallbacks.

**Problem:** on fault submit the old `_auto_dispatch_to_primary_supplier` only fired for engineer-escalated faults **and** only dispatched to an org-level `auto_dispatch=True` supplier (only ever auto-created for partner-referral signups). It **ignored the supplier set against the machine** and **didn't send an email** (just created a portal case). So gyms that set suppliers on machines saw nothing sent, and the manual 2-way comms prompted for an email (because that supplier had none resolved / on file).

**Fix (`routes/issues.py`):**
- New `_resolve_fault_supplier(issue, org)` — machine-first resolution: (1) supplier on the faulted **equipment** (`supplier_id` → `supplier` name, resolved against `db.suppliers`), (2) supplier named on the fault, (3) org primary `auto_dispatch` supplier. Only returns suppliers **with an email**.
- Rewrote `_auto_dispatch_to_primary_supplier` to fire for any **open** (non-self-fix) fault: creates the supplier case via `_ensure_supplier_case`, posts a first message, and **emails the supplier** (`_send_comment_notification`, in its own try/except so a mail failure never undoes the dispatch). Tags the issue `auto_dispatched_supplier_*` + `supplier_case_token`. Idempotent (one supplier case per `issue_id`).
- Wired into both the single (`POST /issues`) and multi-machine batch (`POST /issues/batch`) submit paths (each machine → its own supplier).

**Bonus:** because the supplier case now exists with the resolved email on submit, the fault card's 2-way comms (`issue.supplier_case.supplier_email`) is pre-populated → **no more "set an email" prompt** (when the supplier has an email on file).

**Operational note:** dispatch only happens when the resolved supplier has an **email**. Suppliers without an email on file → nothing sent (no spurious emails). Operators should ensure machine suppliers have emails.

**Verified:** live e2e (Jack Ottey / Third Space) — logged a fault on a machine with a supplier set (no supplier in payload) → machine's supplier resolved, supplier case + token created, issue tagged, email triggered. New pytests `tests/test_iter_220ea_39_fault_supplier_dispatch.py` (3: machine-supplier dispatch, self-fix does NOT dispatch, helper/wiring guards) green, in Makefile. Lint clean.

**Files:** routes/issues.py, tests/test_iter_220ea_39_fault_supplier_dispatch.py (new, in Makefile). **Production:** ships on redeploy.

Daniel on production):** Master Admin → Partners → the engineer's row → **"Start trial"** (Rocket) button (`POST /api/partners/{id}/start-trial`); shows whenever `status=approved && !trial_used`. This writes the proper timer and unsticks the dashboard. ## Iter 220ea·35 — P2: offline engineer quoting + flaky-test fix ✅ (Feb, 2026)

Smart: existing account → password-reset email; not yet activated → re-issues the activation welcome email via the application.
- `AdminPartners.js` — "Send link" button (`admin-partner-signin-link-{id}`) on every approved engineer row.

## Iter 220ea·31 — Watertight engineer 10-day trial → feedback → Stripe process ✅ (Feb, 2026)

User needs a watertight trial pipeline before the "WE NEED YOU!" adverts drive an intake. Confirmed choices: admin button to start a 10-day FREE trial (Partners list + one-click "Approve & start trial" on a pending application); on day-10 access continues during a **3-day grace** then auto-suspends if no decision; feedback form emailed (rating / worked well / missing / continue Yes-No); ACCEPT → Stripe £30/mo, DECLINE or no-response → suspended (access revoked, feedback kept); reminders day-9 + day-10 + a +2-day last-chance nudge. **One trial per engineer, ever.** Backend 6/6 pytest + full lifecycle curl-verified (start → time-travel → feedback → accept gives a real Stripe checkout URL → decline/no-response suspend); frontend tested (admin buttons + on-brand public feedback page); test data cleaned (counter 10/10).

**State machine** (on `partner_engineers.trial`): `active → feedback_pending → (accepted → converted_paid) | declined | expired`. `trial_used:true` blocks repeat trials. Suspension sets `partner.status=suspended` and returns in-flight jobs to dispatch (`_handle_partner_loss_of_access`).

**Backend (`routes/partners.py`):**
- `_start_partner_trial(partner, by, *, force)` — sets the trial object + `trial_used` + trialing subscription, emails "trial started". One-trial guard (400 on repeat).
- `POST /api/partners/{id}/start-trial` (master admin) — Partners-list button.
- `POST /api/partners/applications/{id}/approve-with-trial` (master admin) — promotes + starts trial in one click. `approve_partner_application` also auto-starts the full lifecycle for campaign `tester_cohort` applicants.
- `GET/POST /api/partners/trial/feedback/{token}` (PUBLIC, tokenised) — render + submit. accept → `_create_partner_checkout_session` returns a Stripe URL (free-tier handled); decline → suspend.
- `_create_partner_checkout_session` factored out and shared with the authed `/partners/me/subscription/checkout`.
- `handle_partner_checkout_completed` → flips trial to `converted_paid` and lifts a trial-expiry suspension on payment.

**Worker `utils/partner_trial_lifecycle.py`** (registered in server.py, 6h, idempotent per-step timestamps): day-9 "ends tomorrow" → day-10 feedback form (token + `grace_until=+3d`) → +2-day last-chance nudge → grace passed & unpaid ⇒ expired + suspended. Emails in `utils/partner_emails.py` (send_trial_started / _ending_tomorrow / _feedback_request / _lastchance).

**Frontend:** `AdminPartners.js` — "Start trial" button (`admin-partner-start-trial-{id}`) + `TrialBadge` (active/feedback-due/accepted/paid/declined/expired with countdown). `PartnerApplicationDrawer.js` — footer now has "Approve" + "Approve & start trial". New public on-brand page `pages/PartnerEngineer/TrialFeedback.js` at `/partner-engineer/trial-feedback/:token` (5-star + 2 textareas + continue/decline → Stripe redirect).

**Files:** routes/partners.py, utils/partner_trial_lifecycle.py (new), utils/partner_emails.py, server.py, AdminPartners.js, PartnerApplicationDrawer.js, PartnerEngineer/TrialFeedback.js (new), routes/AppRoutes.js, tests/test_iter_220ea_31_engineer_trial.py (new, in Makefile).

**Notes:** Stripe is real test-mode; emails via Resend (real). `routes/partners.py` is ~5,100 lines — flagged for a future split (applications / trial / subscription / public). Production: works after redeploy.

## Iter 220ea·26c — PPM recurrence rollover (G2 follow-up) ✅ (Feb, 2026)

Made the preventive-maintenance cadence self-driving: once a PPM visit completes, the next is auto-created `interval_days` later, until the contract end. Lint clean, 12/12 iter-26 pytests green, verified live (function + endpoint).

- **Worker** `utils/ppm_rollover.py::roll_ppm_schedules_once(organization_id=None)` + `run_forever(hours)`: scans active `svc_ppm_schedules` — latest visit still open → skip; latest closed/invoiced/cancelled → create the next visit at `due + interval_days` (via canonical `intake._create_case`, scheduled, linked via `ppm_schedule_id`) and bump `visits_generated`/`next_due_date`; next due past `end_date` → retire the schedule (`active=False`). Self-healing (periodic sweep, not just an event hook) + idempotent (one open visit per schedule, dedupe by due date).
- **Registration:** background loop started in `server.py` startup (`PPM_ROLLOVER_HOURS`, default 6h). Confirmed in logs: "[ppm-rollover] loop started (6h)".
- **Manual trigger:** `POST /api/svc/admin/ppm/roll` (manager-only) in `customer_links.py` — ops can materialise upcoming visits on demand; also used for testing.
- **Verified:** complete→roll creates next visit at due+30 (12 visits/yr); idempotent re-roll; end-date retirement. Endpoint-based regression test (runs the roll in the server's healthy loop to avoid the shared-test-loop `_create_case` orphan-task issue).
- **Files:** utils/ppm_rollover.py (new), server.py, routes/svc/customer_links.py, tests/test_iter_220ea_26_crm_service_bridge.py.

## Iter 220ea·15 — Blog generation resilience (no broken/AI placeholders go live) ✅ (Feb, 2026)

**Field-reported bug:** the daily SEO autopilot published a blog whose
body was the LLM-unreachable placeholder *"Article generation is
temporarily unavailable. Please regenerate once the AI service is back
online."* (screenshot from gymaxisai.com). The LLM had a transient blip;
the code fell to the placeholder on the first failure and auto-published
it live. Two user requirements: (1) make generation work reliably, and
(2) any failure copy must NEVER mention AI.

### Fixes — `routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py`
1. **`_llm_text` retries** up to 3× with exponential backoff (2/4/8s)
   and treats an empty response as a failure — recovers from transient
   blips instead of giving up on the first error.
2. **Neutral placeholder + `generation_failed` flag.**
   `_generate_article_payload` now returns `generation_failed` and the
   placeholder body reads *"This article is being prepared and will be
   published here shortly. Please check back soon."* — no AI mention.
3. **Never auto-publish a failed article.** `generate_article` holds a
   failed generation in `needs_review` (never `published`) when
   `publish_now=True`. `generation_failed` is persisted on the doc for
   observability. Manual `publish_now=False` drafts behave as before.
4. **Autopilot retries the topic.** `run_autopilot` keeps the keyword
   `queued` (doesn't retire it to `published`) when generation fails, so
   the next daily run retries rather than burning the topic.

### Cleanup
- Regenerated the one broken live article in the DB
  (`gym-treadmill-downtime-impact-on-retention`) — now real 1,235-word
  content, verified via the public `/api/blog/posts/{slug}` endpoint.

### Tests
`tests/test_iter_220ad_seo_autopilot.py` (+3): failed generation not
published live, placeholder never mentions AI, autopilot keeps keyword
queued on failure. 21/21 in-file + 67 nearby SEO tests pass. Lint clean.

### NOTE — production article in the screenshot
The screenshot is from production (gymaxisai.com), whose DB is separate
from preview. This code fix prevents recurrence after deploy; the
existing broken production post should be regenerated post-deploy
(Master Admin → Marketing → SEO → regenerate, or next autopilot run).



## Iter 220ea·14 — Starter Field Templates ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Cuts the cold-start "what fields should I even ask the engineer
to capture?" problem for new operators. Six platform-shipped
templates, one-tap apply, idempotent.

### Catalogue (6 starter templates)

| Template ID | Scope | Job types | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `treadmill_ppm` | `equipment_type=Treadmill` | `ppm` | 6 (Belt tension, wear, motor brush, deck wax, firmware, incline cal) |
| `treadmill_repair` | `equipment_type=Treadmill` | `repair` | 5 (Fault code, motor amps, belt slip, drive belt, harness) |
| `cycle_ppm` | `equipment_type=Indoor Cycle` | `ppm` | 5 (Crank play, brake pads, BB grease, saddle, batteries) |
| `rower_ppm` | `equipment_type=Rower` | `ppm` | 5 (Drag factor, chain lube, shock cord, rollers, firmware) |
| `strength_ppm` | `equipment_type=Strength` | `ppm` | 5 (Cable, pulleys, weight pin, upholstery, guide rods) |
| `installation_handover` | `global` | `install` | 5 (SN photo, customer name, warranty, floor, cleaning) |

### Backend (`routes/svc/work_report_fields.py`)

* **`FIELD_TEMPLATES`** — in-code catalogue (editorial content,
  ships with platform). Each template is `(id, name, summary,
  scope_kind, scope_value, job_types, fields[])`.
* **`GET /api/svc/work-report-fields/templates`** — read-only
  catalogue endpoint; returns template metadata + full field
  preview so the modal can render the `<details>` preview.
* **`POST /api/svc/work-report-fields/apply-template`** —
  seeds the fields. Accepts optional `scope_kind` /
  `scope_value` / `job_types` overrides so operators with their
  own taxonomy can re-map at apply time. Idempotent: skips any
  field whose `(name, scope_kind, scope_value)` already exists
  (non-archived) on the org. Returns `created_count` +
  `skipped_count` so the toast can report both. Stamps each
  seeded field with `created_via_template` for observability.

### Frontend (`EngineerWorkReportFields.js`)

* New **Templates** button in the page header
  (`wrf-templates-btn`), and an **Or pick a starter template**
  CTA on the empty state (`wrf-empty-templates-btn`).
* New **`FieldTemplatesModal`** — bottom-sheet on mobile, modal
  on desktop. Each template card shows name, field count
  badge, scope chip (e.g. "TREADMILL"), job-type chip(s) (e.g.
  "PPM"), summary, and a collapsible `<details>` preview that
  lists every field with its type + required marker. Apply
  button per card, with `Loader2` → `Check` transition.
* On apply: re-loads the parent field list so the seeded rows
  appear inline immediately. Confirms via `notify.success`
  with skipped-count breakdown when re-applying.

### Tests

`backend/tests/test_iter_220ea_14_field_templates.py` (7 tests):
* Source-level catalogue sanity
* Live `GET /templates` returns ≥6
* Live two-step E2E: apply seeds fields → re-apply skips them
* 404 on unknown `template_id`
* Invalid `job_types` are filtered (not 400)
* Frontend modal + endpoints wired correctly

93/93 nearby tests pass. Lint clean.


## Iter 220ea·13 — Custom Fields react to Case Type ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

**User confirmation request** — "Custom Fields must also react to
Case Types — a repair will need different custom fields than a
Preventative Maintenance Service." This iter confirms (and locks
in with regression tests) that the existing wiring already does
this end-to-end.

### Existing wiring (Iter 220du, already shipped)

* Admin editor (`EngineerWorkReportFields.js`) exposes the
  multi-select **Only on these job types (leave empty for all)**
  with chips: Repair · PPM Service · Installation · Inspection ·
  Emergency callout · Asset audit (`id`s `repair`, `ppm`,
  `install`, `inspection`, `callout`, `audit`).
* Backend `WorkReportFieldIn` / `WorkReportFieldPatch` accept
  `job_types: list[str]`.
* `GET /svc/work-report-fields/for-case/{case_id}` and
  `GET /svc/work-report-fields/for-machine-row/{row_id}`
  filter the result set against the case's `case_type` — an
  empty/missing `job_types` list still returns the field
  (backward-compat) but a non-empty list must include the
  current case's `case_type` for the field to surface.
* `case_type` defaults to `"repair"` for legacy cases without a
  stamped type so behaviour stays sensible.

### Verified end-to-end (Feb 14, 2026)

```
case_type=repair → field with job_types=["repair"]      ✓ shown
case_type=ppm     → field with job_types=["repair"]      ✗ hidden
```

### Tests
`backend/tests/test_iter_220ea_13_custom_fields_react_to_case_type.py`
(5 source-level guards) added to `Makefile` regression target.
Lock-in tests for: admin UI chips, both Pydantic models, allowed
job types, and both `for-case` + `for-machine-row` resolvers
applying the filter correctly.

## Iter 220ea·9 — Inline H&S checklist on Summary ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

**Bug found from live user QA:** tapping the Pre-job H&S banner
on the Summary tab jumped to the Complete tab — but the H&S
checklist UI had never been ported from the legacy
`EngineerJobDetail.js` (Iter 216h89) into `EngineerJobDetailV2.js`.
Engineers were landing on a dead-end with no way to actually tick
off the checklist or sign off, despite the amber banner saying
"Tap to complete 8 items".

### Fix — `SafetyChecklistInline`
Built a new `SafetyChecklistInline` component that renders
**inline on Summary** when the engineer taps the amber banner:

- Banner is now an `aria-expanded` toggle (`setSafetyOpen(v => !v)`)
  — no tab navigation; the chevron rotates `90°` when open.
- Inline card renders each template item with a tickbox and `*`
  for required items; outstanding-required counter in the header
  ("0/8 ticked · 5 REQUIRED OUTSTANDING").
- Remarks textarea (max 2000 chars, optional).
- "Add signature" opens the existing fullscreen `SignatureCanvas`
  modal; signature is staged into local state and confirmed
  before submit.
- "Sign off & continue" POSTs `/svc/engineer/jobs/{caseId}/safety/signoff`
  with `ticked_item_ids` + `signature_image` + `remarks`. On
  success the parent reloads, the banner collapses (because
  `safetyNeeded` flips false), and the stats-grid H&S tile turns
  green ("Cleared").
- Graceful empty-template state when no checklist is configured.
- `onJumpToSafety` prop deleted from `JobAtAGlance`. Stale
  "Open the Complete tab" copy in the arrival-error toast updated
  to point at the Summary banner.

### Tests
`backend/tests/test_iter_220ea_9_inline_safety_checklist.py`
(9 source-level guards). Old `test_iter_220ea_5` test
`test_safety_banner_is_clickable_to_complete_tab` updated to
assert the new inline-toggle behaviour. Added to `Makefile`
regression target (tab-indented). 71/71 nearby tests + 8/8

## Iter 220ea·5 — Engineer App UX fixes ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Three engineer-app pain points from a live user report, plus a
visual cleanup of the bottom-right FAB stack.

### 1 · Pre-job H&S checklist banner on Summary

Previously the engineer only saw "checklist required" when they
tried to start the on-site timer (on the Time tab). Now the
amber banner is the FIRST thing on the Summary tab when the job
requires a signoff:

- New `summary-safety-checklist-banner` test-id, prominent amber
  warning-icon avatar, count of outstanding items.
- Whole banner is a `<button>` — tapping it jumps activeTab to
  `complete` where the checklist UI lives.
- Detection is "no `safety_signoff` yet AND a `safety_template`
  exists" so it only nags on jobs that actually need it.

### 2 · Equipment-new round-trip stays on Equipment tab

After adding a new asset from the Equipment tab, the engineer
was being bounced to Summary. Two-part fix:

- `EngineerEquipment.handleSave` (the new-asset flow) now
  navigates back with `?tab=equipment` instead of the bare
  `/svc/engineer/jobs/{id}`.
- `EngineerJobDetailV2` now reads `?tab=` from
  `useSearchParams` on mount, validates against the known
  `TABS` ids, and lands on the requested tab (falling back to
  `summary` for unknown / missing query).

### 3 · One SpeedDial replaces three FABs

The bottom-right corner had three independently-positioned
launchers (voice mic, AskGymAxis sparkle, FeedbackWidget). On a
mobile screen they were stacked tightly and visually crowded.
Now there's a single FAB that expands into a labelled vertical
arc on tap.

- **New `EngineerSpeedDial.js`** — single launcher
  (`engineer-speed-dial-launcher`), expandable arc with three
  labelled options (`engineer-speed-dial-voice/ask/feedback`).
- Closes on outside-tap, Escape, or after selecting an action.
- Each action dispatches a `gx:open-{voice|ask|feedback}` window
  event. The three existing modal components were modified to
  (a) listen for the corresponding event and open programmatically,
  and (b) suppress their own launcher render when
  `/^\/svc\/engineer/.test(location.pathname)` — so the engineer
  sees exactly one launcher (the SpeedDial), not four.
- Mounted in `AppRoutes.js` alongside the existing
  `EngineerVoiceToJobButton` (whose modal logic is now driven by
  the SpeedDial event).

## Iter 220ea·4 — Resume-failed-upload UX ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the loop on iter 220e9: when a chunked upload fails halfway
(tab killed, signal dropped, phone died), the engineer can now
come back, see a "N uploads paused" pill on the home screen, tap
to resume from exactly the chunk that failed — without
re-selecting the file.

### `chunkedUpload.js` (extended)

- New `resumeUploadId` param — when present, pre-fetches
  `/files/upload/chunks/{id}/status`, marks any already-received
  chunks as done, and only PUTs the missing ones before calling
  `complete`.
- New `onSession({uploadId, totalChunks})` hook fires immediately
  after init returns, so the caller can persist the session
  blob BEFORE the first chunk PUT lands.
- Resume failures no longer auto-abort (the session must stay
  live for the next attempt). Non-resume failures keep the
  existing best-effort `DELETE` cleanup.
- Errors are stamped with `err.uploadId` + `err.code =
  'session_expired'` (when the server has TTL-collected the
  session) so the UI can drop dead stash rows cleanly.

### New `utils/engineerUploadStash.js`

- Vanilla IndexedDB store `paused_uploads`, keyed by `upload_id`,
  scoped to the current engineer via a first-12-chars token
  namespace (so shared tablets don't leak between engineers).
- Persists the actual `Blob` so resume works after tab close —
  the browser can't re-read a File handle after the original
  session is gone.
- Public surface: `stashPausedUpload`, `dropPausedUpload`,
  `listPausedUploads`, `getPausedUpload`, `countPausedUploads`,
  `subscribePausedUploads` (pub/sub for the pill to refresh on
  state changes without polling).

### New `PausedUploadsPill.js`

- Amber pill in the engineer home header — only renders when
  there's at least one paused row.
- Tap opens a bottom-sheet listing each paused upload with
  filename, size, age, optional caption, and **Resume / Discard**
  CTAs.
- Resume: re-runs `chunkedUpload` with `resumeUploadId`, then
  POSTs to `/svc/engineer/photos` with the stashed `case_id` /
  `machine_row_id` / `caption` so the resumed bytes appear on
  the same row the original attempt targeted.
- Session-expired path: drops the stash row + notifies the
  engineer that the server forgot the session (TTL collected) so
  they need to re-attach the file from the job.
- Polls on window-focus + every 30s so a pause that happened in
  one tab surfaces in another.

### Real upload flow rewired

`WorkVisitMachinesCard.attachPhoto` — the path field engineers
actually use — was still on single-shot FormData (iter 220e9 had
only wired the dead `PhotosTab`). It now routes through
`chunkedUpload`, stashes the session blob via `onSession`, and
drops the stash row on success via a best-effort cleanup walk
(matching case + filename + size).

### Tests

- `test_iter_220ea_4_resume_upload_ux.py` — 13 wiring guards:
  resume id / onSession ordering, no-auto-abort, stash CRUD
  surface, owner-namespacing, Blob persistence, pill render-
  conditions, resume flow + finalisation POST, focus/interval
  poll, EngineerHomeV2 mount position, and the WorkVisitMachines
  flow rewrite.
- Existing 220e9 backend tests still pass (status endpoint, chunk
  idempotency, MIME guard, abort) — the new wiring rides the
  same backend.

### Verified

- 47 related tests pass.
- Full regression **2129 / 2129 passing**.
- `make lint-frontend` clean.
- Frontend compiles cleanly.

## Iter 220ea — Engineer App Playwright E2E smoke suite ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the deferred release-readiness gap from iter 220e6: real
browser coverage for the Engineer PWA flows. The pytest layer can
only check source-level wiring; this spec runs the actual app in a
mobile-viewport headless Chromium so blank screens, error
boundaries, and offline-indicator regressions are caught before
release.

### New Playwright spec (`tests/mobile-regression/engineer-smoke.spec.js`)

- **6 route smoke tests** at iPhone 13 Pro viewport — every
  Engineer route must either render its happy-path testid OR the
  partner-engineer access-gate (both are valid landings for
  master admin without partner-engineer role):
  - `/svc/engineer` → `engineer-home-v2`
  - `/svc/engineer/jobs` → `engineer-home`
  - `/svc/engineer/quotes` → `engineer-quotes`
  - `/svc/engineer/invoices` → `engineer-invoices`
  - `/svc/engineer/diary` → `engineer-diary`
  - `/svc/engineer/inbox` → `engineer-inbox`
- Each test asserts:
  - `engineer-error-boundary` fallback was NOT triggered.
  - No `console.error` outside a known-noise allow-list
    (React DevTools, posthog, CSP-blocked Emergent/Cloudflare
    third-party scripts, expected 4xx warmups, intentional
    offline-test ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED).
- **Offline pill wiring test**: navigates to `/svc/engineer/jobs`,
  flips `context.setOffline(true)` + dispatches the `offline`
  event, asserts the pill becomes visible, flips back online,
  asserts the pill clears.

### Resilient global setup rewrite (`global-setup.js`)

The previous UI-driven flow (open /login → fill → click submit →
waitForURL) was racy on the preview environment: the cookie banner
mounted after inputs hydrated and intercepted the submit click,
and lazy-loaded chunks for `/master-admin` regularly exceeded the
25 s `waitForURL` budget.

The rewrite:
- POSTs `/api/auth/login` directly via Playwright's request
  context (single round-trip, ~250 ms).
- Seeds the resulting JWT into `localStorage.token` via
  `addInitScript`, plus a `cookie_consent_v1` flag so the
  banner doesn't intercept clicks in downstream tests.
- Falls back to `/app/frontend/.env` for
  `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL` when the shell env doesn't carry it
  (previously baseURL silently defaulted to localhost:3000 and
  every API call 404'd).

`playwright.config.js` got the same `resolveBaseURL` helper so the
runner itself uses the correct backend even outside CI.

### Static guard (`backend/tests/test_iter_220ea_engineer_e2e_smoke.py`)

- 9 pytest assertions guarding the spec from drift: every route
  must remain listed, every critical testid must still be
  asserted, console-noise allow-list must include the platform
  scripts and offline-test signals, and the global setup must
  keep using the API path rather than the UI flow.

### Verified

- All 7 Playwright tests pass against the live preview environment
  (master-admin lands on the access-gate route in this env, which
  is treated as a valid landing).
- pytest regression **2115 / 2115 passing**. Lint clean on new
  files.

### How to run

```
cd /app/frontend && yarn test:mobile-regression -- tests/mobile-regression/engineer-smoke.spec.js
```

## Iter 220e9 — Chunked uploads for engineer media ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the last release-readiness gap from the iter 220e6 audit: a
field engineer on a flaky 4G connection no longer loses a 25 MB
video because the connection blipped at 90%. Large uploads are
sliced into 1 MB chunks with per-chunk retry; small files keep
riding the original single-shot path so the happy path stays fast.

### Backend (`routes/files_chunked.py`)

- `POST /api/files/upload/chunks/init` — body `{filename, size,
  content_type, category, total_chunks}`, returns `{upload_id,
  max_chunk_bytes, expires_at}`. Persists session in
  `file_upload_sessions`.
- `PUT /api/files/upload/chunks/{upload_id}/{index}` — raw
  `application/octet-stream` body, **idempotent** (retries
  overwrite). Caps at 4 MB/chunk, validates index in range, blocks
  empty bodies. User-scoped — another user with the same upload_id
  gets 404.
- `POST /api/files/upload/chunks/{upload_id}/complete` —
  assembles chunks in order, runs the SAME `validate_upload` byte
  sniff + category MIME allow-list as the legacy endpoint, stores
  via `put_object`, inserts a `files` row, deletes the chunk rows.
  Returns a file_doc interface-identical to `/files/upload` so the
  frontend treats both paths uniformly. Stamps
  `upload_method: "chunked"`.
- `DELETE /api/files/upload/chunks/{upload_id}` — best-effort
  abort + chunk cleanup.
- `GET /api/files/upload/chunks/{upload_id}/status` — reports
  `received/missing` chunk indices for resume-on-reopen flows.
- 60 min TTL via `expires_at` so abandoned uploads don't bloat
  Mongo.

### Frontend (`utils/chunkedUpload.js`)

- Pure helper, zero npm dependencies (matches the existing vanilla
  IndexedDB outbox posture).
- Auto-routes: ≤ 4 MB → legacy `/files/upload` (with axios
  `onUploadProgress`); > 4 MB → init → 2-in-flight parallel
  worker pool over 1 MB chunks with exponential backoff
  (300 / 600 / 1200 / 2400 ms + jitter, 4 retries) → complete.
- Aggregates progress across chunks via `onProgress(pct)` callback
  so the existing progress bar plugs in without modification.
- Best-effort `DELETE` abort on terminal failure so the server-side
  TTL doesn't have to wait.

### Wiring

- `EngineerJobDetailV2.js` `PhotosTab.uploadFile` now goes through
  `chunkedUpload(...)`. The category, error surfacing, and progress
  UI are unchanged — only the transport.

### Tests

- `tests/test_iter_220e9_chunked_uploads.py` — 20 scenarios
  covering init validation matrix, chunk store + idempotency +
  oversize + out-of-range + empty + user-scoping, assembly +
  size-mismatch + missing-chunk guards + post-assembly MIME sniff,
  abort cleanup, resume status, and route-registry smoke.
- Updated `test_iter_216h257_*` and `test_iter_220db_*` to match
  the new wiring (category now a parameter, not a querystring).
- Regression **2106 / 2106 passing**. Lint clean on all new
  files.

## Iter 220e5 — Workspace mode + Engineer ↔ CRM feedback loop ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the operator's "must work for both enterprise + one-man-band"
brief on top of the iter 220e3/e4 contracts overhaul. The brief
called for a single connected module that adapts to org size and a
two-way information flow between the CRM contract record and the
Engineer App — neither requirement involved new data domains, so
everything below builds on existing collections.

### What changed

**Backend** (`routes/crm_contract_workspace.py`):

- New `GET /api/crm/v2/contracts/workspace` returns the computed
  workspace mode (`solo` vs `enterprise`) based on user count, site
  count, and active approval rules. Ships a `capabilities` map so
  the frontend can drive feature visibility from a single source.
  - Solo (1 user, ≤2 sites, no active approval rules):
    `show_approval_queue=false`, `show_team_assignment=false`,
    `show_finance_review=false`, `default_engineer_to_self=true`,
    `primary_cta="Create Contract"`.
  - Enterprise: opposite, plus region filters once site count > 5.
- New `crm2_contract_feedback` collection — single canonical store
  for engineer-submitted contract feedback. Rows reference the
  existing `svc_cases` job + `crm2_contracts` row + engineer record.
  No data duplication.
- New `POST /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/contract-feedback`
  (under the existing engineer entitlement wall) — engineer posts
  observations (`asset_condition / exclusion_recommended /
  upgrade_recommended / renewal_review / repeated_fault /
  capex_replacement / upsell_opportunity / contract_dispute /
  chargeable_flag / pricing_review / general_note`). Drops a system
  activity on the contract feed so coordinators see it in context.
- New `GET /api/crm/v2/contracts/feedback-queue?status=` — Contract
  Review Queue. Filterable by status (open / actioned / rejected /
  reviewed / all).
- New `POST /api/crm/v2/contracts/feedback/{id}/action` —
  coordinators accept / reject / note / mark_reviewed. On `accept`
  for renewal-relevant kinds, drops a `contract_renewal` task
  activity so the renewal pipeline picks it up.
- New `GET /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/contract-entitlement` —
  mobile-friendly entitlement payload (plain-English `Covered` /
  `Chargeable` fields for callout, labour, major parts, wear & tear,
  treadmill belts/beds, upholstery + exclusion labels + emergency SLA).

**Frontend**:

- `pages/CRM/Contracts/ContractReviewQueue.js` — new coordinator
  surface listing engineer feedback with accept / reject / note
  actions and status / kind filters. Reachable from a new
  **Review Queue** tab in CRM → Contracts.
- `pages/CRM/CRMContracts.js` — new `useWorkspaceMode` hook drives a
  visible **Solo / Enterprise workspace** badge top-right and the
  Review Queue tab visibility. Workspace object is also passed into
  `ContractDetail` for downstream consumers.
- `pages/ServiceOps/Engineer/EngineerEntitlementPanel.js` —
  read-only panel mounted on the Engineer App job Summary,
  immediately below the cover banner. Renders the entitlement
  endpoint as plain-English coverage pills. Includes a "Send

## Iter 220e4 — Auto-renewal autopilot ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Operator continuation of the "potential improvement" suggested at
iter 220e3 finish:

> the renewals dashboard auto-fires an outbound email to the customer
> at the 30-day threshold (with the branded PDF + accept link), so a
> contract literally renews itself if both sides agree.

### What changed

- **New endpoint**: `POST /api/crm/v2/contracts/renewals/auto-send`.
  For every active contract that has `auto_renew=True`, is within 30
  days of expiry, has a contact email, and wasn't auto-dispatched in
  the last 60 days, the autopilot:
  1. Clones the contract into a renewal draft (`status=sent`,
     `auto_dispatched=true`, version + 1, `contract_number` suffixed
     with `/R{n}`) with the **suggested uplift applied** to
     `annual_value` + `pricing`.
  2. Copies the `crm2_contract_assets` rows so the new contract
     carries the same equipment out of the gate.
  3. Mints a public accept-token (`_ensure_accept_token`).
  4. Builds the branded PDF and emails it to the billing contact (or
     primary contact if no billing contact) via Resend with the
     accept link.
  5. Marks the **original** contract with `auto_renewal_sent_at` and
     `renewal_contract_id`, plus an audit activity on
     `crm2_activities`.
- **NEVER auto-signs / auto-activates** — the customer still has to
  click "Accept & sign" on the public page (which moves the renewal
  draft to `status=active`).
- Idempotent within a 60-day window per contract — running twice the
  same day is a no-op for already-dispatched contracts.
- Graceful degradation: if Resend isn't reachable, the renewal draft
  + accept-token are still created so the operator can copy/paste
  the accept link manually.

### Frontend

- New **"Auto-renewal autopilot"** emerald button on CRM → Contracts
  → Renewals tab, sitting alongside "Run reminders now". Confirms
  before firing and shows dispatched / skipped counts.

### Tests (5)

`test_iter_220e4_auto_renewal_autopilot.py`:
- Dispatches a renewal for an eligible contract; renewal status is
  `sent` (not `active`); uplift > 0; assets copied; original tagged.
- Skips contracts auto-dispatched in the last 60 days.
- Skips contracts without a contact email (and lists the reason).
- Ignores contracts without `auto_renew=True`.
- UI button wired through and hits the new endpoint.

Lint clean (ruff + ESLint). Endpoint smoke-tests `401` (auth-gated route registered).

## Iter 220e3 — CRM → Contracts: Premium overhaul (Phases A–G) ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Operator brief:

> Evolve the existing CRM → Contracts module into a premium,
> enterprise-grade service-contract management system for the
> fitness industry — without duplicating customers, sites, assets,
> contacts, engineers, contracts, quotes, invoices, jobs or CRM data
> already in the system.

### What changed (all phases shipped in a single iter)

#### Phase A — Foundation schema + Templates
- **New collection** `crm2_contract_templates` (admin-renameable Silver/Gold/Platinum/Custom). System defaults seed lazily on first list call so empty tenants always have a starting point. Slug is immutable; name is freely editable so tenants can rebrand to "Basic / Standard / Premium / Labour Only" etc.
- **New endpoint** `GET /api/crm/v2/contract-catalog` returns the canonical inclusion / exclusion / consumable / response-time catalog. Per-tenant `PUT /contract-catalog/labels` for label overrides (slugs never change).
- **Contract schema extension** — `crm_contracts._build_contract_doc` now carries `inclusions{}`, `exclusions_structured[]`, `consumables[]`, `response_times{}`, `pricing{}`, `terms_md`, `template_id`, `billing_contact_id`, `assigned_engineer_id`, `site_id`, `renewal_date`, `contract_length_months`. Additive — legacy contracts continue to work.
- **Apply-template endpoint** overlays cover fields onto a draft without clobbering customer / dates / assets.

#### Phase B — 10-step Create Contract Wizard (frontend)
- New `pages/CRM/Contracts/ContractWizard.js` replaces the 1-screen modal as the primary "New Contract" CTA. Steps: Customer & Site → Assets → Cover Type → Inclusions → Exclusions → Consumables → Response Times → Pricing (with computed margin %) → Terms (auto-generated from cover) → Review.
- Wizard consumes the existing `companies / contacts / sites-and-equipment` endpoints — **no duplicated data**. Quick-Create modal kept as a fallback path.
- "From Template" picker on step 3 pre-fills inclusions/exclusions/consumables/response-times.

#### Phase C — Comparison Matrix
- New `pages/CRM/Contracts/ContractMatrix.js` renders a grouped tick / cross / response-time matrix.
- Visible in the wizard's Review step **and** as a new **Compare** tab on Contract Detail (templates vs. this contract — perfect for upsell at renewal).

#### Phase D — Branded PDF + Send + E-sign
- New `utils/crm_contract_pdf.py` (reportlab) renders a branded contract PDF with header / parties / cover summary / inclusions / exclusions / consumables / response-times / pricing / T&Cs / signature box.
- **New endpoints** `GET /contracts/{id}/pdf` (auth'd download), `POST /contracts/{id}/send` (Resend + accept-token mint), `GET /public/contracts/{token}` (customer snapshot — strips cost / margin), `POST /public/contracts/{token}/sign` (idempotent accept).
- New **Public Accept page** at `/contracts/accept/:token` with signature canvas. Marks contract `active` + fires the existing `contract_activated` integration event on sign.
- **Download PDF** + **Send** buttons added to the Contract Detail header.

#### Phase E — Renewals pipeline + reminders
- New `GET /contracts/renewals/pipeline` buckets active contracts by 30/60/90-day windows with suggested uplift (heuristic baseline: 5% CPI + 3% if cost/annual > 70%, capped 12%).
- New `POST /contracts/renewals/run-reminders` — operator-triggered, **idempotent per (contract_id, threshold)**.
- New **Renewals** view in CRM → Contracts (top-level toggle alongside the list) shows the three buckets with per-card uplift suggestions and a "Run reminders now" button.

#### Phase F — Reports / Analytics
- New `GET /contracts/reports/dashboard` aggregates ARR / MRR / at-risk value by 30/60/90 / tier breakdown / status / coverage gap (assets without an active contract).
- New **Reports** view in CRM → Contracts presents ARR, MRR, at-risk pipeline, tier breakdown, and the uncovered-assets upsell signal.

#### Phase G — AI assistance
- New endpoints `POST /contracts/{id}/ai/recommend-cover`, `/ai/suggest-uplift`, `/ai/draft-terms` — use the Emergent LLM key (gpt-4o-mini) when configured, fall back to deterministic baselines otherwise. **Never auto-send, auto-sign or auto-activate** — the spec was explicit and the code enforces it.

### Files

Backend:
- New: `routes/crm_contract_templates.py` · `routes/crm_contract_send.py` · `routes/crm_contract_lifecycle.py` · `utils/crm_contract_pdf.py`
- Updated: `routes/crm_contracts.py` (build_contract_doc carries new fields) · `route_registry/crm.py` (three new routers)

Frontend:
- New: `pages/CRM/Contracts/{contractCatalog,ContractWizard,ContractMatrix,ContractDashboards,PublicContractAcceptPage}.js`
- Updated: `pages/CRM/CRMContracts.js` (Cover & Compare tabs · view switcher · PDF/Send buttons) · `routes/AppRoutes.js` (public accept route)

### Tests

- `test_iter_220e3_contracts_phase_a_templates.py` (12 tests) — catalog, template seeding, CRUD, apply-template, build_contract_doc fields.
- `test_iter_220e3_contracts_phase_a_frontend.py` (4 tests) — wizard step labels, matrix surfaces, CRM page wiring, fallback catalog.
- `test_iter_220e3_contracts_phase_def_g.py` (9 tests) — PDF byte output, renewal buckets, idempotent reminders, reports dashboard math, AI fallback baselines, public sign idempotency, internal pricing strip.
- `test_iter_220e3_contracts_phase_def_g_frontend.py` (5 tests) — public accept page, route, dashboards & buttons.

Regression: **2042 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** (`make regression`). Lint clean (ruff + ESLint).

## Iter 220e1 — Cover chip + banner on Summary, cover chip on public tracking ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Operator follow-up:

> The engineer also needs to see what type of cover if any the
> gym has on the summary screen so they know they can work on the
> machines and fit parts or they have to wait for authorisation.

### Shared helper: `computeCoverState(job)`

Extracted from the iter 220e0 Complete-tab logic into a single
exported function. Reads `case.source_meta.coverage_status`,
`source_meta.warranty_active`, and `case.cover_type` and returns
a `{covered, kind, label, short, detail}` shape. Recognises:

- Active warranty → `kind='warranty'`, short label
  *"Warranty"*, detail *"Parts + labour are warranty-funded.
  Proceed without spend approval."*
- Active contract → `kind='contract'`, short label
  *"GOLD contract"* (or *"Contract"* when no tier), detail
  *"Parts + labour covered by the contract. Proceed without
  spend approval."*
- Otherwise (no contract, no warranty, `cover_type` empty /
  `chargeable` / `none`) → `kind='chargeable'`, detail
  *"Confirm any spend with the customer before fitting parts."*

### Engineer Summary (JobAtAGlance)

- **Chip** added to the chip row next to Priority + Job-type
  (`jaag-cover-chip`). Green when covered, amber when
  chargeable. Title attribute shows the full long-form label.
- **Banner** added above the existing overrun / sibling /
  handoff warnings (`jaag-cover-banner` + `-label` + `-detail`).
  First actionable signal the engineer reads on every job:
  *"Under GOLD service contract until 31/12/2027 — Parts +
  labour covered by the contract. Proceed without spend
  approval."*
- Chargeable cases get the same banner in amber with the
  *"Confirm spend"* detail so the engineer knows to ring ops.

### Complete tab refactor

- The iter 220e0 `coverState` memo was duplicating the cover
  logic. Now a one-liner that delegates to `computeCoverState`,
  so future tweaks land in one place and the two surfaces can't
  drift.

### Public live-tracking customer chip

- Backend `public_track` payload exposes a customer-safe `cover`
  block (`{covered, kind, label}`). Customer-visible label only —
  contract numbers / titles / ids / warranty expiry stay
  internal.
- Frontend renders a green emerald chip
  (`track-cover-chip` + `track-cover-label`) above the return-
  to-fix / compliance sections when `cover.covered` is true.
  Says *"Covered by service contract · no charge"* or *"Under
  manufacturer warranty"*.
- Chargeable cases render NO chip — no point worrying the
  customer pre-quote.

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220e1_cover_chip_summary_and_public.py` —
  **9 tests** green:
  - `computeCoverState` exported with correct logic for
    warranty / contract / explicit / chargeable / "none" slugs.
  - Complete tab reuses the shared helper.
  - Summary renders the chip with correct conditional label.
  - Summary renders the banner with actionable detail (proven
    via the helper detail strings).
  - Public payload returns contract / warranty / chargeable
    labels.
  - Public payload doesn't leak contract numbers, titles, ids,
    or warranty expiry.
  - Public tracking page renders the cover chip when covered.

- 0 new lint warnings.

## Iter 220dz + 220e0 — Empty custom fields hidden + cover-aware close-out ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Two screenshot-driven UX polish pins.

### 1 · Empty machine-row custom fields no longer clog Equipment

Previously every machine row rendered an ~80 px "No custom
fields yet for this machine type. Tap '+ Custom field' to add one"
placeholder, even when the org had nothing pre-configured. On a
gym with 30 machines that's 2 400 px of empty noise.

- `MachineRowCustomFields.js` now early-returns a tiny right-
  aligned "+ Custom field" link when:
  - `fields.length === 0`
  - `!creating`
  - No saved values on this row (`hasSavedValues`)
- Verbose placeholder copy deleted.
- All paths to the full panel preserved (resolved fields, saved
  values, or active editor) so engineers can still create fields
  ad-hoc when they need to.

### 2 · Close-out flow respects warranty / contract cover

The "Close & invoice" button used to fire regardless of whether
the gym was already paying for cover. Operators flagged this on
the screenshot: *"If the gym is within warranty/contract there
would be no need to invoice the job unless mis-use."*

- New `coverState` memo on the Complete tab reads
  `source_meta.coverage_status`, `source_meta.warranty_active`,
  and `case.cover_type`. Returns one of three states (warranty /
  contract / chargeable).
- When covered:
  - **Green banner** at the top of the Outcome card surfaces the
    cover label (e.g. *"Under GOLD service contract until
    31/12/2027"* or *"Under manufacturer warranty until …"*)
    plus a *"Mis-use / chargeable — bill anyway"* checkbox.
  - **"Close & invoice"** chip becomes **"Close (no invoice)"**.
  - **Auto-invoice toggle hidden** (misuse override controls
    billing for covered cases).
  - **Fast-path CTA** changes to **"I'm done — close & send the
    report"** instead of **"... close & send the invoice"**.
  - Backend complete call sends `chargeable: false` and
    `target: 'repaired'` instead of `'closed'` so the case isn't
    auto-locked to the invoice workflow.
  - Invoice draft generation **skipped entirely** when the misuse
    override isn't ticked.
  - Service report still goes to the customer (toast reads
    *"Service report emailed · no charge (under cover)"*).
- Misuse override flips every above behaviour back to the
  chargeable path — one tick is enough to invoice a mis-use case.

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220dz_engineer_ux_polish.py` — **9 tests**
  green:
  - MachineRowCustomFields collapses when empty.
  - Verbose placeholder text removed.
  - Panel stays open when row has saved values.
  - `coverState` memo + banner testids pinned.
  - Close chip label swaps to "no invoice".
  - Auto-invoice toggle hidden when covered.
  - `chargeable: willBill` pinned (was hard-coded true).
  - Fast-path skips invoice when covered, flips target to
    'repaired'.
  - Fast-path button label swaps to "send the report".
  - `coverState` recognises contract / warranty / explicit cover_type.
- Added to `Makefile` regression block (TAB indent).
- 0 new lint warnings.

### Result
- `make regression` → **1993 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Equipment tab feels half as long on a multi-machine gym.
- Engineers can no longer accidentally invoice a customer who's
  under contract — misuse is now an explicit, audit-friendly
  choice rather than the default.


## Iter 220dy — Modularise `server.py` (P3 hygiene) ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

P3 hygiene task — extract stateless startup work into a dedicated
package.

### Before / After

| File | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `server.py` | 1027 lines | **548 lines** (−47%) |
| `bootstrap/__init__.py` | — | 27 lines |
| `bootstrap/seed.py` | — | 212 lines |
| `bootstrap/indexes.py` | — | 353 lines |

### What moved

**`bootstrap/seed.py`**
- `seed_master_admin` — idempotent master-admin seed + self-heal
  of the master admin's password, lockouts, and missing org doc.
- `seed_services` — integrations + CRM admin + picklists +
  stakeholder + products + tenant mirror + membership indexes +
  optional demo-seed branches.

**`bootstrap/indexes.py`**
- `create_indexes` — every collection's index family in one
  audit-friendly file. Idempotent (MongoDB no-ops on identical
  existing indexes). Organised by tier (core / tier-2 / tier-3 /
  tier-4) with the original commentary preserved.

### Backwards compatibility

`server.py` keeps the three underscored shims
(`_seed_master_admin`, `_seed_services`, `_create_indexes`) as
thin `await bootstrap.x()` wrappers so any out-of-tree caller
importing the old names still works.

### What didn't move (and why)

- FastAPI `app` instance, mount calls, CORS / GZip middleware,
  the security-headers middleware, and the `startup` / `shutdown`
  orchestrators stay in `server.py` because they directly
  reference module-level state (`app`, `api_router`, `logger`)
  that doesn't compose cleanly into a stateless module.

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220dy_server_modularisation.py` — **7 tests** green:
  - `bootstrap` package + submodules importable + expose three
    async public functions.
  - All three underscored shims still defined in `server.py` and
    delegate to bootstrap (no inline body).
  - `server.py` line-count guard (`<700` lines, ensures the
    refactor can't be silently re-inlined by a future iter).
  - `seed_master_admin` functional: inserts when missing, self-
    heals the org doc when it's deleted.
  - `create_indexes` runs the core block end-to-end with all
    `ensure_*_indexes` patched at the call site — proves no
    historic index call was dropped.
- Three existing tests updated to read from the new locations:
  - `test_iter_216h259_engineer_lite_crm` → reads
    `bootstrap/indexes.py` instead of `server.py`.
  - `test_iter_216h272_module_trials_org_resolve` → reads
    `bootstrap/seed.py` and splits on `seed_master_admin`.
  - `test_iter_216h276_tenant_mirror` → reads
    `bootstrap/seed.py`.
- Added to `Makefile` regression block (TAB indent).
- 0 new lint warnings.
- Backend verified live (supervisor restart + curl smoke).

### Result

## Iter 220dx — Engineer "Capture serial on visit 1" auto-task ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the rubbed-off-serial loop end-to-end. Three iters
combined produce a complete experience:

1. **220dw** — Customer ticks "Serial unknown" on Log-a-Fault →
   case stamped with `capture_serial_required=True` + reason.
2. **220dx** (this iter) — Engineer's Equipment tab shows an
   amber "Action required · Capture serial on visit 1" card with
   the customer's reason; engineer reads the plate on site, types
   the serial, optionally snaps a photo, taps submit.
3. **Backend** stamps the case, flips the flag off, and back-
   fills the canonical equipment row when it doesn't already
   have a serial.

### Backend — `routes/svc/engineer_phase3.py`

**`POST /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/capture-serial`**
- `CaptureSerialIn { serial, photo_file_id?, asset_id? }`.
- 409 when the case doesn't require capture (idempotency guard —
  prevents accidental re-stamping).
- Stamps the case with `captured_serial`, `serial_captured_at`,
  `serial_capture_engineer_id`, `serial_capture_engineer_name`,
  optional `serial_capture_photo_id`, and flips
  `capture_serial_required: False`.
- Back-fills the canonical equipment row when:
  - `asset_id` resolves to an equipment doc.
  - The doc has no existing `serial_number`.
  We never overwrite an existing serial — engineer may be
  capturing a secondary plate; the primary record stays
  authoritative.
- Appends a `serial_captured` event with serial value, photo id,
  and equipment-update outcome for full audit traceability.

### Frontend — `EngineerJobDetailV2.js`

**`CaptureSerialCard` component** pinned at the very top of the
Equipment tab when `case.capture_serial_required` is true:
- Amber visual treatment (reuses the return-to-fix palette so
  engineers recognise it as an "action required" surface).
- `<QrCode>` icon. Header line: *"Action required · Capture
  serial on visit 1"*.
- Reason rendered from a `REASON_LABELS` map (rubbed_off /
  not_visible / never_had_one).
- Serial text input (autoComplete off, `capture-serial-input`).
- Photo upload (`capture="environment"` so phones jump straight
  to the rear camera; `capture-serial-photo`).
- Submit button toasts either "Saved to the case + back-filled
  on the equipment record" or "Saved to the case audit trail"
  depending on the backend's `equipment_updated` flag.
- Card disappears after success (the case's flag flipped off →
  the conditional render hides it on the next case fetch).

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220dx_capture_serial.py` — **7 tests** green:
  - 409 when case doesn't require capture.
  - Case is stamped + flag flipped off.
  - Equipment row back-filled when serial was missing.
  - Existing equipment serial is NOT overwritten.
  - No asset_id → no equipment lookup attempted.
  - Audit event recorded with serial, photo, equipment outcome.
  - Frontend renders the card + has all 5 testids + handles all
    3 reason slugs/labels.
- Added to `Makefile` regression block (TAB indent).
- 0 new lint warnings.

### Result
- `make regression` → **1977 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed**.

Engineer captures → equipment record back-filled →
Next fault by the same gym shows the right serial in the

## Iter 220dv — Per-machine field auto-load by job type ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the user's original feature request:

> "Custom Fields option should be moved to Account Settings - Where
>  the engineer can create the custom fields and tag them to
>  specific equipment based on the job type"

The end-to-end loop is now live:

1. **Admin** creates a custom field in Account Settings → Manage
   Custom Fields, tagged with `job_types: [ppm]` + scope
   `equipment_type: Treadmill`.
2. **Customer / Service desk** logs a fault with
   `case_type='ppm'`.
3. **Engineer** opens the case → Equipment tab → expands the
   Treadmill row → `MachineRowCustomFields` calls
   `GET /api/svc/work-report-fields/for-machine-row/{row_id}`.
4. **Resolver** looks up the row's parent case, reads
   `case_type='ppm'`, filters defs to job_types `[]` or `['ppm']`,
   joined with the equipment_type scope.
5. **Engineer** sees the right field set per machine row —
   universal + PPM-tagged fields render; Repair-only fields stay
   hidden.

### Why no frontend change?

`MachineRowCustomFields.js` was already wired to the
`for-machine-row` endpoint when iter 220 shipped per-machine
custom fields. The case_type filter sits in the **backend
resolver**, so the React component automatically inherits the
job-type-aware filtering — zero FE refactor needed. The pytest
suite pins the contract so a future refactor can't regress it.

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220dv_per_machine_field_autoload.py` — **6
  tests** green:
  - PPM case row sees universal + PPM-tagged fields, NOT
    repair-only.
  - Repair case row sees universal + repair-only, NOT PPM.
  - Install case sees only the universal field (no install-
    tagged def in this fixture, proving the filter excludes
    unrelated job types).
  - Legacy parent case (missing `case_type`) → resolver falls
    back to "repair" so the engineer still sees a useful set.
  - The `values` payload echoes the row's saved `custom_fields`
    so React can pre-fill on first paint.
  - Frontend contract pin: `MachineRowCustomFields.js` still
    uses the per-row endpoint + `custom_fields: next` patch.
- Added to `Makefile` regression block (TAB indent).
- 0 new lint warnings.

### Result
- `make regression` → **1966 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed**.
- User's original requirement fully satisfied — engineer auto-
  loads matching custom fields onto the Equipment tab per-machine
  based on the case's job type, configured from Account Settings.

## Iter 220dr — Equipment auto-populate + Summary capture-media removal ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Driven by the operator screenshot on the Treadmill-belt-slip job:

1. **Capture-Media block still appeared on Summary** → removed.
2. **Equipment tab was empty** when a customer had logged a fault
   against a specific machine via the portal / inbound email /

### Backend — `routes/svc/engineer.py`

**New helper `_ensure_customer_machines_attached(case, of)`**
- Reads `case.asset_id` (single) + `case.equipment_ids[]` (multi).
- For each unique ID not already in `svc_work_visit_machines` for
  this case, inserts one row populated from the canonical
  `equipment` collection (serial, manufacturer, model,
  equipment_type, asset_name).
- Falls back to `case.asset_name` when the equipment row is
  missing (free-text customer-described asset).
- Idempotent — re-runs on every engineer GET, but already-attached
  IDs are skipped. `source='customer_logged'` so the audit trail
  distinguishes auto-attached rows from manual `From site` picks.
- Best-effort — exception just logs `[engineer] customer-machine
  auto-attach failed for case=…` and continues. Never breaks
  the case load.

**`GET /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}`**
- Calls the helper after the access check, before any expensive
  enrichment. Engineer-side semantics unchanged — `machines` list
  the engineer fetches separately just naturally returns the new
  rows.

    created_at }`, reschedules `case.scheduled_at`, and flips
    `status → scheduled`.
  - Appends a `return_to_fix` event to the audit trail.
  - If `notify_customer` AND `customer_email` exists, emits a
    `job_rescheduled` notification with branded copy
    ("Return visit booked · GA-100 — back on Thu 04 Jun · 09:30").

Frontend — `EngineerJobDetailV2.js`

  Complete tab.
- "Did you fix it on this visit?" → **Yes / No**.
- "No" expands into datetime picker + reason field + customer-
  notify toggle (default ON).
- Submit posts to `return-to-fix`, clears the draft, toasts
  "Return visit booked — customer notified", and refreshes.

## Iter 220dm-hotfix — Regression hygiene cleanup ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Cleared the last three pre-existing failures from the regression
gate so the suite finishes **1908/1908 green** with zero linter
warnings.

### 1 · `emergentintegrations` sys.modules pollution
- `tests/test_iter_216h283_compliance_docs.py::test_ai_check_parses_valid_json_and_flags_match`
  previously inserted fake `emergentintegrations`,
  `emergentintegrations.llm`, and `emergentintegrations.llm.chat`
  stubs into `sys.modules` but only popped the `chat` child on
  cleanup. The bare `emergentintegrations.llm` module left behind
  had no `__path__`, so later tests that legitimately
  `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat` (via
  `routes/files.py`) blew up with
  ``'emergentintegrations.llm' is not a package``.
- Fix: snapshot whatever was in `sys.modules` before the test
  patches in fakes, and restore the snapshot on teardown.
  Cleanup is now safe regardless of which other tests ran first.

### 2 · Engineer Equipment CSV testid contradiction (220cj vs 220cl)
- `test_iter_220cj_engineer_extras_frontend::test_equipment_csv_actions_present`
  expected `equipment-csv-actions` / `equipment-csv-download` /
  `equipment-csv-import` test ids on
  `pages/ServiceOps/Engineer/EngineerEquipment.js`.
- Iter **220cl** explicitly **moved CSV off the engineer page**
  into the per-customer drawer (`EngineerCustomers.js` →
  `CustomerEquipmentCsv`), and added a negative test pinning their
  absence.
- The two iters were in direct contradiction. 220cl is the newer
  product decision, so:
  - Updated the 220cj test to a SUPERSEDED stub that asserts the
    legacy testids are **absent** (preserves the audit trail
    without contradicting 220cl).
  - EngineerEquipment.js untouched — CSV stays in the customer
    drawer as the single source of truth.

### 3 · Monthly reputation reports — partner sweep capped at 2000
- `tests/test_iter_220m_reputation_reports::test_run_sweep_with_force_period_sends_once`
  flaked once the DB grew past 2000 approved partners — the
  freshly inserted test partner was no longer in the first 2000
  rows returned by `to_list(2000)`, so the sweep never reached it
  and `sent` stayed at 0.
- Fix in `utils/reputation_reports.py::run_monthly_reputation_reports`:
  - Filter scoped to `user_id` present (an approved partner
    without a user can never receive an email).
  - `to_list(length=None)` — fetch the full eligible cohort so the
    iter is deterministic regardless of DB size. The cohort is
    "approved partner engineers with a user_id" — a bounded set
    in production, not a scaling risk.

## Iter 220dm — Push-backend wiring sweep ✅ (Feb 14, 2026)

Closes the loop on the Web Push channel enabled in Iter 220df by
guaranteeing the three highest-value engineer alert kinds actually
fire from the producers — no more silent gaps where the badge
shows zero because the dispatcher route forgot to insert a
notification row.

### Backend

**`routes/svc/diary.py` — dispatcher push wiring**
- `admin_assign_case` now fires three distinct notification kinds
  from a single transition:
  - `job_assigned` when a job lands on a new engineer (also fires
    `job_unassigned` to the previous holder, if any).
  - `job_rescheduled` when the same engineer keeps the job but the
    scheduled time changes.
- Notification-failure path now `logger.warning(...)`s instead of
  the previous bare `pass` — regressions become visible in the
  logs rather than being silently swallowed.

**`routes/svc/ppm_reminders.py` (NEW)**
- New admin sweep endpoint `POST /api/svc/admin/ppm/fire-due-reminders`
  scans open PPM cases (`case_type='ppm'`, status ∈ {new,
  scheduled, assigned}) scheduled within `hours_ahead` (1–168 h,
  default 24) and emits one `ppm_due` notification per case to the
  assigned engineer.
- Dedupe guard (`DEDUPE_WINDOW_HOURS=18`): if a `ppm_due` already
  fired for the same case + engineer within the window, the sweep
  skips and increments `skipped_dupe` so a daily cron + manual
  trigger don't double-notify.
- Master Admin may target a single org via `?organization_id=`;
  all other roles are scoped to their own org.
- Returns counts (`scanned`, `fired`, `skipped_dupe`,
  `skipped_unassigned`, `window_hours_ahead`) so the operator can
  audit the sweep result.
- Wired into `route_registry/features.py` (auto-mounted under
  `/api`).

### Tests / lint

- `tests/test_iter_220dm_push_wiring.py` — **11 tests** green:
  - PPM sweep requires admin/owner/manager (403 otherwise).
  - Sweep fires one `ppm_due` per case + counts returned.
  - Dedupe skip when `svc_notifications` already has a recent
    matching row.
  - Mongo filter pinned to `case_type='ppm'`, open states only,
    assigned engineer required, window narrowed.
  - Master-admin can target a different org explicitly.
  - Dispatch fires `job_assigned` for a brand-new engineer.
  - Dispatch fires `job_rescheduled` when the engineer is the same
    but the time changes (and does NOT fire `job_assigned`).
  - Dispatch fires `job_unassigned` to the previous engineer when
    reassigning.
  - Notification failures don't break dispatch (dispatch returns
    success and logs the warning).
  - `TOGGLEABLE_PUSH_KINDS` still contains all three pinned kinds.
  - The bare `pass` → `logger.warning(...)` source-level swap is
    audited.
- Added to `Makefile` `regression:` block (TAB-indented).

## Iter 220dk — Mid-journey ETA drift re-notify ✅ (May 30, 2026)

When traffic, a detour, or a tool-fetch swings an engineer's
arrival time by ≥ 10 min from the last sent ETA, the customer now
gets a fresh email automatically — without the engineer needing to
remember to fire one. Closes a real-world friction point flagged
in the operations audit.

### Backend — `routes/svc/engineer_eta_update.py`

**Refactor**
- Extracted the email-rendering body of `send_eta_update` into a
  reusable `_send_eta_email(*, case, user, eta_mins, message,
  trigger)` helper. The manual endpoint + the new drift checker
  share rendering, branding, logging, event emission, and the
  case-stamp update — single source of truth for the ETA email
  surface.

**New `maybe_renotify_eta_drift(*, user)`**
- Pulls the engineer's open `en_route` cases for their org (cap 5).
- For each, computes a fresh haversine ETA via
  `build_eta_minutes_estimate`. Skips when:
  - `customer_email` missing / invalid
  - `comms_auto_notify is False`
  - No baseline `eta_last_minutes` yet (first email comes from the
    `en_route` auto-comm, not from the drift checker — we don't
    second-guess that transition email)
  - Fresh estimate is `None` (stale ping / no coords)
  - `|fresh - last| < DRIFT_THRESHOLD_MIN` (10 minutes)
  - Cooldown < `DRIFT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (5 minutes) since last send
- Fires `_send_eta_email` with `trigger='eta_drift_renotify'` for
  qualifying cases and returns one result row per case touched.

**Constants pinned**
- `DRIFT_THRESHOLD_MIN = 10`
- `DRIFT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 300`

### Backend — `routes/svc/engineer_location.py`
- After persisting the ping, run `maybe_renotify_eta_drift` and
  return the renotified case IDs to the engineer mobile app
  (so it can show a small "customer notified" toast).
- The entire drift check is wrapped in try/except — a downstream
  comms failure must never break the engineer's critical-path
  location ping.

### Tests / lint
- `tests/test_iter_220dk_eta_drift_renotify.py` — **10 tests** green
  covering:
  - No baseline → quiet.
  - Missing customer_email → quiet.
  - `comms_auto_notify=False` → quiet.
  - Drift under threshold → quiet.
  - Cooldown active → quiet.
  - Happy path → fires `_send_eta_email` with `trigger=eta_drift_renotify`
    and a fresh ETA (≪ baseline of 30 min).
  - Mongo filter pinned to `en_route` + assigned engineer.
  - Constants pinned (10 / 300).
  - Location ping invokes drift check + returns renotified IDs
    in response.
  - Location ping resilient to drift-check exceptions.
- 220dg suite unaffected by refactor: **15/15 still green**.
- Combined 220c+220d suite: **106/106 green**.
- Backend ruff clean.
- Live smoke: `POST /svc/engineer/location` → 401 (registered).

### Out of scope (deferred)
- "Significant slowdown / speedup" annotation in the renotify email
  ("running 12 min later than planned" vs the silent number swap
  the customer sees today).
- SMS variant of the drift renotify (no Twilio creds; would reuse
  the same trigger gate).
- Customer-side "Pause notifications" link in the email footer
  (would set `comms_auto_notify=False` on the case via a tokenised
  URL).

## Iter 220dj — Compliance evidence pack on service-report PDF ✅ (May 30, 2026)

Every customer-facing service report now ships with a full audit
trail of the safety / regulatory work the engineer did on the
visit. Closes the loop opened by Iter 220de — the compliance pack
data was being captured per case but never surfaced to the
customer. This turns "we recorded it internally" into a tender-
winning evidence pack.

### Backend — `routes/svc/service_report.py`

**`_gather_report_data` (extended)**
- Pulls per-case `svc_ptw_requests` filtered to `status ∈ {issued,
  completed}` (a stale "requested" permit isn't customer-visible
  evidence).
- Pulls per-case `svc_loto_checklists` (all of them — every isolation
  signoff is evidence).
- Pulls per-case `svc_coshh_usage` rows (which already snapshot the
  chemical name + hazard class onto the usage doc, so the PDF
  stays consistent even if the register entry is later renamed).
- Includes a `loto_step_labels` map derived from `compliance.DEFAULT_LOTO_STEPS`
  so the report can render human-readable step text from the stored
  step IDs.

**`_build_pdf` (new section)**
- Renders a **COMPLIANCE EVIDENCE PACK** block between the existing
  H&S signoff and the customer-rating star strip.
- Three sub-blocks render independently — each only appears when
  data exists. No empty headers, no orphaned dividers:
  - **Permit to Work**: emerald "✓ completed" or blue "✓ issued"
    chip + template name + hazard category + validity window + issuer.
  - **Lockout / Tagout**: per-checklist line with engineer +
    timestamp + step count + comma-separated tick labels (humanized
    via `loto_step_labels`) + energy sources.
  - **COSHH usage**: per-record line with engineer + timestamp +
    chemical names with hazard classes + free-text notes (if any).
- Entire section omitted when there is zero compliance data on
  the case (so unrelated 5-minute callouts stay clean).
