## Iter 220dg — Engineer → customer outbound ETA push ✅ (May 30, 2026)

We had inbound (customer-facing live tracking page via `track_token`)
but the outbound nudge was thin: the auto-comm on `en_route` showed
only the scheduled time and had no Track-live CTA. Closed both gaps:
the auto-comm now renders a live ETA + Track-live button, and the
engineer has a one-tap "Send ETA update" chip on JobAtAGlance.

### Backend — `routes/svc/engineer_eta_update.py` (new)

**Helpers (re-used by auto-notify + manual endpoint)**
- `build_tracking_url_for_case(case)` — lazy-mints `track_token` if
  missing; composes `{FRONTEND_URL}/track/{token}`. Single source of
  truth so auto-comm + manual nudge always link to the same page.
- `build_eta_minutes_estimate(case)` — haversine from latest
  `svc_engineer_locations` ping to the case `site_lat`/`site_lng`,
  divided by 35 km/h. Returns `None` when no recent (<5 min) ping,
  case isn't `en_route`, or coords missing.
- `eta_label_from_minutes(mins)` — friendly phrases ("in about 25
  minutes", "in about 1 hour", "in about 2h 5m"); `None` collapses
  to "shortly" so templates always render cleanly.

**New endpoint `POST /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/eta-update`**
- Pre-conditions: case exists (404), caller is assigned engineer
  or admin (403), status ∈ {assigned, en_route, on_site} (409),
  customer_email present (400), `comms_auto_notify` not False (409).
- Body: `{eta_minutes?: 0–480, message?: ≤400 chars}`. Engineer-
  supplied minutes win over the live estimate; message renders as
  a callout in the email.
- Renders via the `engineer_en_route` template + auto-injects the
  Track-live CTA (belt-and-braces if operator stripped the token).

  emits a `comm` event with full context (`tracking_url`,

  `tracking_link_html`, `engineer_message_html` in the email context.
- Lazy import to keep the dependency one-way
  (`engineer_eta_update → comms`).
- Wrapped in try/except so any failure during ETA lookup falls back
  cleanly to "shortly" + no Track-live button.

**Default template update**
- `engineer_en_route` body now references `{{eta_label}}`,
  `{{engineer_message_html}}`, `{{tracking_link_html}}` so a
  freshly-seeded org's first `en_route` transition includes a
  Track-live CTA out of the box.

  `jaag-eta-cancel`, `jaag-eta-preset-{5|10|20|30}`,

## Iter 220de — Compliance Pack: PTW, COSHH register, LOTO ✅ (May 30, 2026)

Three field-engineering compliance gates shipped together. Required
for MOD / NHS / national-chain contracts; HSE-mandated for hot work,
electrical isolation, working at height. All endpoints registered;
all gates lazy-seed sensible defaults on first read so the engineer
can use them on day one without admin setup.

### Backend — `routes/svc/compliance.py`

**Permit to Work (PTW)**
- 8 hazard categories (hot_work, electrical, height, confined_space,
  asbestos, lifting, excavation, other).
- 3 default templates lazy-seeded (Hot Work, Electrical Isolation,
  Working at Height) each with hazards + controls + validity_hours.
- Admin: `GET/POST/DELETE /svc/compliance/ptw/templates`.
- Engineer: `POST /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/ptw-requests` →
  `GET /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/ptw-requests`.
- State machine: `requested → issued → completed`. Admin issues
  via `POST /svc/admin/ptw-requests/{id}/issue` (stamps valid_from /
  valid_until from `validity_hours`); engineer completes via
  `POST /svc/engineer/ptw-requests/{id}/complete`. 409 on bad state.

**COSHH register**
- 8 hazard classes (flammable, corrosive, irritant, toxic, harmful,
  environmental, oxidising, other).
- 3 default chemicals lazy-seeded (WD-40, IPA, treadmill silicone)
  with supplier + controls.
- Admin: `GET/POST/DELETE /svc/compliance/coshh` (soft-delete).
- Engineer picker: `GET /svc/engineer/coshh/active`.
- Per-case usage: `POST /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/coshh-used`
  accepts 1–20 entry_ids and snapshots `{id, name, hazard_class}`
  onto the usage doc (immutable record even if the register entry
  is later renamed).

**LOTO**
- 7 default steps (notify, shutdown, isolate, lockout, tagout,
  dissipate, verify) with 5 marked required.
- `GET /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/loto` returns the template
  steps + history.
- `POST /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/loto` 400s if any required
  step is missing; persists `{ticked_step_ids, energy_sources,
  signature_url, notes}` and emits a `loto_checklist` event.

**Compliance summary**
- `GET /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/compliance-summary` —
  composes the three sections into one read for the JobAtAGlance
  card: `{ptw:{requests, active, needs_action}, loto:{completed_count,
  needs_action}, coshh:{recorded_count}}`.

### Frontend — `ComplianceCard.js` (new component)
- Single card mounted on `JobAtAGlance` between handoff notes and
  the arrival button. Goes quiet when nothing needs attention,
  collapses to a single "Log compliance" link when no records exist.
- Amber header with chips when an action is needed:
  - **PTW needed** (rose) / **PTW issued** (blue chip with state).
  - **LOTO needed** (rose) / **LOTO ✓** (emerald) when complete.
  - **COSHH ✓** (emerald) when usage logged.
- Three modal dialogs (PTW / LOTO / COSHH) bottom-sheet on mobile:
  - `PtwDialog`: template picker + notes + Request CTA + inline
    "Complete" button per issued permit.
  - `LotoDialog`: full checkbox list with required-* indicator,
    energy-sources free-text, Submit gated on required steps.
  - `CoshhDialog`: scrollable register picker (controls shown
    inline) + notes + Log CTA.
- All test IDs stable: `compliance-card`, `compliance-toggle`,
  `compliance-ptw-*`, `compliance-loto-*`, `compliance-coshh-*`,
  `ptw-template-select`, `ptw-request-submit`, `loto-steps`,
  `loto-submit`, `coshh-list`, `coshh-submit`.

### Tests / lint
- `tests/test_iter_220de_compliance_pack.py` — **16 tests** green:
  - PTW: lazy seed, admin gate, category validation, request emits
    event, issue stamps validity, complete-from-non-issued 409.
  - COSHH: lazy seed, usage snapshots names, empty-pick 400.
  - LOTO: default steps, missing required → 400, happy path persists
    + emits event.
  - Summary: composes all three, PTW-needed flag respects
    `case.ptw_required`.
  - Frontend: ComplianceCard mounted, all dialogs + endpoints wired.
- Added to `Makefile regression:` (TAB-indented).
- Combined 220c+220d series: **50/50 green**.
- Backend ruff + frontend ESLint clean.
- Live smoke: 5 new endpoints all return 401 unauthenticated
  (registered through the ingress).

### Out of scope (deferred)

- Multi-engineer LOTO (group lockout) — current MVP is single-engineer.

## Iter 220cw — Voice-to-job (driver-friendly mic FAB) ✅ (May 30, 2026)

The big engineer-review remaining win: one-handed / driving voice
capture that ends with a pre-filled New Job form.

### Backend — `POST /api/svc/engineer/ai/voice-to-job`
- New endpoint on `engineer_ai.py`. Pipeline:
  1. **Validate** audio mime (webm / mp4 / ogg / mp3 / wav / m4a)
     and size (≤ 20 MB) — same gate as the existing `/transcribe`
     and `/dictate-summary` endpoints.
  2. **Whisper** transcription via the existing
     `_transcribe_audio` helper (Emergent LLM Key, model
     `whisper-1`). 422 returned on empty transcript so the engineer
     gets a clear retry prompt.
  3. **GPT-5.2 extraction** by re-using
     `routes/svc/independence.py::jobs_parse_email` — same JSON
     schema as the paste-email helper, so the field shape matches
     what the New Job form already knows how to consume.
     Soft-fails to `{parsed: {}}` if the LLM errors so the engineer
     never loses the transcript.
  4. **Audit-logs** via the existing `_log_call` hook
     (`kind="engineer_voice_to_job"`).
- Returns `{transcript, parsed, raw}`.

### Frontend — `VoiceToJobButton.js`
- Brand-new component. Floating gradient-blue mic FAB pinned to the
  bottom-right of EngineerHomeV2.
- Reuses the proven MediaRecorder pattern from
  `EngineerDictationButton`:
  - Auto-detects best supported codec (`audio/webm;codecs=opus`
    preferred).
  - 90s auto-stop cap (longer than the dictate-summary 60s — voice
    job briefings tend to be richer).
  - Pulsing red ring while recording, tap-to-stop.
- On success:
  - Stashes `{transcript, parsed}` in
    `sessionStorage["svc.engineer.voiceJobDraft"]`.
  - Navigates to `/svc/engineer/jobs/new?from=voice`.
  - Notifies engineer with the field count pre-filled.
- Falls back to `null` (no FAB) on browsers without MediaRecorder.

### Frontend — `EngineerNewJob.js`
- New `useEffect` reads `?from=voice` on mount, pulls the draft from
  sessionStorage, deep-merges `{customer_*, site_*, title,
  description, priority, scheduled_at}` onto the form, and clears
  the draft so a refresh doesn't replay the prefill.
- `description` falls back to the raw transcript when the parser
  couldn't synthesise one — so the engineer always has something
  usable.

### Tests / lint
- `tests/test_iter_220cw_voice_to_job.py` — **6 tests**, all green:
  - Happy path returns transcript + parsed fields.
  - 415 on unsupported mime.
  - 413 on > 20 MB audio.
  - 422 on empty transcript.
  - Soft-fail on parser error (transcript still returned).
  - Endpoint contract guard.
- Added to `Makefile regression:` (TAB-indented).
- Combined 220c-series suite: **56/56 green**.
- Frontend lint clean (3 files). Backend ruff clean.
- Live smoke: endpoint registered (401 unauthorised, expected).

had to push 4 buttons across 2 screens to wrap a job. This collapses
the whole sequence into one tap.

### Frontend — `EngineerJobDetailV2.js`
- New `completeAndSendInvoice()` action in `CompleteTab`. Runs the
  full close-of-day sequence with each step wrapped in its own try
  so a single failure (e.g. no chargeable lines yet) never blocks
  the next step:
  1. **Stop the timer** (any open `on_site` / `travel` entry) via
     the existing offline-queue helper so a flaky signal doesn't
     leak £ from the engineer's hours.
  2. **Capture signature** (if drawn).
  3. **Complete the job** with `target=closed`.
  4. **Generate invoice draft** from time + mileage + parts via
     the existing engineer_phase3 endpoint.
  5. **Email branded service report** to the customer via
     `POST /svc/cases/{case_id}/service-report/email` (default body
     — endpoint already defaults to `case.customer_email`).
- Bottom sticky bar now shows two CTAs:
  - **"I'm done — close & send the invoice"** (big emerald primary).
  - **"Or set status manually"** (secondary, falls back to the
    original target-picker flow with the `awaiting_sign_off /
    repaired / closed` chips).
- Test IDs: `complete-fast-path`, `complete-submit` (preserved).

### Tests / lint
- `tests/test_iter_220cv_fast_path_close_out.py` (**5 tests**, all
  green) — contract guards pinning the 4 endpoints the fast-path
  CTA calls so a future refactor that renames any of them will
  fail loud:
  - `POST /svc/engineer/time/stop`
  - `POST /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/complete`
  - `POST /svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/generate-invoice-draft`
    (lives on `engineer_phase3.py` router)
  - `POST /svc/cases/{case_id}/service-report/email`
  - + a signature check that the report-email endpoint accepts an
    empty body (so `axios.post(url, {}, …)` works).

### 2. Duplicate-job warning on the New Job form
- New endpoint **`GET /api/svc/engineer/customers/open-cases`** in
  `engineer_customers.py`. Matches on email / phone / case-insensitive
  name (plus optional site disambig) and returns up to 5 currently-open
  cases with `status ∈ {new, scheduled, in_progress, on_hold, awaiting_parts}`.
- `EngineerNewJob.js` debounces (400ms) on customer-name/email/phone/site
  changes and renders an amber warning panel listing the open cases.
  Each row is a button that navigates straight to that case so the
  engineer can pick up the existing job instead of duplicating it.

  form polls opportunistically on every keystroke).

  `newjob-open-case-{id}`.

### 3. Quote/Job → Invoice continuity
- New endpoint **`GET /api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}/invoice-prefill`**
  in `engineer_invoices.py`. Pulls everything needed to skip manual
  re-keying at close-out:
  - Labour: sum of `svc_time_entries.duration_minutes` (on_site) ÷ 60
    × engineer's hourly rate.
  - Travel: sum of `svc_mileage_entries.miles` × mileage rate.
  - Parts: one line per `svc_cases.allocated_parts` row (SKU + machine
    surfaced in line notes).

  - Falls back to a single labour line if there's nothing to bill yet.
  - 404 on missing/cross-engineer case (defensive).
  - Returns `totals_meta { on_site_minutes, on_site_hours, miles,
    parts_count, … }` so the UI can show "Loaded 1.5h labour · 12 mi
    · 1 part" in the success toast.
- `EngineerInvoiceBuilder.js` now reads `?case_id=` from the URL on
  mount and (when `isNew`) fetches the prefill, then deep-merges into
  the form state. Manual input is never overwritten on subsequent edits.

## Iter 220cq — Channel Performance reports tile ✅ (May 30, 2026)

**Why now**: 220cp gave every case a normalised `intake_channel`.
The natural follow-up is *acting on the signal* — surfacing
"Where work comes from" so the tenant operator can see whether
their portal investment is shifting jobs off the (expensive)
phone-call path.

### Backend — `GET /api/svc/reports/channel-performance`
New endpoint in `routes/svc/reports.py`. Aggregates `svc_cases` by
`intake_channel` (fallback `source` for legacy rows) over a window
(default 90 days) and joins invoiced quote totals per case so we
can attribute revenue back to channel.

Response shape:
```json
{
  "from": "…", "to": "…",
  "totals": { "case_count": N, "closed_count": N, "revenue_gbp": £ },
  "rows": [{
    "channel": "portal",
    "count": 12,
    "closed_count": 7,
    "close_rate": 0.5833,
    "avg_hours": 18.4,
    "revenue_gbp": 1240.00
  }, …]
}
```

Rules:
- Unknown channels collapse to `other` (closed taxonomy for the UI).
- `avg_hours` only averages *closed* rows — open cases never blend
  in as zero.
- Window defaults to 90 days (longer than the 30-day summary because
  the channel mix changes slowly).
- Live smoke against the master-admin tenant: 526 cases bucketed as
  phone (312), other (166), portal (35), email (10).

### Frontend — `ServiceOpsReportsPage.js`
Added a **"Where work comes from"** Section (Inbox icon) inside the
existing reports grid, sitting between Downtime and AI observability.
Per channel:
- Channel label (rendered via the shared `resolveChannel` helper
  introduced in 220cp).
- Right-aligned stats: `N cases · X% closed · Yh avg · £Z`.
- Blue bar = case-count share; green bar underneath = revenue share
  (only shown when the channel has revenue, so unmonetised channels
  don't carry a confusing zero-bar).
- Footer summary chip with platform totals.

Test IDs: `reports-channels`, `channel-row-{channel}`, `channel-totals`.

### Tests
- `tests/test_iter_220cq_channel_performance.py` (5 tests):
  - Buckets by `intake_channel`, attributes invoice revenue, computes
    close-rate.
  - Falls back to `source` for legacy rows; missing both → `other`.
  - `avg_hours` only averages closed rows.
  - Unknown channels collapse to `other`.
  - Empty window returns zero totals without crashing.
- Added to `Makefile regression:` (TAB-indented).
- Combined 220c[m,n,o,p,q] suite: **25/25 green**.
- Pre-existing live-server reports suite still **27/27 green**.

## Iter 220co — Parts cost per machine rollup ✅ (May 30, 2026)

  `svc_work_visit_machines.id` set, filtered to
  `status ∈ {pending, approved, fulfilled}`. Each row contributes
  `qty × list_price_gbp` to the bucket.

  - `totals.parts_cost = { approved_gbp, pending_gbp, total_gbp,
    approved_qty, pending_qty, request_count }` — all £ values rounded
    to 2dp.

    pending_qty }` — same breakdown per case so the timeline can show
    a £ chip beside each visit.

  `equipment-history-visit-cost-{rowId}`).

  - Mixed approved/fulfilled + pending → totals split correctly,

## Iter 220ca / 220cb — Competitor signup defense ✅ (May 29, 2026)

**User ask**:
> "The mandatory fields are because I'm worried about competitors on the free trial."

The mandatory address fields alone don't stop a determined competitor.
Real defenses target identity, not form length. User chose **b**
(competitor-domain blocklist, named Orbit 4 + ServiceSport) and **e**
(Companies House lookup with "flag for review" fallback for sole
traders / non-UK / fresh businesses).

### Iter 220ca — Competitor email-domain blocklist

#### Backend
1. **`utils/competitor_blocklist.py`** — static, suffix-aware
   blocklist with two helper functions:
   - `is_competitor_email(email)` → bool. Case-insensitive. Walks the
     domain tree so `team.uk.orbit4.com` matches `orbit4.com`.
     Prefix matches do NOT trip (`orbit4-fans.com` is fine).
   - `competitor_block_reason(email)` → friendly "email sales" message
     used as the 400 detail body.
2. **Blocked domains** (15 total): orbit4.com/.co.uk, servicesport.co.uk/.com,
   trainerize.com, mindbodyonline.com/.io/hq.com, perfectgym.com,
   glofox.com, abcfitness.com, xplor.com/xplortechnologies.com/.io,
   clubright.co.uk, gymmaster.com, wellnessliving.com, mywellness.com,
   technogym.com, fitnessfix.co.uk, fitlock.co.uk, gymequipmentcare.co.uk.
3. **`POST /api/auth/register`** — for trial signups only, calls
   `competitor_block_reason()` before any state mutation. Blocked →
   400 with a "talk to sales@gymaxisai.com" message. Non-trial CRM
   invite path is untouched (the CRM team can still invite a
   competitor employee as a B2B contact).

#### Tests
4. **`tests/test_iter_220ca_competitor_blocklist.py`** — 23 tests:
   user-named + parametric across all 12 known-competitor domains,
   sub-domain walk, prefix-doesn't-match safety, case + whitespace,
   malformed-input doesn't-crash, integration with `/auth/register`
   blocking trial signups + allowing non-trial signups from the same
   domain + allowing clean emails.

### Iter 220cb — Companies House verification on trial signup

#### Backend
5. **3 new endpoints at `/api/account/companies-house/*`** — same
   client as the existing `/master-admin/companies-house/*` proxies
   but reachable by ANY logged-in user (so the post-step-1 trial
   user can search), rate-limited per-user (30 searches / 5 min,
   15 profile fetches / 5 min) to stop a competitor harvesting our
   key:
   - `GET /account/companies-house/status` — health probe for the
     frontend; falls back to manual entry when disabled.
   - `GET /account/companies-house/search?q=...&limit=` — typeahead
     search. Short-circuits at `len(q)<2` to avoid burning API calls
     on every keystroke.
   - `GET /account/companies-house/company/{number}` — full profile
     so the form can auto-fill the registered address.
6. **`ORG_ALLOWED_FIELDS`** extended with `company_number`,
   `companies_house_verified`, `pending_review`,
   `pending_review_reason` (whitelist-enforced — callers cannot
   spoof their way to verified status).
7. **`_serialise_org`** surfaces all 4 keys on `/auth/me` so the
   Master Admin org drawer can render a "Pending review" badge.

#### Frontend
8. **`<CompaniesHouseSearch/>`** — new typeahead inside
   `<ProfileCompletionFields/>` at the top of the Company section.
   Debounced 350ms search → result list → click a match → fetches
   full profile → auto-fills `address_line1/2/3 + city + postcode`
   + stamps `company_number` + `companies_house_verified=true`.
   Renders a green "verified" pill with a "Change" action.
9. **"Can't find your company?" escape hatch** — clicking it
   reveals the manual address inputs and stamps `pending_review=true`
   with reason `manual_company_entry`. The operator sees an amber
   banner explaining the review.
10. **Graceful fallback** — when `/status` reports `enabled=false`,
    the typeahead doesn't render and the operator gets plain manual
    address entry (matches the pre-220cb experience).

#### Persistence
11. **`/api/account/complete-profile`** accepts and persists all 4
    new keys; the whitelist still strips anything outside the
    allowed set (e.g. a caller can't sneak in
    `companies_house_verified_by_admin: true`).

#### Tests
12. **`tests/test_iter_220cb_companies_house_signup.py`** — 11 tests:
    status enabled/disabled, search short-circuit, search rate-limit
    key-scoping, profile happy-path, profile 503 when disabled, and
    complete-profile persisting verified + pending-review states +
    stripping spoofed keys.
13. End-to-end smoke on preview: fresh trial → /complete-profile
    auto-redirect → typed "orbit4" → 4 CH results → picked Orbit4
    Group Limited (no. 12175398) → verified banner + address
    "7 School Lane, Hartford" auto-filled from CH.

### Combined Regression
14. **Full `make regression` (1570 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failures, ~159s).**
    Frontend + backend lint clean.

### Notes for production
15. The CH API key is **already configured on production**
    (`gymaxisai.com/api/master-admin/companies-house/status` returns
    `enabled: true`) — the new `/account/companies-house/*` routes
    will work the moment we redeploy. Added the same key to the
    preview `.env` so this iter could be tested live.

## Iter 220bz — Mandatory trial-signup profile completion ✅ (May 29, 2026)

**User ask** (verbatim from a frustrated screenshot):
> "Customer sign up/trial - We need to make fields Mandatory. Primary
> Contact, Full Name, Full Address, phone number, email, date of birth,
> Company Name, Company Address, Company Phone Number if different.
> We've had someone sign up and I don't know anything about them!"

**Chosen design** (after a clarification round):
- DOB → dropped (not GDPR-defensible for B2B trial intake).
- UX → two-step mandatory: Step 1 = email + password + phone (20s, account created), Step 2 = full primary-contact + company addresses (gated, no skip).
- Company phone → conditional behind a "Company has a different phone number" toggle.
- Backward-compat → existing trials (e.g. Waris Gym) are blocked at the dashboard route and routed to `/complete-profile` until they fill the form.

### What shipped

#### Backend
1. **`POST /api/account/complete-profile`** — validates all required
   keys, strips non-allowed payload fields through `ORG_ALLOWED_FIELDS`,
   stamps `profile_completed_at` on the org doc, idempotent re-submits
   preserve the original timestamp.
2. **`ORG_ALLOWED_FIELDS`** extended with the new keys:
   `primary_contact_name`, `primary_contact_address_line1/2/3`,
   `primary_contact_city/postcode/country`, `company_phone`,
   `profile_completed_at`.
3. **`/api/auth/login`** and **`/api/auth/me`** now surface
   `profile_completed_at` so the React gate can short-circuit without
   an extra round-trip.

#### Frontend
4. **`TrialSignupModal.js`** — Step 1 now requires phone, Step 2
   replaced entirely with the new `<ProfileCompletionFields>` form
   (no skip button, must submit to proceed). Modal auto-widens to
   `max-w-2xl` on step 2 to fit the address grid. Dead `INDUSTRY_OPTIONS`,
   `EMPLOYEE_RANGES`, `REFERRAL_SOURCES`, `SelectField` removed.
5. **`<ProfileCompletionFields>`** — new shared component
   (`components/shared/ProfileCompletionFields.js`) used by both the
   signup modal and the backward-compat gate. Two-section layout with
   conditional "Company has a different phone number" toggle. Every
   input has a unique `data-testid`. Exports `emptyProfileForm()` and
   `findMissingRequired()` helpers so callers don't duplicate
   validation logic.
6. **`/complete-profile` route** + **`CompleteProfilePage.js`** —
   standalone full-page gate for legacy trials. Pre-fills name + email
   from `useAuth()`. The only escape hatch is "Sign out" (no skip).
7. **`DashboardRoute` gate** — wraps the existing `is_master_admin`
   redirect. When `user.trial.is_trial && !user.profile_completed_at`
   and the user isn't master-admin, redirects to `/complete-profile`.

#### Regression
8. **`tests/test_iter_220bz_profile_completion.py`** — 7 tests
   covering: missing-required-fields → 400 (names every missing key),
   happy path stamps + persists, idempotent re-submit preserves the
   original stamp, whitelist strips unallowed keys (e.g. callers
   cannot smuggle `is_master_admin: true` through), missing org → 404,
   `/auth/me` surfaces the stamp.
9. **`tests/test_iter_220by_security_document.py`** refactored to
   mount only the `security_document_router` on a throwaway FastAPI
   app instead of importing `server.py`. Fixes a transient
   regression-suite collection error where Stripe SDK imports failed
   when this test ran after `sys.modules`-patching tests.
10. Both registered in `make regression`. **Full run: 1536 passed,
    15 skipped, 0 failures (~159s).** Frontend + backend lint clean.

#### End-to-end smoke (preview)
11. Registered a fresh trial via `/api/auth/register` → `/auth/me`
    returns `profile_completed_at=""` → logged in via `/login` form
    → was correctly redirected to `/complete-profile` with the
    form pre-filled from the auth context (name + email).
12. Submitted the full payload → `/auth/me` now returns
    `profile_completed_at="2026-05-29T21:..."` → idempotent
    re-submit preserves the original timestamp.

## Iter 220bx — Pre-publish Social Autopilot Launch-Tone checker ✅ (May 29, 2026)

**User ask**:
> "Pre-publish post-checker that warns if a generated post sounds like
> an established brand (references case studies, claims metrics, talks
> 'trusted by thousands') while we're still in launch week."

### What shipped

#### Backend
1. **`utils/social_tone_check.py`** — heuristic launch-tone rulebook
   (regex-based, instant, no LLM budget). 14 rules across 3 categories:
   `metric_claim` (percentages, hours-saved, cut-by-N%), `social_proof`
   (thousands of customers, case studies, "since we launched"), and
   `established_voice` ("trusted by", "industry-leading", "proven",
   "founded in YYYY"). Output is a stable dict: `{status:"ok"|
   "warnings"|"failed", findings:[…], checked_at, checker_version,
   on_campaign}`. Severity rollup: any "high" → `failed`; any non-"high"
   → `warnings`; clean → `ok`.
2. **Off-campaign downgrade** — when `on_campaign=False`, the same
   findings surface but as `severity="low"` so the operator deliberately
   publishing under the established voice sees a quiet stripe, not a
   red banner.
3. **`check_draft_tone_with_llm`** — optional Claude Sonnet 4.5 second
   pass for borderline drafts. Fails CLOSED (returns
   `{verdict:"ok", skipped:True}`) when the LLM key is missing or the
   vendor errors, so the route never crashes.
4. **`generate_post_for_channel` runs the check at draft time** —
   every new post is stamped with `tone_check.status` so the panel can
   render a banner without an extra round-trip.
5. **`POST /api/marketing/social-autopilot/posts/{id}/recheck-tone`** —
   re-runs the rulebook on demand (e.g. after the operator edits a
   caption). `?deep=true` invokes the LLM second pass and merges its
   findings. Rate-limited (60 rechecks per admin per 10 min). Persists
   the new `tone_check` back onto the post.

#### Frontend
6. **`<ToneCheckBanner>` in `SocialAutopilotPanel.js`** — renders at
   the top of every `PostCard` between the channel header and the
   image:
   - `status="ok"` → slim green stripe "✓ Launch tone OK · Recheck".
   - `status="warnings"` → amber banner with the top 4 findings, each
     showing the matched phrase + suggested rewrite, plus "Recheck"
     and "Deep recheck (LLM)" actions.
   - `status="failed"` → same shape, rose-coloured.
   - Legacy posts with no `tone_check` field render nothing (silent).
7. **`data-testid` coverage**: `tone-check-ok-{id}`,
   `tone-check-warnings-{id}`, `tone-check-failed-{id}`,
   `tone-check-recheck-{id}`, `tone-check-deep-{id}`,
   `tone-check-findings-{id}`.

#### Regression
8. **`tests/test_iter_220bx_social_tone_check.py`** — 16 tests
   covering: rule-matching for each category, off-campaign downgrade,
   hashtag scanning, span dedup, generator-wiring (tone_check
   persisted on insert), the recheck route happy-path / 404 / 403,
   LLM-second-pass fail-closed paths (no key + vendor exception).
   Wired into `make regression` (Makefile line 207, TAB-indented).
9. **Full regression**: 1523 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failures (~159s).

#### Bug fix bundled in
10. **`image_variant` UnboundLocalError regression in `generate_post_for_channel`**
    — the previous iter accidentally deleted the
    `image_variant = "A" if n_existing % 2 == 0 else "B"` line, which
    made the function crash on every call. Restored. (Iter 220bw's
    own tests `test_generate_post_stamps_campaign_when_active` and
    `test_generate_post_no_campaign_uses_established_prompt` were
    silently broken before this fork — now passing again.)

**User asks**:
> "Social media auto-pilot — We need launch content — the content
> that the AI is creating at the moment is that of an established
> platform — We need a launch campaign and be able to use Keyword to
> create campaigns, such as Launch content feature heavy."
>
> "Keep track of Instagram by regular crawls of
> https://www.instagram.com/p/DYfu35JNbkJ/. I will post TikTok and
> LinkedIn once created."

**User-confirmed scope choices**:
- Launch content mix: feature reveals + problem→solution + "Built by
  ops people for ops people".
- Schedule while active: **blend 70% launch / 30% established voice**.
- IG crawl cadence: **daily, public preview only**.
- Failure mode: **silent retry + log, no UI noise**.

### What shipped

#### Backend
1. **3 launch archetypes** registered in `utils/social_autopilot.py`:
   `feature_reveal`, `problem_solution_story`, `built_by_ops`. Picked
   deterministic round-robin so a fresh feed cycles all three before
   repeating.
2. **`build_launch_prompt(channel, topic, campaign, archetype)`** —
   replaces `build_prompt` when the post lands on-campaign. Includes
   an explicit anti-hallucination preamble:
   > GymAxis is in its LAUNCH WEEK — the platform is BRAND NEW.
   > DO NOT write as if it has existing customers, case studies, or
   > established usage. DO NOT invent metrics like '4 hours saved'.
   > Lean on the ASPIRATION, not the proof.
   Campaign name + keywords woven in.
3. **70/30 deterministic blend** via `should_use_launch_tone(blend, n)`
   — predictable schedule rather than random sampling (easier for the
   operator to predict what tomorrow's feed will look like).
4. **`generate_post_for_channel` now stamps the campaign** —
   `generation_meta.campaign_id`, `.campaign_name`,
   `.campaign_archetype`, `.on_campaign` on every saved draft.
5. **6 campaign-CRUD endpoints**: list, create, activate (singleton
   per type), pause, delete. Master-admin only.
6. **`utils/social_tracker.py`** — public-post crawler with three
   helpers: `parse_engagement_from_html` (OG-tag based, quote-aware
   regex, handles IG + TikTok + LinkedIn shapes); `fetch_public_post`
   (never raises — returns `ok`/`blocked`/`failed`); `crawl_due_tracked_posts`
   (daily sweep, appends to `engagement_history` capped at 60 entries).
7. **4 tracked-post endpoints**: list, add (dedupes by URL, auto-detects
   platform), refresh (manual recrawl), delete. Rate-limited per admin.
8. **Daily background loop** wired in `server.py` startup, gated by
   `SOCIAL_TRACKER_ENABLED` env var.

#### Frontend
9. **`SocialAutopilotCampaignsAndTracker.js`** — two new sections on
   the Social Autopilot Master Admin panel:
   * **Campaigns** — list + create form (name, type, keywords,
     blend ratio) + activate/pause/delete + collapsible "Launch
     archetypes" reference.
   * **Tracked posts** — list (likes/comments/views + caption snippet
     + last-crawl status) + add URL form (pre-filled with the launch
     teaser URL the user mentioned) + manual refresh + delete.
10. 22 new regression tests pinning everything.

### Files touched
- `backend/utils/social_autopilot.py` — archetypes, launch prompt,
  blend predicate, generator wiring, expanded `__all__`.
- `backend/utils/social_tracker.py` — new module.
- `backend/routes/marketing/social_autopilot.py` — 10 new endpoints.
- `backend/server.py` — tracker loop startup hook.
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/SocialAutopilotCampaignsAndTracker.js` — new module.
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/SocialAutopilotPanel.js` — import + wire.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bw_launch_campaigns_and_tracker.py` — 22 tests.
- `Makefile` — registered under `regression:`.

### Verified
- `make regression` → **1507 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped** (was 1485 → +22).
- Live API:
  * `GET /campaigns` → 200 with 3 archetypes.
  * `POST /campaigns` with `{name:"GymAxis Launch Week", type:"launch", keywords:[...], blend_ratio:0.7}` → 200, status: paused.
  * `POST /tracked-posts` with `{url:"https://www.instagram.com/p/DYfu35JNbkJ/"}` → 200, platform auto-detected.
- Boot log:
  * `[social-tracker] crawler registered (interval=86400s)`
  * `[social-tracker] loop started (interval=86400s)`

### Design choices
- **Singleton invariant per campaign type** — activating a campaign
  auto-pauses any other ACTIVE campaign of the same type. Means the
  operator can prep multiple drafts but only one is live at a time.
- **Soft-dedupe on tracked URLs** — adding the same URL twice
  re-activates the existing row instead of creating a dupe.
- **Engagement history capped at 60 entries** (2 months of daily
  crawls) — defensive against an oversized array.
- **The IG launch teaser URL is pre-filled** in the "Track URL" form
  so the user's first interaction is zero-friction.
- **Anti-hallucination preamble** in the launch prompt is the same
  pattern as the AI assistant's prompt-injection guardrail (Iter 220bp).

### Out of scope (tracked separately)
- Inline UI to view the engagement history sparkline (current row
  shows latest reading only; click-to-expand chart is a follow-on).
- Auto-extracting hashtag performance from the crawled posts.
- TikTok / LinkedIn URLs — user said they'll post these once made.
  The crawler already accepts them when added.

  a no-op so clicking an event highlights it; real navigation is a
  separate small ticket once we decide the destination drawer
  contract.
- Filtering / search on the timeline feed.
- Contract events (`crm_contracts`) — backend not yet merged.


## Iter 220bu — Cross-module unified timeline ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: ship the chronological 360° feed per Company / Opportunity /
Tender that combines activities, quotes, cases, and tender events
into a single ordered stream the UI can render without N+1 round-trips.

### What shipped

1. **New endpoint** `GET /crm/v2/timeline` accepting exactly one of:
   * `company_id` — pulls activities + quotes + cases + tender events.
   * `opportunity_id` — pulls activities + quotes + tender events.
   * `tender_id` — pulls linked quotes + synthesised tender events.
   * Pagination: `limit` (1–500, default 100) + `skip`.
   * Returns `{scope, events, total, limit, skip}`.

2. **Parallel multi-source query** via `asyncio.gather` across
   `crm2_activities`, `crm_quotes`, `crm2_cases`, `crm2_tenders` —
   all org-scoped via `_of(user)`. The scope entity itself is
   validated against the requesting org first (404 on mismatch).

3. **Tender events synthesised** from the tender row itself —
   `tender:created` always; `tender:status_changed` only when
   `updated_at` ≠ `created_at` (no duplicate noise for never-touched
   rows).

4. **Normalised event shape** — every event carries the same 11 keys
   regardless of source so the React renderer doesn't need a
   per-source branch:
   `{id, source_collection, source_id, type, occurred_at, subject,
   body, actor, icon_hint, status_hint, deep_link}`. Deep links are
   CRM-internal routes (`/crm/...`) so the UI can drill in without
   parsing a full URL.

### Files touched
- `backend/routes/crm_v2.py` — new `unified_timeline` endpoint +
  4 `_norm_*` helpers (`_norm_activity`, `_norm_quote`, `_norm_case`,
  `_norm_tender_event`).
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bu_unified_timeline.py` — new, 10 tests:
  scope validation, 404 on cross-tenant scope, limit guard, full
  merge, sort order, org-scoped queries (defensive), tender event
  synthesis (touched vs untouched), pagination, normalised shape
  stability.
- `Makefile` — registered under `regression:`.

### Verified
- `make regression` → **1475 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped** (was 1465 → +10).
- Live API:
  * `GET /api/crm/v2/timeline?company_id=<real-id>` → 200 with
    `{scope:{type:"company",id,label:"Third Space"},events:[],total:0,…}`.
  * `GET /api/crm/v2/timeline` (no scope) → 400 "Pass exactly one of
    company_id, opportunity_id, tender_id."
  * `GET /api/crm/v2/timeline?company_id=nonexistent-id` → 404
    "Scope entity not found in this organisation."

### Design choices
- **Sort happens in Python after the gather** — each source is queried
  with its own `created_at` index then merged. The `limit+skip`
  over-fetch (limit + skip per source) caps Mongo load at ~600 rows
  for the default limit of 100.
- **Status-changed event uses `updated_at`** — good enough for now;
  a future iteration could record discrete status_history events
  on the tender row and emit one event per transition.
- **`opportunity_id` scope intentionally skips cases** — cases link
  to companies, not deals, in our schema. Pulling cases via the
  company would be a "noisy" mismatch (you'd see every case for the
  company on the deal timeline).
- **`tender_id` scope intentionally skips activities** — activities
  don't carry a `tender_id` foreign key today. Linked quotes (which
  do) carry the tender connection through.

### Out of scope (tracked separately)
- Frontend timeline component — the API surface is stable; a future
  iteration plugs `<TimelinePanel scope={{type,id}}/>` into the
  Company / Opportunity / Tender drawers.
- Contract events (`crm_contracts`) — not yet merged into the feed.
- Activity-to-tender direct link (would require a small schema
  migration before adding `tender_id` to the activity create payload).


## Iter 220bt — Frontend picklist UX polish ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: turn the new strict-picklist 400 from "punitive" into
"intelligent" — when a user submits a bogus `lead_source`, surface a
**"Did you mean: LinkedIn?"** toast instead of a silent
`console.error`.

### What shipped

1. **`frontend/src/lib/picklistErrorHandler.js`** — single source of
   truth, exports two functions:
   * `extractPicklistError(err)` — reads the structured 400 payload
     (`error: "invalid_picklist_value"`, `key`, `field_label`,
     `received`, `valid_examples`, `hint`) and returns a normalised
     object with a fuzzy "did you mean" `suggestion` (three-tier
     fallback: case-insensitive exact → substring → token overlap).
   * `notifyPicklistError(err, notify)` — convenience that surfaces
     a rich toast and returns `true` on match so callers can fall
     through to their normal handler when it isn't a picklist error.

2. **Wired into 4 CRUD call sites**:
   * `CRMPipeline.js` → opportunity create (`handleCreate`).
   * `CRMPipeline.js` → opportunity edit save (`saveEdit`).
   * `CRMTenders.js` → tender create (list-page `handleCreate`).
   * `CRMTenders.js` → tender re-link save (`save` on the
     company/opp drawer).

3. **Lint clean** — all three touched JS files pass ESLint with 0
   warnings. The `console.error(e)` swallow pattern is gone from
   every picklist-touching save handler.

### Files touched
- `frontend/src/lib/picklistErrorHandler.js` — new helper module.
- `frontend/src/pages/CRM/CRMPipeline.js` — 2 save handlers wired.
- `frontend/src/pages/CRM/CRMTenders.js` — 2 save handlers wired.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bt_picklist_ux.py` — 7 new tests
  (helper exports, suggestion logic, both pages wired, no duplicate
  helpers, no silent swallows on save).
- `Makefile` — registered under `regression:`.

### Verified
- `make regression` → **1465 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped** (was 1458 → +7).
- Live API trace: `POST /api/crm/v2/opportunities` with
  `lead_source: "Supreme Overlord"` → **400** with full structured
  detail (`valid_examples` has 11 entries; `hint` points at
  `/api/crm/picklists/lead_source`).
- CRM page loads cleanly after the wiring, no console errors.

### Design choices
- The helper is a **stand-alone pure function** so any future CRM
  drawer (companies, contacts, cases) can drop it in as a one-liner.
  A regression test asserts there is **exactly one** copy of the
  helper to keep the toast behaviour consistent.
- The suggestion uses a three-tier fallback (exact CI → substring →
  token overlap) — no heavy Levenshtein dependency.
- For the tender re-link save which already shows an inline banner,
  the helper takes priority for picklist errors but the inline banner
  still fires for other failures (consistent UX).

### Out of scope (tracked separately)
- Inline-suggestion chip below the offending input (this iteration
  surfaces the suggestion via toast; an inline UX is the next polish
  step if/when sales-ops feedback asks for it).
- Picklist enforcement for `companies.sector` (schema migration first).
- The cross-module unified timeline (still on backlog).


## Iter 220bs — CRM evolution: strict picklists + Tender deep-linking ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: close the last unaddressed strand of the original problem
statement — "strict data typing, Picklists, cross-module relationships,
Tenders deep-linking".

### What shipped

1. **`validate_picklist_value` + `validate_picklist_fields` helpers**
   (`routes/crm_picklists.py`):
   * Case-insensitive matching; returns the canonical label so storage
     is normalised regardless of UI casing.
   * `strict=True` (default) raises `HTTPException(400)` with a
     structured detail: `error`, `key`, `field_label`, `received`,
     `valid_examples`, `hint` (pointing at `/api/crm/picklists/{key}`).
   * `strict=False` returns `None` on miss — escape hatch for legacy
     importers.
   * Empty / None passes through (picklists are optional unless the
     caller enforces requiredness separately).
   * `validate_picklist_fields(payload, {field: key}, org_id)` bulk
     normalises a CRUD payload in-place — one call per endpoint.

2. **Two new picklists** seeded:
   * `tender_status` (Draft, Parsing, In Progress, Internal Review,
     Submitted, Awarded, Lost, Withdrawn) — replaces the hard-coded
     `TENDER_STATUSES` constant.
   * `tender_outcome_reason` (Best technical answer, Best commercial
     answer, Lost — price, Lost — technical, etc.) — for win/loss
     analysis on the bid dashboard.

3. **Enforcement wired at every CRUD boundary** in `crm_v2.py`:
   * `create_opportunity` / `update_opportunity` — `lead_source`,
     `opportunity_type`, `lost_reason`.
   * `create_contact` / `update_contact` — `job_title`, `department`,
     `contact_role`.
   * `create_case` — `case_type`.
   * `create_tender` / `update_tender` — `tender_status`,
     `tender_outcome_reason`.

4. **Quote ↔ Tender deep-linking** (`routes/crm_cpq.py` +
   `routes/crm_v2.py`):
   * `crm_quotes.tender_id` foreign key. `create_quote` and
     `update_quote` both enforce same-org ownership when linking; a
     crafted cross-tenant `tender_id` gets a 400 "Linked tender not
     found in this organisation".
   * Unlink path (`tender_id: None` on update) is allowed.
   * `GET /crm/v2/tenders/{id}` now hydrates a `quotes` array (id,
     number, title, status, total, version, latest-flag) so the bid
     team can see every commercial response against the spec in one
     screen.

### Files touched
- `backend/routes/crm_picklists.py` — 2 new keys, 2 new helpers.
- `backend/routes/crm_v2.py` — picklist enforcement at 4 CRUD
  endpoints; tender ↔ quote hydration on `get_tender`.
- `backend/routes/crm_cpq.py` — `tender_id` schema field + same-org
  guard on create/update.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220an_tender_deep_linking.py` — added
  `crm_quotes` to the fake-db registry (existing 10 tests still pass).
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bs_crm_evolution.py` — new, 16 tests.
- `Makefile` — registered under `regression:`.

### Verified
- `make regression` → **1458 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped** (was 1442 → +16).
- Live API:
  * `GET /api/crm/picklists/tender_status` → 200 with 8 values seeded.
  * `POST /api/crm/v2/opportunities` with `lead_source: "Supreme Overlord"`
    → **400** with structured detail listing valid examples + hint.
  * `POST /api/crm/v2/opportunities` with `lead_source: "linkedin"`
    → **200** (canonical "LinkedIn" stored — case-insensitive match).

### Design choices
- Enforcement is **strict by default** to catch bad data at the door,
  but the `strict=False` mode is available for the bulk-import path
  if we ever need it (warn-only migration).
- Errors return `detail` as a **dict** (not a string) — the React
  picklist dropdown component reads `detail.valid_examples` to show
  inline suggestions.
- `tender_id` is **optional** on quotes — a freestanding commercial
  quote (no source tender) is the normal case.

## Iter 220bq — GDPR Article 17 polish ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: close four genuine gaps in the existing right-to-erasure
workflow ahead of the external pen-test / ICO audit.

### Polish items closed

1. **Auto-execute scheduler** — `run_gdpr_erasure_auto_executor`
   wakes hourly (configurable via `GDPR_ERASURE_AUTOEXEC_INTERVAL_MIN`)
   and calls `auto_execute_due_requests` which sweeps every
   `pending` row whose `execute_after` has elapsed. Closes the ICO
   "fulfil within one month" requirement — previously pending rows
   could sit indefinitely. Gated by `GDPR_ERASURE_AUTOEXEC_ENABLED`
   (default on). Also exposes `POST /api/gdpr/erasure/auto-execute/run-now`
   for operator-triggered sweeps.

2. **Fail-closed audit trail** — every create / execute / cancel now
   writes through `audit_required("gdpr_erasure_audit", …)`, the
   same retry-and-fail pattern used by webhooks / impersonation. If
   the audit insert fails, the user-facing request fails with 503 —
   regulator gets a guaranteed paper trail.

3. **Pre-scrub PII snapshot** — `_execute_request_impl` now captures
   the full pre-scrub PII payload (only fields the spec touches,
   skipping empty values) into `gdpr_erasure_requests.pre_scrub_snapshot`.
   The canonical row genuinely loses the data, but the org keeps an
   auditable "what was erased" record on the request.

4. **Cancellation reason** — new `CancelPayload(reason: str)`
   accepted by `/requests/{id}/cancel`; persisted into
   `gdpr_erasure_requests.cancellation_reason` and the audit row.
   Backwards-compatible (payload optional, defaults to empty string).

### Files touched
- `backend/routes/gdpr_erasure.py` — `CancelPayload`, extracted
  `_execute_request_impl`, `auto_execute_due_requests`,
  `run_gdpr_erasure_auto_executor`, `auto_execute_run_now` endpoint,
  3× `audit_required` calls, pre-scrub snapshot.
- `backend/server.py` — startup hook registers the auto-executor.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220ao_gdpr_erasure.py` — autouse fixture
  to mock `audit_required` (existing 16 tests stay green).
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bq_gdpr_polish.py` — new, 12 tests.
- `Makefile` — registered under `regression:`.

### Verified
- `make regression` → **1434 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped** (was 1422 → +12).
- Boot log: `[gdpr-erasure] auto-executor registered (interval=60m)` +
  `[gdpr-erasure] auto-executor started (interval=3600s)`.
- `GET /api/gdpr/erasure/requests?limit=1` → 200.
- `POST /api/gdpr/erasure/auto-execute/run-now` → 200

## Iter 220bp — Pen-test readiness audit (security hardening) ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: close the five gaps identified in `/app/memory/SECURITY_AUDIT_2026Q1.md` before the upcoming external pen test.

### Findings closed
| # | Severity | Gap | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-220bo-1 | HIGH | `assistant_execute_action` allowed any logged-in user (incl. Member tier) to trigger `clear_demo_data` DELETE on their org. LLM-amplified privilege risk. | Role-gated via `assert_role(["operator","owner","manager","admin","marketing_admin"])`. Master / Pulse admins still pass. |
| F-220bo-2 | MEDIUM | `/marketing/assistant/chat` accepted unbounded `message` length — 100k char prompt would burn through LLM budget. | Hard cap at 4,000 chars (400 on overflow). |
| F-220bo-3 | MEDIUM | Outbound Stripe SDK writes (`checkout.Session.create`, `Subscription.modify`) didn't pass `idempotency_key`. Retries on 5xx / double-clicks could create duplicate sessions / charges. | New `utils/stripe_client_idempotency.stripe_idem_key()` helper (deterministic, bucketed). Wired into 6 call sites across `partners.py`, `master_admin_trials.py`, `crm_modes.py`. |
| F-220bo-4 | MEDIUM | New Autopilot generate endpoints had no per-user rate limit — a leaked master-admin token could burn Sora 2 / Nano Banana budget unboundedly. | `rate_limit_async` layered on top of `_require_master_admin`. Tiers: generate / run-now → 20/hr; video-gen → 5/hr. |
| F-220bo-5 | LOW | User input concatenated into LLM prompts without delimiter framing. | `ai_guardrails.wrap_user_input()` enhanced — now emits an injection-guard header instructing the model to treat content between `<user_input>` tags as DATA, not instructions. Attacker-typed closing tags get redacted. |

## Iter 220bo — SocialAutopilotPanel "Not Found" hotfix ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Bug**: `SocialAutopilotPanel` (Master Admin → Growth → Social
Autopilot) rendered a literal "Not Found" badge in its body even
though the backend endpoints returned 200. The panel was unusable.

**Root cause** (single line):
The component destructured `const { API } = useAuth()` where `API`
already includes the trailing `/api`, then prefixed `/api/marketing/...`
itself → every fetch hit `${BACKEND_URL}/api/api/marketing/...` → 404
→ FastAPI's default `{"detail": "Not Found"}` body → the panel's
`setErr(e?.response?.data?.detail)` rendered the string verbatim.

**Why the existing regression missed it**
The 79 Pytest cases for `220bl/220bm/220bn` are all **backend-only**
(they assert routes, scheduler behaviour, idempotency, etc.). They
hit the FastAPI app directly so they never exercise the URL the
frontend actually composes. There was no integration / E2E test
that booted the browser, intercepted the network and verified the
fetch path — so a typo in the client-side URL slipped through.

**Fix**
1. `SocialAutopilotPanel.js` now follows the SEOAutopilotPanel
   convention — `const API = process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL`
   (no `/api` suffix). The `useAuth` import and the `API` prop
   drilled into `<VideoSection>`, `<PostCard>` and
   `<LegacyLibrarySection>` are gone. Net diff: -8 lines.
2. Stale companion regression in `_fake_db()` (`test_iter_220ad`)
   updated to also stub `seo_autopilot_config` — two SEO tests
   started failing once `_load_config()` awaited it; now green.
3. **New regression guard** (`test_iter_220bo_no_double_api_prefix.py`,
   3 cases):
   * Scans every `frontend/src/**/*.js` file for the smell
     "imports `API` from `useAuth()` AND also writes `${API}/api/...`"
     and fails if any file combines both.
   * Pins the SocialAutopilotPanel to the env-URL convention.
   * Asserts `/api/api/` literal never re-appears in the panel.

**Files touched**
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/SocialAutopilotPanel.js` —
  swap API source, drop `useAuth`, drop API prop drilling.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220ad_seo_autopilot.py` — extend
  `_fake_db` to cover `seo_autopilot_config`.
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bo_no_double_api_prefix.py` — new
  3-test regression guard.
- `Makefile` — register new test file under `regression:`.

**Verified**
- Network trace shows `200 OK` on `/api/marketing/social-autopilot/{status,posts,legacy-library}`.
- Panel renders hero, channel cards, status filters, 3 draft cards
  with imagery — no "Not Found" badge.
- `make regression`: **1410 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped**.

## Iter 220bk — Fully autonomous SEO keyword auto-discovery (GDPR-safe) ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Goal**: stop the master admin from having to keep researching seed
topics. The autopilot now top-up the keyword queue itself by blending
industry pillars, anonymised platform signals, and content-gap
analysis — every aggregate guarded by k-anonymity (k=5) and number
bucketing so no single organisation can be identified.

### Three-stream discovery
1. **Industry pillars** — 12-pillar deck (downtime, PPM, SLA, RIDDOR,
   member retention, contract negotiation, multi-site ops, partner
   engineers, BER/lifecycle, tender management, service desk, energy).
   LRU rotation with a 14-day cooldown per pillar.
2. **Platform-data signals** (GDPR-safe):
   - Top-fault machine type (last 90d, k≥5 orgs, n≥10)
   - Mean resolution-hours gap (rounded to nearest hour, k≥5, n≥10)
   - Top resolution-type breakdown (percent bucketed to nearest 5)
   - Daily rotation between signal types
3. **Content gap** — picks the pillar with the fewest published
   articles, ensures evergreen coverage.

### GDPR/PII safeguards
- **k-anonymity (k=5)**: every aggregate requires ≥5 distinct orgs;
  cells below threshold are suppressed (not redacted).
- **Number bucketing**: percentages → nearest 5, counts → nearest 5,
  hours → nearest int.
- **No identifier fields** in any returned dict (org_id, user_id,
  serials, names, emails, phones, sites — all stripped at the query
  layer).
- **No special-category data** — RIDDOR/H&S records excluded from
  signal queries entirely.
- **Audit trail**: every auto-discovered keyword carries
  `source` + `discovery_pillar_id` + `discovery_signal` +
  `discovery_metadata` for provenance.
- **Test coverage**: `test_signal_outputs_contain_no_pii_fields`
  scans every returned dict for forbidden field names.

### Threshold-driven top-up
- `queue_min_threshold` (default 3): refill triggers when queued
  keywords drop below this.
- `queue_target_size` (default 8): refill stops when queue hits
  this.
- Daily autopilot calls `autodiscover_top_up_queue()` before
  pulling the next keyword — so the queue self-replenishes
  silently.

### Endpoints
- `POST /api/marketing/seo/keywords/auto-discover` — manual trigger.
- `GET  /api/marketing/seo/keywords/discovery-feed` — list recent
  auto-discovered keywords with provenance metadata.
- `GET  /api/marketing/seo/autopilot/status` extended with
  `auto_discovery_enabled`, `queue_min_threshold`, `queue_target_size`.
- `PUT  /api/marketing/seo/autopilot/config` accepts the three new
  fields (validated 0-50/1-50).

### UI (SEOAutopilotPanel.js)
- "Discover keywords" button next to "Run now" in the Dashboard
  status card.
- Schedule editor extended with an "Auto keyword discovery" section:
  toggle + refill-when-below + top-up-to inputs.
- Notification on save shows added count and "GDPR-safe aggregates".

### Files touched
- `backend/utils/seo_keyword_discovery.py` — new module
- `backend/routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py` — wire into
  `run_autopilot`, add 2 endpoints, extend config schema/loader
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/SEOAutopilotPanel.js` — Discover
  button + config UI
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bk_keyword_auto_discovery.py` — 16 tests
- `Makefile` — registration

### Verified end-to-end on preview pod
First curl produced 3 auto-discovered keywords:
- Pillar: "gym treadmill downtime impact on retention"
- Signal: "why treadmills break most in UK gyms" (n=9 orgs aggregated)
- Gap: "reducing gym equipment downtime"
All GDPR-compliant, full provenance metadata persisted.

## Iter 220bj — Blog freshness & duplicate-content guard ✅ (Feb 2026)

**Problem**: The SEO autopilot was producing near-identical articles
(e.g. "How to reduce gym equipment downtime…" and "Gym equipment
downtime management software UK: a practical guide") because the
article-generation prompt had zero awareness of what had already been
published. The user spotted two articles on gymaxisai.com/blog with
the same hook ("A broken treadmill at 6 am costs you more than a
repair bill") and the same opening paragraph.

**Solution** — Four layers of anti-repetition, all in
`utils/seo_article_freshness.py`:

1. **Recent-articles context**: `build_recent_articles_context()` loads
   the last 8 published articles (title + opener + H2 list) and the
   prompt now ends with an explicit DO-NOT-ECHO block listing them.
2. **Archetype rotation**: 8 editorial archetypes (peak-hour failure,
   member-churn data, RIDDOR/compliance, contract-renewal,
   peer-benchmark, ops-director letter, data-led trends,
   myth-busting). Each new article picks the least-recently-used one
   and the prompt enforces it.
3. **Keyword-queue dedup**: `find_similar_keywords()` (Jaccard token
   overlap, stopwords stripped). New keywords above threshold 0.7 are
   saved as `needs_review` with `near_duplicates[]` instead of
   `queued`, so the autopilot won't auto-pick them.
4. **Post-generation uniqueness gate**: `check_article_uniqueness()`
   scores each new draft against every existing published article. If
   composite (title + opener) similarity ≥ 0.6, the system regenerates
   ONCE with hardened "must be different" instructions; if still
   similar, the article publishes as `needs_review` (hidden from the
   public blog).

**Master admin endpoints**:
- `GET /api/marketing/seo/articles/duplicates?threshold=0.6` — list
  all duplicate pairs in the published corpus.
- `POST /api/marketing/seo/articles/{id}/archive` — one-click archive.

**Frontend (SEOAutopilotPanel.js)**:
- New "Blog freshness check" panel at the top of the Articles tab
  with a "Find duplicates" button.
- Per-pair side-by-side display with one-click Archive buttons.
- Per-row Archive button on every article in the list.
- New `needs_review` status pill (yellow) for articles flagged by
  the uniqueness gate.

**Article doc extensions**:
- `archetype_id` — which scenario archetype generated the article
- `regenerated_for_freshness` — bool, true if Layer 4 forced a redo
- `uniqueness_score` / `uniqueness_best_match_id` — telemetry
- `status` can now be `needs_review` when post-gen similarity fails

**Tests** (`test_iter_220bj_blog_freshness.py`): 19 passing tests
covering all four layers using an in-memory fake DB.

**Production duplicate cleanup**: The two duplicate articles the user
screenshotted live on the prod MongoDB (not this preview pod). Lee can
now log into Master Admin → Growth → SEO Autopilot → Articles, click
"Find duplicates", and Archive the older one with one click.

### Files touched
- `backend/utils/seo_article_freshness.py` — new module
- `backend/routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py` — wire all 4 layers +
  add `duplicates` + `archive` endpoints
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/SEOAutopilotPanel.js` — duplicate
  audit UI + per-row archive button + `needs_review` pill
- `backend/tests/test_iter_220bj_blog_freshness.py` — 19 tests
- `Makefile` — regression registration (TAB-indented)

   pen-tester via your secure-share channel.
5. As findings arrive, append them to `PEN_TEST_FINDINGS.md`. Dev team
   triages in-place + lands fixes as `Iter 220az+` with Pytest
   regression coverage.

### Eight risk-register findings closed (or confirmed N/A)

* **F-20 — Export audit decorator.** New

  response_bytes, timestamp). Best-effort: audit-log failures NEVER
  break the user-facing download. Wired into tender-pitch +
  tender-submission PDF exports as exemplars.
* **F-23 — Single email-send write point.** Confirmed by inspection
  that every `utils/email.send_email` call routes through
  `_record_send_event()` (audit row written on every send_status:

  - `routes/service_desk.impersonate_customer` (1h JWT, reason=
    `service_desk_impersonate`)

  `utils/audit_log.assert_engineer_owns(engineer_id, row_engineer_id,

* **F-31 — /health minimal.** Confirmed `GET /api/health` + `GET /health`
  return `{"status":"ok"}` only — no version / env / build / commit

* **F-32 — Prod 500-handler scrub.** Confirmed global
  `@app.exception_handler(Exception)` returns a canned

## Iter 220aw — Security Wave 5: SSRF / AV / Secret-Vault (May 28, 2026) ✅

### Three risk-register findings closed

* **F-24 — AV scan provider.** Two-stage scan in
  `utils/malware_scan.scan_bytes`:
  1. Always-on static-signature scan (EICAR + `#!/bin/sh` / `#!/bin/bash`
     headers smuggled into binary uploads). Fires regardless of ClamAV
     availability — closes the test-signature class of pen-test
     probes even when no AV daemon is running.
  2. ClamAV daemon scan when `CLAMAV_HOST` is set.
  Behaviour matrix:
  - Static hit → 400 always.
  - No ClamAV, dev → return (open).
  - No ClamAV, prod → 503 (`STRICT_AV_MODE` env opt-in forces this in dev too).
  - ClamAV unreachable, dev → return; prod / strict → 503.
  - ClamAV virus → 400 with signature.
* **F-26 — SSRF guard.** New `utils/ssrf_guard.py` exports
  `assert_safe_external_url(url)` (raises `SSRFBlocked` HTTPException(400))
  + `is_safe_external_url()` boolean wrapper. Rejects:
  - Schemes other than `http`/`https` (no `ftp://`, `file://`, `gopher://`)
  - RFC1918 / loopback / link-local / multicast / reserved / unspecified IPs
  - AWS / GCP IMDS (`169.254.169.254`, hostname `metadata.google.internal`)
  - Userinfo-bearing URLs (`http://attacker@host`)
  - URLs > 2 KB
  - DNS-rebind: every resolved A/AAAA checked, not just one.
  Wired into `routes/crm_website_recognize._fetch` (CRM auto-recognise
  fetches user-supplied URLs) and
  `routes/marketing/brand_discovery._fetch` / `_fetch_bytes`
  (competitor-site brand crawler).
* **F-27 — Fernet field-level encryption for integration secrets.**
  New `utils/secret_vault.py` exports `encrypt_value` / `decrypt_value` /
  `encrypt_secrets_in_dict` / `decrypt_secrets_in_dict` /
  `redact_secrets_in_dict`. Reuses the `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`-derived
  Fernet key (one secret to rotate, not two). Self-describing
  `{"__enc": "v1", "data": "<fernet>"}` sentinel — both encrypt + decrypt
  are idempotent so we can migrate gradually (plaintext legacy rows
  pass through; first PUT after deploy encrypts them). Default secret
  field allow-list covers `api_token`, `webhook_secret`, `client_secret`,
  `refresh_token`, `access_token`, `private_key`, `signing_secret`,
  `password`, `secret`, `auth_token`, `consumer_secret`. The whole
  `credentials` sub-dict is encrypted as one blob to avoid leaking new
  field names as plaintext.
  Wired into `routes/integrations.py`:
  - `update_integration` encrypts on write.
  - `get_integration_config` decrypts for internal upstream-API calls.
  - `list_integrations` + `get_integration` redact to a static `••••••`
    mask for the operator UI (operators don't need to see their own
    token, only that it's set).

### New modules

* `/app/backend/utils/ssrf_guard.py` (full SSRF allow-/deny-list)
* `/app/backend/utils/secret_vault.py` (Fernet field-level enc)

### Modified files

* `utils/malware_scan.py` — static-signature scan + `STRICT_AV_MODE`.
* `routes/integrations.py` — encrypt on write, decrypt at use-time,
  redact at API surface.
* `routes/crm_website_recognize.py` — SSRF guard around URL fetch.
* `routes/marketing/brand_discovery.py` — SSRF guard around URL fetch.

### Tests

* **25 new unit tests** in `tests/test_iter_220aw_ssrf_av_vault.py`:
  - F-24: static scan detects EICAR, detects shell-in-image, misses
    clean PDF/JPEG, raises 400 in scan_bytes, clean bytes pass in dev,
    STRICT_AV_MODE fails-closed without ClamAV.
  - F-26: rejects non-http schemes, literal private IPs (IPv4 + IPv6
    + IMDS), metadata hostnames, userinfo URLs, garbage / oversize;
    allows public URLs (mocked DNS); rebind-detection (public host →
    private DNS); `assert_safe_external_url` raises SSRFBlocked.
  - F-27: encrypt → sentinel dict, roundtrip string + dict,
    idempotent on blob, decrypt-plain-unchanged, encrypt_secrets_in_dict
    covers default fields, encrypt→decrypt full roundtrip, redact
    masks values (encrypted + plain), masks empty token correctly.
  - End-to-end smoke: PUT /integrations encrypts api_token + webhook_secret
    so plaintext never reaches mongo.
* All 25 green; added to Makefile regression block with TAB.

## Iter 220av — Security Wave 4: Web-surface scrubbers (May 28, 2026) ✅

### Three risk-register findings closed

* **F-04 — Bleach allow-list on stored rich text.** New
  `utils/web_security.sanitize_rich_text()` runs every persisted HTML
  string through bleach with a conservative tag/attr/protocol set.
  Strips `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<svg>`, `<style>`, `<object>`,
  `<embed>`, `<form>`, `<link>`, `<meta>`, every `on*=` event handler,
  and `javascript:` / `data:` / `vbscript:` URLs. Clamped to 200 KB
  per field so the DB can't store 1 MB of attacker markup. Wired into:
  - `routes/crm_v2.py`: `create_activity` / `update_activity`
    (subject + body), `create_tender` / `update_tender` (title +
    issuer + executive_summary), `add_tender_question` /
    `update_tender_question` (text + response + ai_draft).
  - `routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py`: second-pass over
    `sanitize_llm_markdown` on title / excerpt / body_md /
    meta_description / qa_blocks before persist.
* **F-05 — Open-redirect on `?next=` param.**
  `utils/web_security.is_safe_next_url()` + `safe_next_or()` reject
  every classic bypass: protocol-relative `//evil.com`, backslash
  tricks `/\evil.com`, embedded schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`),
  netloc-bearing absolute URLs, control chars (`\r\n\t\0`),
  > 512-char inputs, missing leading slash. Frontend `LoginPage.js`
  + `LoginRedirectPage.js` tightened to the exact same rule-set so a
  malicious deep-link can't survive the auth bounce.
* **F-22 — Email recipient validation.** New
  `utils/web_security.validate_email_recipient()` gates every
  `send_email()` call (the helper accepts an optional `kind=`
  argument identifying the transactional family). Trust ladder:
    1. Transactional kinds (auth/system/public/supplier/engineer/
       partner — full list in `_TRANSACTIONAL_KINDS`) → pass.
    2. Same-org user → pass.
    3. CRM contact in `crm2_contacts` / `crm_contacts` / `members`
       (same-org) → pass.
    4. Partner / supplier / engineer-customer (same-org) → pass.
    5. Otherwise → 400 with a redacted reason.
  Off-by-default in dev (`ENFORCE_EMAIL_RECIPIENT_VALIDATION=false`)
  so the existing ~1200-test regression doesn't have to set up CRM
  rosters for every send_email call site. Flip on in production.

### New module

* `/app/backend/utils/web_security.py` — single home for all three
  helpers. Bleach installed via `pip` (now pinned in
  `requirements.txt` as `bleach==6.3.0` + `webencodings==0.5.1`).

### Modified files

* `routes/crm_v2.py` — 6 endpoints scrubbed.
* `routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py` — second-pass bleach over LLM output.
* `utils/email.py` — `send_email()` now accepts a `kind=` arg and
  routes through `validate_email_recipient` (no-op when env flag off).
* `frontend/src/pages/LoginPage.js` + `LoginRedirectPage.js` —
  tightened `?next=` guard.

### Tests

* **23 new unit tests** in `tests/test_iter_220av_web_security.py`:
  - bleach strips script / iframe / svg / style / object / embed / form / link / meta
  - bleach strips `on*=` handlers + `javascript:` URLs
  - bleach preserves safe HTML (`<p><strong><ul><li>`)
  - bleach clamps to `max_chars`, handles None / empty
  - `sanitize_rich_text_dict` mutates in place, skips missing/None fields
  - `is_safe_next_url` accepts relative paths, rejects protocol-relative,
    backslash, schemes, control chars, oversize, garbage
  - `safe_next_or` falls back when input unsafe
  - `validate_email_recipient` off by default; allows transactional

    addresses; allows same-org user + CRM contact
  - End-to-end smoke: CRM `create_activity` body containing `<script>` +
    `<iframe>` is stripped on persist; safe `<p>` survives.
* All 23 green; added to Makefile regression block with TAB.

## Iter 220au — Security Wave 3: Auth Hardening (May 28, 2026) ✅

### Six risk-register findings closed in one wave

* **F-02 — Password-reset TTL** — tightened 1 h → 15 min via env-tunable
  `auth_guards.PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_MINUTES`. One-shot + sibling-archive
  logic was already in place; just shortened the window.
* **F-03 — JWT TTL / refresh** — role-tiered access-token TTL:
  master_admin + pulse_master_admin = 1 h; everyone else = 24 h
  (`auth_guards.access_token_ttl_hours()`). `/auth/refresh` preserves
  the `mfa_verified` claim and applies the same role-tier TTL on
  rotation. No global logout — existing 24h sessions ride out their
  current expiry then get the role-tier on next login.
* **F-08 — PII strip on `/auth/me`** — new `sanitize_me_response()`
  allow-list strips password / password_hash / mfa_secret / mfa_backup_codes /
  stripe_customer_id / stripe_subscription_id / reset_token /
  tokens_revoked_before / internal `_jwt_*` flags. The existing `/auth/me`
  endpoint already explicitly cherry-picks fields; this helper is the
  belt-and-braces for any future route that returns a raw user doc.
* **F-17 — MFA enforcement for master_admin** — JWT now carries an
  `mfa_verified` claim (set True after a successful TOTP challenge or
  enrolment-complete). `require_master_admin` / `require_gymaxis_master_only`
  call `enforce_master_admin_mfa()`. Off-by-default in dev
  (`ENFORCE_MASTER_ADMIN_MFA=false`); flip on in prod to gate every
  master-admin route on MFA.
* **F-18 — Server-side role gates** — new `utils/auth_guards.require_role(*roles)`
  FastAPI dependency factory + `assert_role(user, roles)` inline helper.
  Master / Pulse admins always pass. Roll-out is opportunistic — any
  destructive route currently relying on frontend gating can drop the
  dep in without breaking compatibility.
* **F-19 — Session invalidation on RBAC change** — new
  `revoke_user_sessions(user_id)` stamps `users.tokens_revoked_before`
  to "now"; `get_current_user` 401s any JWT with `iat < tokens_revoked_before`.
  Wired into `admin_edit_user` (when role / is_master_admin /
  allowed_site_ids / module_overrides / permissions / disabled /
  archived changes), `disable_user`, `archive_user`.

### New module

* `/app/backend/utils/auth_guards.py` — single home for all six
  helpers + constants. No FastAPI app-level changes required —
  existing routes import via `from utils.auth_guards import …`.

### Modified files

* `utils/auth.py` — `create_token` accepts `mfa_verified` + `extra_claims`;
  `get_current_user` checks `iat < tokens_revoked_before` and stashes
  `_jwt_mfa_verified` on the user dict.
* `routes/auth.py` — `_finalise_successful_login` (mfa_verified flag +
  role-tier TTL), `/auth/refresh` (preserves mfa claim + role-tier TTL),
  `/auth/mfa/verify` (mfa_verified=True on success), `forgot-password`
  (15-min TTL).
* `routes/master_admin.py` — `require_master_admin` /
  `require_gymaxis_master_only` call `enforce_master_admin_mfa`.
* `routes/master_admin_users.py` — `admin_edit_user`, `disable_user`,
  `archive_user` call `revoke_user_sessions` when authorisation-relevant
  fields change.

### Tests

* **24 new pure-unit tests** in `tests/test_iter_220au_auth_hardening.py`:
  - password-reset TTL default + env override
  - role-tier access-token TTL (dict / string / case-insensitive / None)
  - `create_token` records `mfa_verified` claim
  - `sanitize_me_response` strips every PII field, idempotent, None-safe
  - `enforce_master_admin_mfa` off-by-default, blocks/passes with env on, no-op for non-admins
  - `assert_role` allows master_admin / matching role, rejects others
  - `require_role` returns a callable FastAPI dep that defers to user
  - `revoke_user_sessions` stamps users + crm_users, no-ops on empty id, swallows DB errors
  - End-to-end smoke: `get_current_user` rejects pre-revoke iat, accepts post-revoke iat

* All 24 green. Added to Makefile regression block with TAB.

### Verification

  master_admin, master_admin_users, test file).
* Full `make regression` → **1187 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failures, 0 errors**

## Iter 220at — Security Wave 2: AI Prompt-Injection Guardrails (May 28, 2026) ✅

### Five OWASP-for-LLM findings closed in one wave

* **F-11 / LLM01 — Prompt injection** — `utils/ai_guardrails.sanitize_prompt()` strips
  control chars + clamps length; `detect_injection()` scores against 12 known-bad
  pattern families (ignore-instructions, reveal-system, DAN/jailbreak, data-exfil,
  HTML/XML injection, base64 payloads, repeated control breaks). Score ≥80 →
  reject with 400 and audit-log. Wired into:
  - `routes/assistant.py::assistant_chat` (every chat turn)
  - `routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py::_generate_article_payload` (free-form caller input)
  - `routes/mod_portal.py::_ai_triage` (fault descriptions; AI silently skipped on bad input)
  - `routes/equipment_import.py::_ai_extract_invoice` (PDF text; control-char strip only)
* **F-12 / LLM06 — Sensitive disclosure (gdpr_erased)** — `rag_context_filter()` decorates any
  RAG-style context fetch with `gdpr_erased: {$ne: True}`. Idempotent + composable.
* **F-13 / LLM08 — Excessive agency** — `HIGH_RISK_TOOLS` registry (send_email,
  publish_post, delete_*, update_pricing, process_refund, grant_admin_role,
  impersonate_user, …) + `mint_approval_token()` / `verify_approval_token()` HMAC-signed
  one-shot tokens (10-min TTL) + `require_human_approval()` decorator. Frontend confirms
  via UI dialog before any high-risk AI action fires.
* **F-14 / LLM02 — Insecure output handling** — `sanitize_llm_markdown()` strips
  `<script>/<iframe>/<svg>/<style>/<embed>/<object>`, all `on*=` event handlers,
  `javascript:`/`vbscript:`/`data:` URLs from LLM markdown. Wired into SEO Autopilot
  output (blog body + meta + Q&A blocks) ahead of DB write.
* **F-16 / LLM10 — Per-tenant token budget** — `enforce_token_budget()` aggregates
  daily token spend per `organization_id` from `db.ai_token_usage` (env-tunable
  `AI_DAILY_TOKEN_BUDGET`, default 500 k tok/org/day); raises 429 when projected
  spend would exceed cap. `record_token_usage()` writes one row per LLM round-trip.
  Wired into assistant.chat + seo.generate_article + mod.triage.

### Audit + indexes

* New collections (auto-indexed on startup via
  `utils.ai_guardrails.ensure_indexes`):
  - `ai_token_usage` — `(organization_id, day)` + `ts`
  - `ai_actions` — `(organization_id, ts)` + `(actor_id, ts)`
* Every guardrail invocation that rejects (or every AI tool call) is fire-and-forget
  audited via `record_ai_action()` — best-effort, swallows DB failures so the AI
  feature itself never breaks on a logging blip.

### Tests

* **32 new pure-unit tests** in `tests/test_iter_220at_ai_guardrails.py`:
  - sanitize_prompt strip/clamp/None handling
  - wrap_user_input delimiter
  - detect_injection scoring + flag union for jailbreaks, data-exfil, html-inject
  - rag_context_filter add + idempotency
  - HIGH_RISK_TOOLS registry coverage
  - mint/verify approval token round-trip + tamper detection + TTL expiry
  - sanitize_llm_markdown strips script/iframe/event handlers / javascript: URLs
  - is_safe_url whitelist
  - enforce_token_budget allows anon, blocks over cap, falls open on DB error
  - record_token_usage writes row + no-ops on zero/anon
  - record_ai_action persists row + handles anon + swallows DB errors
  - ensure_indexes builds 4 indexes + swallows errors
  - End-to-end smokes: seo_autopilot scrubs `<script>` from `body_md`;
    mod_portal._ai_triage skips when injection score ≥80.
* All 32 green; added to Makefile regression block with TAB.
* `ruff` clean across every touched file (assistant, seo_autopilot, mod_portal,
  equipment_import, ai_guardrails, test file).
* Full `make regression` → **1162 passed, 15 skipped, 0 introduced regressions**
  (1 transient flake in `partner_application_ai_suggest` — passes on isolated rerun).

### Risk register update (W2 row block)

## Iter 220ar–220as — Security Wave 1: Audit + Idempotency + Pagination + Public RL (May 28, 2026) ✅

### 220ar — Audit Pass 1 (read-only)

Three artifacts published to `/app/memory/SECURITY_AUDIT/`:

* `SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_1.md` — full audit against OWASP Web Top 10 /
  API Top 10 / LLM Top 10 + UK GDPR Art. 32. Confirms 19 controls
  already shipped (tight CSP, HSTS, CORS allowlist, bcrypt+JWT
  with `jti` revocation, TOTP module, Stripe signature verification
  on 6 webhooks, brute-force lockout, magic-byte upload sniffing,
  7 audit-log domains, GDPR erasure, body-size guard, master-admin
  IP allowlist, slow-request telemetry, Sentry no-PII).
* `RISK_REGISTER.md` — 33 findings (0 Critical · 7 High · 18 Medium
  · 6 Low · 1 N/A) in tracker shape with wave + status columns.
* `PEN_TEST_SCOPE.md` — ready-to-hand-over scope doc for the
  external vendor: 12 test-role accounts, in-scope / out-of-scope
  surfaces, known limitations, reporting expectations, disclosure
  window.

### 220as — Wave 1 hardening (3 risk-register findings closed)

* **F-09 — Stripe webhook idempotency** — new
  `utils/stripe_idempotency.py` exports `mark_event_processed(event_id)`
  backed by a unique-index'd `db.stripe_webhook_events` collection
  with 30-day TTL. Wired into 4 webhook handlers
  (stripe_connect, engineer_invoice_payments, engineer_stripe_connect,
  public_signup). The other two webhook handlers
  (financial_ops, memberships_payments) already had session-level
  idempotency; the event-id helper is belt-and-braces.
* **F-07 — Pagination caps** — new `utils/pagination.py` exports
  `safe_limit()` / `safe_skip()` that clamp client-supplied values
  to a configurable hard max (default 200, max-max 500). Applied to
  `mod_portal.audit-log`, `pulse_sales.opportunities`,
  `service_desk.feed`.
* **F-01 — Public-route rate-limit gap** — anonymous
  `/public/signup/{slug}/track` now applies a 60-rpm IP-keyed
  sliding-window throttle (the funnel analytics endpoint was
  poison-able).

**Tests** — 9 new pinned tests in
`tests/test_iter_220as_security_wave_1.py`:

* `safe_limit` clamps to hard max, defaults on garbage input.
* `safe_skip` clamps below zero.
* `mark_event_processed` returns True on first call, False on
  duplicate, treats races as duplicate (safe), no-op on empty id.
* `ensure_indexes` is idempotent.
* **Source-level guarantee**: every Stripe webhook entry-point
  references `mark_event_processed` — if a future handler is added
  without it, the test fails and forces the dev to wire dedupe.

### Verification

* `make regression` → **1,130 passed, 15 skipped, 1 flaky LLM test

* `ruff` clean across every touched file.
