## Iter 220aq — Production bug-fix triplet: Growth Hub deep-links, pipeline scoping, SEO domain (May 28, 2026) ✅

User reported three production bugs from gymaxisai.com:

### 1) Growth Hub "Open ..." buttons → blank screen

Root cause: ``jump(sectionId)`` called ``setSection(deep_link)`` where
the deep_link IDs ``crm-deals``, ``crm-analytics``, ``crm-companies``
had no corresponding ``case`` in ``MasterAdminPage`` — the content
area silently rendered nothing. The CRM doesn't live under Master
Admin (it's a separate portal at ``/crm``).

Fix in ``pages/MasterAdmin/GymAxisGrowthHub.js``:
* New ``CRM_TAB_MAP`` translates CRM deep_links to ``/crm?tab=<x>``
  URL navigations (``crm-deals → pipeline``, ``crm-companies →
  companies``, ``crm-contacts → contacts``, ``crm-analytics →
  pipeline``).
* Hard-coded ``crm-analytics`` on the CRM card replaced with
  ``crm-deals`` so the deep_link matches both backend + frontend
  expectations.

Fix in ``pages/CRM/CRMApp.js``:
* ``activeTab`` now lazy-reads ``?tab=<id>`` from
  ``window.location.search`` synchronously on first render so the
  Master Admin deep-link lands on the right inner tab. We leave the
  query param in the URL on purpose — stripping it in a useEffect
  raced React 18 StrictMode's dev-only double-mount and wiped the
  requested tab on the second pass.

### 2) Pipeline £ showed £50,000 (cross-tenant data leak)

Root cause: ``GET /api/master-admin/growth-hub/overview`` was
summing ALL tenants' ``crm_deals`` globally — any £50k deal in any
customer's CRM bled into the master-admin self-promo Growth Hub.

Fix in ``routes/master_admin_growth_hub.py``:
* Both the overview AND the sparklines endpoints now scope every
  pipeline read to the **master-admin org** via
  ``_master_admin_org_id``.
* Union ``crm_deals`` + ``crm2_opportunities`` (v2 CRM portal
  writes only to the latter; v1 demo-request landing page still
  writes to the former). So ``pipeline_value_gbp``,
  ``deals_open``, ``deals_won_30d``, ``deals_lost_30d``,
  ``companies_total`` and the ``deals_created`` 30-day sparkline
  all return correct master-admin-org-only data.

### 3) SEO Autopilot used wrong domain (``gymaxis.io``)

Root cause: the article-generation prompt mentioned ``/demo`` as a
relative path; the LLM filled in the brand domain itself and
sometimes invented ``gymaxis.io``.

Fix in ``routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py``:
* ``DEFAULT_BRAND_BLURB`` now hard-codes the canonical domain
  ``gymaxisai.com`` and explicitly forbids the LLM from inventing
  alternates.
* The article prompt's CTA line now embeds the absolute URL
  ``https://gymaxisai.com/demo-request`` and explicitly lists
  the bad domains to avoid.
* New ``_scrub_brand_domain`` safety net rewrites any leak of
  ``gymaxis.io / gym-axis.com / gymaxis.co.uk / gymaxis.net /
  gymaxis.app / gymaxis.co / gym-axis.io`` to the canonical
  ``https://gymaxisai.com``. Applied to every article field
  (``title``, ``excerpt``, ``body_md``, ``meta_description``,
  ``qa_blocks``) AND every distribution snippet (LinkedIn posts, X
  thread tweets, Reddit title + body).
* Production retro-fix script (not committed; run once after
  redeploy) provided to scrub any existing bad-domain articles.

### Tests

* 8 new pinned tests in
  ``backend/tests/test_iter_220aq_growth_hub_fixes.py`` covering:
  - domain scrub for ``gymaxis.io`` + 6 other variants
  - canonical domain preservation (no double-rewrites)
  - None / empty input handling
  - collapsed double-protocol URLs
  - master-admin org scoping on pipeline value
  - union of crm_deals + crm2_opportunities counts
  - sparkline deal buckets scoped to master-admin org
* Existing fixtures in ``test_iter_220ag_growth_hub.py`` +
  ``test_iter_220aj_growth_sparklines.py`` patched to add
  ``users`` + ``organizations.find_one`` + ``crm2_opportunities``
  mocks so they survive the new master-admin-org resolver path.

### Verification

* ``make regression`` → **1122 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** in 135 s.
* ``ruff`` / ``eslint`` clean on every touched file.
* Live smoke from Master Admin Growth Hub → "Open CRM" button now
  routes to ``/crm?tab=pipeline`` and lands on the live Pipeline
  view with 3 lead deals (£12k each, £36k total). Pipeline £ tile
  on the Growth Hub now reads **£36,000** in preview (the real
  master-admin-org figure), confirming the cross-tenant leak is
  closed.

> **Production redeploy required** — user's redeploy step will
> push these fixes to gymaxisai.com. The ``gymaxis.io`` article
> already published in prod needs a manual regenerate (or run the
> ``_scrub_brand_domain`` retro-script against the prod DB).

## Iter 220ao — GDPR Article 17 · Right-to-Erasure Workflow (May 27, 2026) ✅

Closes the long-standing P2 compliance gap: the platform now has a
fully-pinned **Data Subject Erasure Request** workflow for the three
PII-bearing record types — gym members, instructors and CRM contacts.
Anonymises PII in place (Art. 17(3)(b) — invoices/bookings survive),
master-admin-gated, with a 30-day ICO-aligned cooling-off window.

**Backend — new `routes/gdpr_erasure.py`** (prefix `/api/gdpr/erasure`)

* `POST /preview` — returns `{label, already_erased, plan, retains}`
  without touching the DB. `plan` shows current PII → planned post-
  scrub value per field. Used by the create-request modal.
* `POST /requests` — files a pending request, stamps a 30-day
  `execute_after`. 409s on duplicate pending for the same subject;
  400s if the subject is already erased.
* `GET  /requests` — paginated list with `status` + `subject_type`
  filters.
* `GET  /requests/{id}` — refreshes the plan against the live row
  in case PII was edited between create + execute.
* `POST /requests/{id}/execute` — performs the in-place anonymisation
  (`first_name`/`last_name` → `[REDACTED]`, `email` →
  `erased+{sha8}@gdpr.local`, phone/dob/address/postcode/notes →
  `None`). Stamps `gdpr_erased`, `gdpr_erased_at`, `gdpr_erased_by`,
  `gdpr_erasure_request_id`. Refuses to fire before
  `execute_after` unless `force=true` (operator fast-track when the
  data subject explicitly requests immediate action).
* `POST /requests/{id}/cancel` — cancels a pending request.
* Every endpoint is `_require_master_admin` gated.

Subject specs (`_SUBJECT_SPEC`):
  - `member` → `db.members` — hashable `email`; redact names; clear
    phone, dob, addresses, emergency contacts, notes, photo_url.
  - `instructor` → `db.membership_instructors` — same shape +
    headline/bio/specialties/photo_url.
  - `crm_contact` → `db.crm2_contacts` — hashable email; redact
    names; clear phone, dob, addresses, job_title, notes, socials.

**Frontend** — new shared
`components/GDPR/GdprErasurePanel.js` (lazy-loaded)

* Hero banner explaining policy + 30-day window.
* Status filter strip (`All / Pending / Executed / Cancelled`).
* Per-row icons (clock for pending, check for executed) + subject-
  type + status badges.
* **New Erasure Request modal** — Subject Type dropdown, Subject Id
  input, **Preview** button that surfaces the scrub plan inline,
  optional reason field, and a 30-day-window warning.
* **Detail modal** — shows status/timestamps/reason, refreshed
  plan, scrub_summary (post-execution), and the right action set
  given current state. Master Admin can **Force execute (skip
  cooling-off)** while pending, **Execute now** once the cooling
  window has elapsed, or **Cancel request**.
* Mounted in **two** surfaces (user-confirmed scope):
  - **Master Admin → Settings & Compliance → Data Subject
    Erasure** (new sub-tab in `SidebarConfig.js`).
  - **CRM Settings → Privacy & GDPR** (new section in
    `CRMSettings.js`).

**Tests** —
`backend/tests/test_iter_220ao_gdpr_erasure.py` (16 tests, all
green) pinned and registered in `Makefile`.

**Verification**

* `make regression` → **1107 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** in
  146 s.
* `ruff` / `eslint` clean on every touched file (no new warnings
  vs. main).
* Live smoke confirmed: the hero panel renders inside
  `/master-admin?section=gdpr-erasure`, the empty list shows the
  empty state, and the New Erasure Request modal opens with all
  three subject types, ID input, Preview button and Reason field.

## Iter 220al — CRM Contacts · Enrol in journey quick-action (May 27, 2026) ✅

Closes the last gap in the GymAxis self-promo funnel: the 4 launched
B2B journeys (Iter 220ah) are now fireable from any CRM contact
detail in **one click** — without leaving the rep's inbox or the
master admin having to drive every enrolment manually.

**Backend — new `routes/crm_journey_enrol.py`.**

* `GET /api/crm/contacts/{id}/journey-options` (CRM-auth scoped).
  Returns the org's non-archived `marketing_journeys` with per-row
  `already_enrolled` flag and node count. Looks up the contact in
  **both** `crm2_contacts` (v2 schema the UI uses) and the legacy
  `crm_contacts` (where the public demo-request endpoint writes).
  Returns `{journeys: [], non_crm_contact: true}` instead of 404
  when the row is a non-CRM contact (e.g. member-portal user
  rendered by the same list) so the UI can silently hide the button.
* `POST /api/crm/contacts/{id}/enrol` — accepts `{journey_id}`.
    - Idempotent: 409 on duplicate active enrolment.
    - Cross-tenant safe: 404 when journey or contact belongs to a
      different org.
    - Inserts a `marketing_journey_enrolments` row with
      `source: "crm-contact-enrol"` + `enrolled_by` user id.
    - Stamps a `journey_enrolled` activity on the contact's timeline,
      writing to `crm2_activities` when the contact is v2 and
      `crm_activities` when it's legacy.
    - Increments `metrics.entered` on the journey row so the Growth
      Hub journey cards update live without rebuilding stats from
      scratch.

**Frontend — `pages/CRM/CRMContacts.js`.**

* New `EnrolJourneyButton` component in the ContactDetail action row.
  Pre-loads the org's journey options once per detail mount; silently
  hides for non-CRM contacts or empty orgs.
* On click, opens a modal showing each journey with description,
  step count, current enrolment count + a green "Enrolled" pill or
  purple "Enrol" launch button. Refresh after enrolment flips the
  badge live without page reload.
* Note: the CRM `headers` is a function (`headers()`) not a value —
  fixed the call sites to invoke it. Also dropped the leading `/api/`
  from URLs since CRMApp's `API` constant already includes it (this
  is what caused the initial 404s during smoke testing).

**Tests — `tests/test_iter_220al_crm_journey_enrol.py`.** 8 new
isolated unit tests:
  * Soft lookup for non-CRM contact (no 404, flag set).
  * Happy-path option list with per-row `already_enrolled`.
  * Enrol writes enrolment + activity (v2 path).
  * **New**: Legacy contact path writes to `crm_activities` instead.
  * 409 on duplicate enrolment (no double-charge of metrics).
  * 404 when journey or contact belongs to other org × 2.
  * Router exposes both endpoints.
* Wired into `make regression` which now stands at **1073 passed,
  15 skipped** (was 1065).

**Live verification.** Browser screenshot shows the "Enrol in journey"
button rendering on the Biz Test contact detail with the
"Trial day 1/7/13 → paid" template visible in the dialog
("3 STEPS · 1 ENROLLED"). Curl-verified the full round-trip
(list → enrol → 409 on re-enrol → metrics.entered bumped to 1).

**Quality gates.** `make lint-python` ✅, `make lint-frontend` ✅,
`make regression` ✅ (126 s).

## Iter 220ak — Public Demo Request landing + inbound feed (May 27, 2026) ✅

Closes the inbound funnel loop: SEO Autopilot publishes blog →
visitor lands → `/demo-request` form → CRM lead + alert + journey
enrolment. Without this, the SEO traffic dead-ended at "read article".

**Backend — new `routes/public_demo_request.py`.**

* `POST /api/public/demo-request` (no auth) — single endpoint that:
    - Validates name (regex-checked, rejects all-numeric / symbol-
      only), work email, company, site_count (1–999), message
      (≤2000 chars).
    - **Honeypot**: if the hidden `website` field is populated, returns
      `{ok:true, queued:true, receipt_id: <fake-uuid>}` and writes
      **nothing** — bots can't detect the rejection.
    - **Rate-limit**: 5 submits / IP / hour using a dedicated
      `demo-request:<ip>` key (isolated from the global per-IP
      buckets).
    - Inserts a contact (`crm_contacts`, tagged `inbound-demo-request`,
      lead score 50), a deal in stage `lead` (`crm_deals`, source
      tagged), an activity row (`crm_activities` type
      `demo_requested`), and a Growth Hub alert (`growth_alerts`).
    - Auto-enrols the contact into the `cold-to-demo` B2B journey
      (Iter 220ah) if launched. Enrolment failure is logged but
      non-fatal — never blocks lead capture.
    - Sends an email notification to the sales inbox (best-effort).
    - Returns a stable receipt id (the deal id) for the SPA to show.
* UTM passthrough (`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`)
  captured into the contact row for attribution.

**Growth Hub alerts — `routes/master_admin_growth_hub.py`.**

* `GET /api/master-admin/growth/alerts` — last 25 alerts + `unread`
  counter.
* `POST /api/master-admin/growth/alerts/mark-read` — bulk clears the
  unread badge.

**Frontend — new `pages/DemoRequestPage.js`.**

* Public route `/demo-request` — two-column hero (social-proof bullets
  left, form right) with brand gradient. Hidden honeypot field, UTM
  capture from query params, inline validation. Success state shows
  the receipt id + return-to-site CTA.
* Marketing footer (`MarketingShell.js`) gets a new "Book a demo" link.

**Growth Hub UI — `pages/MasterAdmin/GymAxisGrowthHub.js`.**

* New amber **"New inbound demo requests"** banner with unread pill,
  per-alert bell rows ("New demo request · Company"), per-row
  "Open deal" deep-link to the CRM, and "Mark all read" bulk button.
  Hidden when there are no alerts.

**Tests — `tests/test_iter_220ak_public_demo_request.py`.** 11 new
isolated unit tests:
  * Honeypot rejects + returns fake receipt + zero writes.
  * Happy path writes contact + deal + activity + alert + enrolment.
  * Skip enrolment when journey not launched.
  * 422 for all-numeric / symbol-only names.
  * 429 after 5 same-IP submits within the window.
  * Growth alerts list — master-admin gating, payload shape.
  * Mark-read — master-admin gating, $set write shape.
  * Name splitter handles single-word + multi-space cases.
  * Router exposes `/public/demo-request`.

* Wired into `make regression` which now stands at **1065 passed,
  15 skipped** (was 1054).

**Live verification.** Two POSTs to the preview endpoint:
  * Real submit → `{ok:true, queued:false, receipt_id:<uuid>}`. CRM
    deal + alert visible in the Hub. Pipeline £ tile flipped to
    "1 new in 30d".
  * Honeypot submit → `{ok:true, queued:true}`, zero DB writes.
  * Growth alerts endpoint returns `unread: 1` with the new row.
  * Browser screenshot: Hub banner rendering with the amber unread

  during a Mongo blip.

  * Blog-view series carries the last known value forward across

  * `_bucket_dates` exact contract (30 chronological ISO strings,

  * Skips rows with missing / `None` date fields.

  15 skipped** (was 1046).

## Iter 220ag — GymAxis Growth Hub (de-duplicated self-promo surface) (May 27, 2026) ✅

**Problem.** Master Admin → Growth → "Marketing Studio" embedded the
operator-facing `MarketingSuite` ("Fill empty classes", "Re-engage
inactive members" etc.) — completely wrong context for marketing
GymAxis as a B2B SaaS. Also worth noting: standing up a separate
"Pipeline / Prospects / Outbound" stack would have duplicated the
existing **CRM**, **Trials**, **Outbound Emails**, **Sales Insights**
and **SEO Autopilot** modules that already live in Master Admin.

**Solution.** Replace the operator-suite embed with a brand-new
**GymAxisGrowthHub** that is a pure *aggregation surface* — every
metric is read live from existing collections, and every drill-down
deep-links into the existing module rather than re-implementing it.

**Backend — new `routes/master_admin_growth_hub.py`.**

* `GET /api/master-admin/growth/overview` (master-admin gated).
  Returns 5 module groups in one payload:
    - `trials` — active + 30-day conversions (reads from
      `organizations` mirroring `master_admin_trials`).

      `metrics.views` across published posts (from `seo_articles`,
      `seo_keywords`, `seo_autopilot_runs`).
    - `outbound` — sent / failed counts (30d) from `email_send_events`.
    - `pipeline` — open / won / lost deals (30d) + summed open
      pipeline £ + total CRM companies.
    - `sales_insights` — public-site chat sessions / messages (30d).
  Every group includes a `deep_link` string matching the sidebar
  section id so the UI knows exactly where to jump.
* All counters fail-safe to `0` (never `None`) via `_safe_count`
  helper — protects the React tiles from a Mongo index hiccup
  during deploys.

**Frontend — new `pages/MasterAdmin/GymAxisGrowthHub.js`.**

* Hero card naming the surface "GymAxis Growth Hub" — purpose-built
  copy ("How we're marketing GymAxis to fitness operators · pulls
  live numbers from Trials, SEO Autopilot, Outbound Emails, CRM
  Pipeline and Sales Insights — no module is rebuilt here").
* 5-tile KPI band (Active trials · Blog views · Emails 30d · Pipeline £ · Site chats 30d).
* 6 funnel cards with stat-grid + 1-click "Open …" deep-link buttons
  that invoke the parent `setSection` to jump to the existing
  Trials / SEO Autopilot / Outbound emails / CRM / Sales Insights
  panels — zero new CRUD UI.
* B2B journey templates section (Cold-to-demo · Demo-booked · Trial
  conversion · Lost-deal revival) — preset preview only; the
  underlying runner stays in Marketing → Journeys.
* Old `GrowthStudio.js` deleted; sidebar label renamed
  "Marketing Studio" → "Growth Hub" with a clearer description.

**Tests — `tests/test_iter_220ag_growth_hub.py`.** 10 new isolated
unit tests (master-admin gating, shape contract, deep-link id
constants, ISO + datetime trial-conversion comparison, blog-view
summing, pipeline-value summing with bad-string tolerance, as_of
timestamp, resilient empty-state behaviour). All green in 4 s.
Wired into `make regression` which now stands at **1023 passed,
15 skipped** (was 1013).

**Live verification.** Curl on the preview backend returned a real

## Iter 220v — Incidents Phase 4 — AI assistance + Whisper voice-to-text (May 27, 2026) ✅

Phase 4 closes out the original RIDDOR brief. Three AI helpers and a
voice-to-text dictation flow turn the incident form from a typing
exercise into a 30-second field report.

**Backend — new `utils/incident_ai.py`.**

* `summarise_incident(incident)` — Claude Sonnet 4.5 via the
  Emergent LLM key. Returns a 2–3 sentence management briefing
  (plain UK English, no jargon, no speculation).
* `suggest_root_causes(incident)` — returns up to 3 keys drawn
  **strictly from the canonical `ROOT_CAUSE_KEYS` enum**. Server-side
  validation drops anything the model hallucinated outside the enum
  so the chips can be pre-selected safely in the Investigation pane.
* `hint_riddor_qualification(incident)` — pre-fills the RIDDOR
  wizard with Yes/No/Don't-know answers. Conservative by design:
  ambiguous descriptions return `null` (don't-know) so a human is
  still forced to confirm. Returns `{answers: {key: bool|None},
  reasoning: str}`.
* `transcribe_audio(file_obj)` — Whisper-1 wrapper via
  `emergentintegrations.llm.openai.OpenAISpeechToText`. Handles
  both string and object return types from the library.
* All helpers return `None` on any failure (network, parse,
  rate-limit) so the calling endpoint can degrade gracefully —
  AI is a nice-to-have, never a hard dependency.

**Backend — new endpoints in `routes/incidents.py`.**

* `POST /incidents/{id}/ai/summarise` — manager+ only.
* `POST /incidents/{id}/ai/root-causes` — manager+ only.
* `POST /incidents/{id}/ai/riddor-hint` — manager+ only.
  **Strictly advisory** — does NOT mutate the incident's RIDDOR
  status. The wizard still has to be run by a human.
* `POST /incidents/ai/transcribe` — multipart upload, ≤25 MB,
  returns plain transcript. Caller decides whether to drop it into
  the description textarea or discard.
* All AI endpoints return 503 (not 500) when the LLM is unavailable
  so the UI can show a friendly "try again or write manually"
  message instead of a crash banner.

**Frontend — additions to `pages/IncidentsTab.js`.**

* **Voice dictate button** on the Quick-Log description field
  (`VoiceDictate` component): start → records via `MediaRecorder`
  with `audio/webm` mime → stop → uploads to
  `/incidents/ai/transcribe` → appends transcript to the textarea.
  Microphone permission requested on demand; clear visual states
  (idle / recording / uploading), red pulsing while recording.
* **"Pre-fill with AI" CTA** on the RIDDOR wizard tab. Pulls the
  hint, updates the local Yes/No/Don't-know state for every
  question the AI gave an answer for, and surfaces the model's
  one-line reasoning in a blue advisory panel below the
  "Run RIDDOR assessment" button.
* **"AI suggest" button** beside the Investigation root-cause
  chips. Merges suggested causes into the existing selection so
  the human can still curate before saving.
* **"AI summarise" button** beside the Investigator findings
  textarea. Appends a separated "— AI summary —" block so the
  investigator can see what the AI inferred without overwriting
  their own notes.
* All AI buttons share the navy `Sparkles` lucide icon for a
  consistent visual cue.

**Tests (`tests/test_iter_220s_incidents_riddor.py` → 38 total).**

Four new Phase 4 tests:

## Iter 220u — Incidents Phase 3 — Repeat detection · Trends · Heatmap · Expanded filters (May 27, 2026) ✅

The Phase 1 + 2 incident system was reactive — record what happened,
file the paperwork. Phase 3 makes it **proactive**: surface assets
that are quietly racking up incidents *before* the CAPEX justification
becomes obvious, show when on the clock incidents cluster, and let
operators slice the data by date + category.

**Backend — additions to `routes/incidents.py`.**

* `GET /incidents/hse/repeat-detection?window_days=N&threshold=K`
  — manager-only. Aggregates incidents by `asset_id` over the
  window, scores each (count × severity-weighted), joins to
  `db.equipment` for friendly name + existing `capex.status`. Returns
  the top 50 ranked by severity score then count. Each row carries
  `capex_already_flagged` so the UI can show "CAPEX flagged" vs
  "CAPEX recommended" badges.
* `GET /incidents/hse/heatmap?days=N` — 7×24 grid of incident
  counts (day-of-week × hour-of-day) plus a parallel
  `grid_severity_score` for future "where do the *worst* incidents
  cluster" heat-maps. Returns day labels in Mon→Sun order.
* `_refresh_asset_incident_flag(asset_id, organization_id)` — pure
  helper invoked **synchronously** from the incident-create hook.
  Recomputes the 90-day rollup for the touched asset and writes a
  tiny `incident_flag` document onto `db.equipment` containing
  `count_90d`, `severity_score`, `last_incident_at`,
  `last_incident_ref`, `capex_recommended`, `updated_at`. Means the
  CAPEX UI sees the flag the moment the 3rd incident lands —
  no nightly sweep needed.
* List endpoint extended with three new query params:
  - `date_from` / `date_to` (ISO date or datetime — filters on
    `occurred_at` so users can drill into a specific incident week).
  - `category` (comma-separated for multi-select; validated against
    the public CATEGORIES enum).

**Frontend — additions to `pages/IncidentsTab.js`.**

* **Trend sparkline** (`TrendSparkline`) — incidents-per-day mini bar
  chart at the top of the HSE dashboard. Uses the existing `by_day`
  array from the dashboard endpoint, gradient bars (navy→purple)
  matching the brand palette.
* **Risk hot-list panel** — red-tinted card listing assets at the
  repeat threshold with their count, severity score, and a badge
  showing whether CAPEX is already flagged or only recommended.
* **Heatmap** (`Heatmap`) — pure-CSS day-of-week × hour grid,
  navy→red intensity scale, hover tooltips. Mobile-scrollable via
  `overflow-x-auto`.
* **Expanded filters** — date_from / date_to inputs above the
  existing search box; filter pills + category multi via the
  CSV-aware backend.

**Headline updated**: the HSE dashboard subtitle now reads
"`N incidents · M RIDDOR · K fatalities · P asset(s) at
repeat-incident threshold`" — the last fragment links the operator's
eye directly to the new hot-list.

**Tests (`tests/test_iter_220s_incidents_riddor.py` → 34 total).**

Six new Phase 3 tests:
* `hse_heatmap_returns_7x24_grid` — shape + labels invariant.
* `repeat_detection_returns_rollup` — shape + flagged-list contract.
* `repeat_detection_flags_asset_after_three_incidents` — creates
  3 incidents on a fresh asset and verifies they hit the rollup at
  threshold=3 with the right count + severity score.
* `list_filters_by_date_range` — `date_from` / `date_to` constrain
  by `occurred_at`; out-of-range queries don't return in-range rows.
* `list_filters_by_category_csv` — single + CSV multi-select gates.
* `equipment_incident_flag_persists_after_third_incident` — direct
  PyMongo read of `db.equipment[asset_id].incident_flag` after a
  3-incident sequence; confirms `count_90d ≥ 3`,
  `capex_recommended=True`, `severity_score` populated.

**End-to-end smoke** confirms the dashboard now reports
"4 asset(s) at repeat-incident threshold" in the headline (real
data from the asset-flag tests above), the incidents-per-day
sparkline renders, and the hot-list + heatmap panels appear below
the four bar-chart panels.

**Regression.** `make regression` reports **915 passed, 15 skipped**
(was 909). Lint clean (backend + frontend).


## Iter 220t — Incidents Phase 2 — PDFs · Signatures · Witness workflow · HSE dashboard (May 27, 2026) ✅

Ships the legally-defensible artefacts on top of the Phase 1
foundation: six branded PDFs, digital signature capture (typed +
drawn), a token-based witness statement workflow that a witness can
fill in from their phone without any GymAxis login, and an HSE
dashboard v1 with severity / kind / category / top-asset bar charts.

**Backend — new files.**

* `utils/incident_pdf.py` — branded PDF generators built on ReportLab.
  Shared header / footer / theming module so all six PDFs feel like
  one product:
  - `accident_report_pdf` — full incident detail with status pills,
    description, injured-party block, witnesses, corrective actions,
    signature block at the foot.

## Iter 220s — Unified Accident, Near-Miss, Hazard, RIDDOR module — Phase 1 (May 27, 2026) ✅ enterprise-grade foundation

Built the **enterprise H&S incident management foundation** the user
asked for — one source of truth across all tenant profiles (gym /
leisure / council / university / MOD / hotel / school / studio /
service engineer). Phase 1 ships the full backend + a complete,
mobile-first frontend control surface. Phases 2–4 build on top.

**Backend — new files.**

* `utils/riddor.py` — pure decision engine for the UK HSE RIDDOR 2013
  regulations. 9-question wizard (2 context gates + 7 qualifying
  triggers). Conservative on unknowns (any ``None`` answer escalates
  to ``potential`` for human review). Maps to the correct HSE form
  (``F2508`` / ``F2508A`` / ``F2508G``) and statutory deadline
  (10 / 14 / 15 days). Public ``WIZARD_QUESTIONS`` constant drives
  the frontend declaratively so the legal wording lives in one place.

* `routes/incidents.py` — unified module covering accident /
  near-miss / hazard / dangerous-occurrence with strict typed
  payloads (Pydantic). Endpoints:
  - `GET /incidents/picklists` — static enums + RIDDOR questions.
  - `POST /incidents` — full create (typed) with severity
    auto-escalation on serious/major/fatal.
  - `POST /incidents/quick` — mobile-first thin-payload create.
  - `GET /incidents` — list with filter (kind/severity/RIDDOR
    status/asset/free-text), RBAC-scoped.
  - `GET /incidents/{id}` — 360° bundle (incident + actions + audit).
  - `PATCH /incidents/{id}` — partial update (manager only).
  - `POST /incidents/{id}/status` — status transitions w/ sign-off.
  - `POST /incidents/{id}/riddor/assess` — runs the engine, persists
    verdict, auto-escalates status on Potential/Confirmed, fires
    escalation email.
  - `POST /incidents/{id}/riddor/submit` — records HSE submission ref.
  - `POST /incidents/{id}/investigation` — upsert with auto status
    transitions (`reported → investigating → actions_pending`).
  - `POST /incidents/{id}/actions` — add corrective action.
  - `PATCH /incidents/{id}/actions/{aid}` — update / complete.
  - `GET /incidents/stats/summary` — dashboard tiles.
* Reference numbering: per-org counter (`db.counters`) → `IR-YYYY-NNNNN`.
* Immutable audit log (`db.incident_audit_log`) — every state
  mutation writes a row (created / status_changed / riddor_assessed /
  riddor_submitted / investigation_started / investigation_completed
  / action_added / action_updated). Never updated, never deleted.
* RBAC: master_admin → all orgs; owner/admin/manager/hse_lead →
  org-wide; staff/engineer → own submissions only. Edit / close /
  RIDDOR-assess gated to manager+.
* Escalation: Serious/Major/Fatal + Potential/Confirmed RIDDOR fire
  an HTML email to `hs_officer_email` (with sensible fallbacks).
  Best-effort — never blocks the API.
* Existing-collection re-use: `asset_id`, `service_case_id`,
  `related_issue_id` link to existing assets / svc / issues so
  Phase 3 dashboards can surface repeat-incident analytics.
* MOD tenant profile preserved (`tenant_profile: 'mod'` field on the
  payload) so the existing `mod_incidents.py` can graduate to this
  unified module in a follow-up without data migration.
* Indexes ensured on startup: `(organization_id, created_at)`,
  `(id)` unique, `reference`, `status`, `severity`, `riddor.status`,
  `asset_id`, action `(incident_id)`, action `(organization_id,
  status)`, action `due_date`, audit `(incident_id, at)`.

**Frontend — `pages/IncidentsTab.js`.**

* Mounted as a new **"H&S Incidents"** sub-tab inside Reports for
  both portals — GymAxis (`Dashboard/ReportsSection.js`) and Pulse
  Pro (`PulseReportsTab.js`).
* Stats strip (Total / Open / Potential RIDDOR / Confirmed RIDDOR)
  with severity-toned cards.
* Filter pills (kind + RIDDOR status) and free-text search.
* List view with severity dot, kind/severity/RIDDOR badges,
  reference number, category, location, occurred-at.
* **Quick-Log** dialog — kind / severity / category / description /
  location. Submits to `/incidents` and opens the detail dialog
  inline.
* **Detail dialog** with 5 tabs:
  - **Overview** — description block + key facts grid + witnesses.
  - **RIDDOR Wizard** — every question with Yes/No/Don't-know
    chip-buttons + help text + statutory deadline display +
    HSE submission ref capture.
  - **Investigation** — findings textarea + multi-select root-cause
    chips + Save / Save-and-close.
  - **Actions** — corrective action board (priority, due date,
    one-click "Mark done").
  - **Audit** — append-only timeline, every event timestamped + user
    + role.
* Every interactive element has a `data-testid`. Responsive — tested
  at 1440×900 and works on mobile widths.

**Tests — `tests/test_iter_220s_incidents_riddor.py` (18 tests, all green).**

* 9 RIDDOR engine unit tests (no answers / context gate / each
  qualifying question / multi-trigger tightest-deadline / unknown
  branch / wizard schema pin).
* 9 HTTP integration tests against the live preview backend
  (picklists / create / serious-auto-escalation / RIDDOR assess /
  investigation + actions workflow / quick-log / stats / payload
  validation).

**End-to-end frontend smoke** — standalone Playwright script logs in
as `craig.henshall@pulsefitness.com`, opens Reports → H&S Incidents,
quick-logs an incident, runs the RIDDOR wizard with Yes-Yes flow,
clicks through all 5 detail tabs. Screenshot analysed and confirmed
professional/clean rendering with the RIDDOR-confirmed banner +
audit trail. Saved at `/tmp/incidents_smoke.png`.

**Regression.** `make regression` reports **899 passed, 15 skipped**
(was 881). Lint clean across all touched files. Frontend lint also
clean.

**What ships next (Phases 2–4).**

* Phase 2: Branded PDF exports · digital signatures · witness
  statement workflow with token-based external signing · HSE
  dashboard v1.
* Phase 3: HSE compliance dashboard with trend charts +
  repeat-incident detection + CAPEX trigger.
* Phase 4: AI summarisation / root-cause suggestion / RIDDOR
  qualification hint · voice-to-text (Whisper).


## Iter 220r-2 — "Who covered for me" thanks workflow (May 27, 2026) ✅ enhancement

Extends iter 220r so the welcome-back digest doesn't just tell the
engineer what's waiting — it also recaps what happened at each of
their **referred gyms** while they were off, and lets them send a
courtesy thanks to those gyms in a single click. Real network effect,
zero ambient guilt.

**Backend — `utils/partner_return_digest.py`.**

* New `_while_away_activity(partner, leave_start, leave_end)` joins
  the engineer's referred gyms (`db.suppliers` where
  `partner_engineer_id == partner.id`) to `db.issues` and counts
  faults opened + resolved per gym during the leave window. Quiet
  gyms (0 + 0) are filtered out — never thank a silent gym. Loudest
  first so the busiest gym sits at the top of the recap.
* New `_mint_thanks_token(partner_id, organization_id, gym_name,
  engineer_name, engineer_email)` persists a 60-day single-use token
  in `db.partner_welcome_thanks_tokens`. Idempotent: if an unused,
  unexpired token already exists for `(partner, gym)` we reuse it,
  so a re-sent digest never fans out duplicates.
* Sweep passes `recent_activity=[…]` into `send_welcome_back_digest`.

**Email — `_while_away_block` in `partner_emails.py`.**

* Renders a soft-grey "WHILE YOU WERE AWAY" panel inside the digest.
* Per gym: gym name + a humanised activity line (e.g. "2 new faults
  · 1 fault resolved") + a `Send thanks →` link wired to the
  tokenised URL.
* Capped at 6 gyms to keep the email scannable on mobile. A tiny
  reassurance footer: "One-click thanks goes to the gym's primary
  contact. We keep your name on it — no surprises."

**Backend — `GET /api/partners/welcome-back/thanks/{token}` in `routes/partners.py`.**

* No auth headers — the token is the auth. Single-use, 60-day
  expiry, validated against `db.partner_welcome_thanks_tokens`.
* Resolves the gym's primary contact via
  `primary_contact_email` / `admin_email` / `owner_email` (same
  precedence as archive_lifecycle).
* Sends a co-branded "thanks from your engineer" email to the
  contact, naming the engineer.
* Flips `used_at` + writes an `outcome` audit field
  (`sent` / `no-recipient` / `send-failed` / `org-missing`).
* Returns a small inline confirmation HTML page (gradient checkmark
  card) — keeps the engineer in their email client instead of
  bouncing them through the SPA. Friendly fallback copy for missing
  contact / org-archived / expired-link states.

**Tests (`tests/test_iter_220r_welcome_back_digest.py` → 18 total now).**

* Sweep surfaces per-gym activity + mints token (recap data + token
  body + 60-day expiry).
* Sweep skips quiet gyms (no insert, empty recap).
* Sweep reuses existing unused token instead of re-minting.
* Email body includes per-gym thanks button + gym name + activity
  copy + token URL.
* Thanks endpoint: fires email on happy path, flips `used_at`,
  records `outcome=sent`.
* Thanks endpoint: 404 for unknown token, 410 for expired token,
  200 + idempotent "Already sent" for used token, 200 + no-contact
  copy when gym has no admin email.

**Regression.** `make regression` now reports **881 passed, 15
skipped** (was 872 before this iter). Lint clean across all four
touched files. No frontend changes — the entire workflow lives in
the email + the backend endpoint, keeping the deploy surface tiny.


## Iter 220r — Return-day welcome-back digest (May 27, 2026) ✅ user-requested

When a partner engineer's `availability.resumes_on` date arrives, the
platform now auto-flips their status back to `available` AND fires a
single tailored welcome-back digest email that catches them up on
what's waiting. Closes the "ghost-return" gap where engineers came
back from leave but our gym-routing / queue UI didn't notice.

**Backend — `utils/partner_return_digest.py`.**

* Daily sweep (`sweep_once()`) driven by `run_forever(24)`, wired
  into server startup alongside the existing `partner_compliance`
  and `reputation_reports` loops.
* Query: `partner_engineers` where `status=approved`,
  `availability.status='unavailable'` and `availability.resumes_on`
  is on/before today. Pulls 2000 rows worst case — fine for a daily
  job, and the partial index on `status` already exists.
* For each partner: counts open `supplier_cases` rows by
  `supplier_email` + `status ∈ OPEN_CASE_STATUSES` (same open-set as
  the iter 220p `/queue/my-gyms` endpoint, so the email matches what
  the engineer sees on the dashboard). Also counts overdue cases
  (`due_at` / `promised_by` in the past).
* Collects compliance heads-ups: any of `insurance_expires_at`,
  `qualifications_expires_at`, or nested `compliance_docs[dbs|rtw|
  safeguarding|public_liability].expires_at` due in the next 30 days
  (or already expired) becomes a friendly bullet in the email.
* `days_away` derived from `availability.updated_at` so the copy
  reads "You've been away for 14 days —" instead of generic
  "You're back." Falls back gracefully when the field is missing.
* **Auto-resume.** After sending, persists
  `availability.status = 'available'`, clears `resumes_on` + `note`,
  and stamps `availability.welcome_back_fired_on = <resumes_on iso>`.
  The marker is the *triggering ISO date* (not "today") so taking
  another leave with a fresh `resumes_on` will fire again, but
  re-running the sweep for the same leave is a strict no-op.
* **Robustness.** Engineers with no email on file still get their
  availability flipped (so the sweep doesn't loop forever) — they
  just don't receive the digest. All exceptions during email send
  are logged and swallowed so a Resend outage can't crash the loop.

**Email template — `utils/partner_emails.send_welcome_back_digest`.**

* Subject varies with workload — "your GymAxis queue is clear" when
  open=0 vs. "3 jobs waiting" when there's real work, so the digest
  doesn't read like generic spam.
* Body sections (all conditional):
  - Welcome headline with first name + days-away phrase.
  - Workload paragraph with **N jobs** + (M overdue) in red when
    applicable; "clean slate" copy when 0.
  - Compliance warning block (amber bar) listing each item with
    its expiry phrasing ("expired on 12 Feb", "expires in 5 day(s)").
  - Echoed leave-note (`"You left a note before going off: …"`) so
    the engineer feels heard.
  - Status footer: "You're now marked **available** on GymAxis again
    — new contact requests will route to you straight away."
  - Single navy CTA → partner-engineer dashboard.

**Tests — `tests/test_iter_220r_welcome_back_digest.py` (9 tests, all green).**

* Fires on return-day; passes the right open / overdue counts.
* Fires for an overdue `resumes_on` (engineer forgot to toggle back).
* Idempotency — won't double-fire for the same `resumes_on`.
* Skips future-dated and available partners.
* Surfaces both legacy and nested compliance warnings.
* Missing-email path: no send, but availability still auto-resumes.
* Email template smoke-tests: full-workload and quiet-inbox branches.

**Regression.** `make regression` now reports **872 passed, 15 skipped**
(up from 863), confirming no other module regressed.

Shipped the engineer-side counterpart to the iter 220n supplier

for all the cases auto-routed to them from gyms they referred —

**Backend — `GET /api/svc/engineer/queue/my-gyms`.**

* Resolves the calling user → `partner_engineers` row via `user_id`.
  Non-engineer users get a soft `{"jobs": [], "is_partner_engineer":
  False}` (no 500 — gates exist higher up too).
* Finds every `db.suppliers` row where
  `partner_engineer_id == partner.id`. Those are the gyms this
  engineer is auto-dispatched to. Empty list → returns
  `no_gyms_yet: true` for the friendly empty state copy.
* Queries `db.supplier_cases` filtered to:
  - `supplier_email == partner.email`
  - `status ∈ ["new", "in_progress", "awaiting_parts", "scheduled",
    "awaiting_customer", "viewed"]` (open work only)
* Decorates each row with `from_referred_gym` + `is_primary_supplier`
  flags (sourced from the supplier row) so the UI can render the
  "★ Referred" provenance badge. Carries `supplier_case_token` so
  the row CTA can deeplink into the public supplier portal.
* Returns `gyms_count` for the pill's badge counter.

**Frontend — `EngineerQueue.js`.**

* New `viewMode` state (`'queue' | 'my-gyms'`). Default is `'queue'`.
  Toggling switches the data source that feeds the row list.
* Mount-time fetch is parallel — `/queue/unassigned` + `/queue/stats`
  + the new `/queue/my-gyms` all in one `Promise.all` so the pill
  has an instant count without a second roundtrip.
* **View-switcher pill** (data-testid `queue-view-switcher`) is
  conditionally rendered on `myGyms.is_partner_engineer === true`,
  so non-engineer users still get the queue UX unchanged. Two pills:
  - "Up for grabs · {N}" (default slate, black active state)
  - "★ My gyms · {N} [N gyms]" — active state uses the canonical
    GymAxis navy→purple gradient (#2563EB → #9D4CDD), the gyms-count
    sub-badge tints to white-on-gradient when active and to violet
    when inactive.
* **Row component branches on `viewMode`**:
  - Always renders the existing priority chip + SLA chip + ETA chip.
  - When `from_referred_gym === true`, renders a violet **★ Referred**
    badge (data-testid `queue-row-referred-{ref}`) with the
    explanation in the title attribute.
  - When `viewMode === 'my-gyms'`, the row's right-side CTA is
    "Open ticket" (violet) linking to `/supplier/case/{token}`
    in a new tab — NOT the claim button. These cases are already
    dispatched; the engineer manages them via the supplier portal.
* **Empty-state copy** is now view-aware:
  - "Up for grabs" empty → "All caught up · No unassigned jobs in your
    org…"
  - "My gyms" empty → either "Your gyms are all clear right now" OR
    (when `no_gyms_yet`) "You haven't been added as a supplier yet.
    Share your referral link to onboard gyms."

## Iter 220o — Instagram-attributed apply form (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

Shipped the "Instagram-attributed apply form" P1 — end-to-end UTM
attribution flow from the launch campaign all the way through to
the master-admin conversion summary.

**Frontend — `hooks/useUtmAttribution.js` (new shared hook).**

* Reads `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`,
  `utm_term`, plus `document.referrer` on mount.
* Persists to `sessionStorage` under `gx_utm_attribution` with
  **first-touch semantics** (matches GA — Instagram still gets
  credit even if the user comes back later via a bookmark).
* Fires a `POST /api/partners/track-source` ping with `keepalive: true`
  on the first tagged landing. Errors swallow — analytics never
  blocks UX.
* Returns `{ utm, isInstagram, applyHref }`. `applyHref` is
  `/partners/engineers/apply` with the UTM params re-attached so any
  CTA that uses it carries attribution into the apply form regardless
  of which button the visitor taps.

**Frontend — `PartnerEngineerLanding` hero swap.** When `isInstagram`
is true:

* Eyebrow: "Partner Engineer Network" → **"Saw us on Instagram"**
* Headline: "For independent fitness engineers." → **"You found us. Now let's talk shop."**
* Sub-copy: opens with "Welcome from Instagram. Everything you saw
  in the campaign is real — £30/mo that drops to free at 10
  referrals…"
* Primary CTA text: "Start application" → **"Claim your Instagram spot"**
* `data-attribution-source` attribute on the section (E2E hook).
* Both the hero and the final-CTA buttons use `applyHref` so
  attribution is preserved regardless of which one converts.

**Frontend — `PartnerApplyPublic` carries attribution forward.**
On submit, reads UTM first from the apply URL's query params, then
falls back to `sessionStorage`. If found, appends six Form fields
(`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`,
`utm_term`, `referrer_url`) to the multipart POST. If the user
didn't manually type a referral source, pre-fills it from
`utm_source` so master admin sees something useful.

**Backend — three new/updated endpoints in `routes/partners.py`.**

1. `POST /api/partners/track-source` (public, anonymous) — increments
   a per-(source|medium|campaign) counter in
   `db.partner_attribution_landings`. Upsert with `$inc`,
   `$setOnInsert`, `$set` on last-seen timestamps. Skips silently
   on no-UTM payloads so organic traffic doesn't pollute the bucket.
   Inputs lowercased + capped at 200 chars at the boundary.
2. `POST /api/partners/public-apply` — extended with six new Form
   fields (`utm_source`/medium/campaign/content/term + `referrer_url`),
   persisted onto the `partner_applications` doc with the same
   normalisation rules.
3. `GET /api/partners/attribution-summary` (master-admin only) — rolls
   up landings + applications per source. Each row gets enriched with
   `applications` count + `conversion_rate_pct`. Totals across all
   tagged channels included.

**Live smoke test.** Hit
`/partners/engineers?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=partner_launch_2026`
on the preview env via Playwright:

* `data-attribution-source` = `'instagram'` ✓
* Eyebrow = `SAW US ON INSTAGRAM` ✓
* Headline = `You found us. Now let's talk shop.` ✓
* Hero CTA text = `Claim your Instagram spot` ✓
* Hero CTA href = `/partners/engineers/apply?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=partner_launch_2026` ✓

Hit `POST /api/partners/track-source` with the same payload via curl:

```json
{"ok":true,"key":"instagram|social|partner_launch_2026"}
```

Hit it with `{}` → `{"ok":true,"skipped":"no-utm-source"}` (organic
filter working). Hit `GET /api/partners/attribution-summary` without
auth → HTTP 401 (master-admin gate working).

**Regression coverage.** New `test_iter_220o_instagram_attribution.py`
— **9 tests** (all green), wired into `Makefile::regression`:

| Test | Invariant pinned |
|---|---|
| `test_track_source_increments_counter_with_utm_source` | Right $inc + $setOnInsert + $set shape, upsert=True |
| `test_track_source_skips_when_no_utm_source` | Organic traffic must NEVER hit the counter |
| `test_track_source_normalises_utm_to_lowercase_and_caps_length` | Case-insensitive bucketing + 200-char cap |

| `test_apply_form_reads_session_storage_key` | E2E contract: same sessionStorage key on both sides |
| `test_partner_engineer_landing_swaps_hero_for_instagram` | All swap branches present + applyHref used ≥2× |

User direction was:

  with module bolt-ons, no Pro tier.
* **(2)** Build the supplier auto-dispatch feature so referred-gym faults
  flow to the referring engineer.

  Health"** in GymAxis-branded contexts.
* **(4)** AI Triage tab — "a must, should already have been included."
* **(5)** Strip any testimonial / customer-attribution copy because we
  have no real customers yet.
* **(6)** Skip master-admin parity work (user has what they need).
* **(7)** Polish landing page where required (audit showed
  `MarketingHome.js` was already on-brand with no fabricated proof).

**1. Partner Engineer → auto-supplier auto-dispatch (the headline
feature).** The Partner Plan promise — *"every gym you bring in is
recurring revenue AND recurring work"* — now delivers both halves:

* `routes/partners.py::attach_referral_to_org` — when a gym signs up
  with a Partner Engineer's referral code, idempotently insert a row
  into `db.suppliers` with `partner_engineer_id` link,
  `auto_dispatch=True`, `is_primary_supplier=True`,
  `auto_created_from_referral=True`. Rates (callout fee, labour rate,
  mileage, parts markup) are carried over from the partner profile.
  Failures are best-effort logged — never block a successful referral.
* `routes/issues.py::_auto_dispatch_to_primary_supplier` — new helper
  invoked from `create_issue` after the case is mirrored to Service
  Desk. Triggers ONLY when `resolution_type == 'engineer'` (in-house
  faults stay in-house). Picks the top-priority auto-dispatch supplier
  (sort: `is_primary_supplier desc, created_at asc`), calls the
  existing `routes.supplier_portal.create_supplier_case` to mint a
  token + send the supplier-portal email, and stamps the issue with
  `auto_dispatched_supplier_id/name/partner_engineer_id/at`.
  Idempotent — skips if a `supplier_cases` row already exists for the
  (issue_id, supplier_email) pair (covers retries + multi-machine
  batch flows).
* **Gym keeps full agency.** The existing Supplier Dashboard tab lets
  the gym disable `auto_dispatch`, swap the primary, or add more
  suppliers — nothing forced. Auto-created rows carry a flag the
  dashboard can render as an "Auto-added from your referral signup"
  badge in future polish.

**2 + 3. Brand-aware UI (Pulse Score → Gym Health, AI Triage tab).**

* `frontend/src/components/PulseScoreCard.js` — wired in `useAuth()`,
  branched on `account_type`. `pulse_pro` / `lite` accounts see "The
  Pulse · today" with the cyan→navy gradient ring; everyone else
  (GymAxis ops) sees "Gym Health · today" with the canonical navy
  `#2563EB` → purple `#9D4CDD` gradient. Loading + error strings also
  brand-switch.
* `frontend/src/pages/PulseAIDiagnosisTab.js` — un-orphaned (was
  imported nowhere). Wired into `LiteDashboardPage`'s `proBase` tab
  list as **"AI Triage"** (GymAxis) / **"AI Diagnosis"** (Pulse).
  Component-internal headings + tab labels also brand-switch via the
  same `account_type` probe.
* `LiteDashboardPage.js` — added the new TabsContent wrapper, imported
  `PulseAIDiagnosisTab`, added `Brain` icon for the tab.

**5. Fabricated customer names removed from PulseLandingPage.**

The mockup-email preview used "Sarah Johnson", "Lee Somers", and
"Tottenham Green" — all sufficiently plausible that a visitor could
reasonably mistake them for real customer references. Replaced with
"Floor Member", "Gym Manager", and "Example Gym" — clearly placeholder
strings. Pinned by regression test
`test_pulse_landing_has_no_fabricated_customer_names` so the banned

## Iter 220m (cont.) — Brand preview wired into CI quality gate (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

Wired `make brand-preview` into the GitHub Actions quality gate so any
PR that bumps a canonical hex without regenerating
`BRAND_PALETTE_PREVIEW.html` fails CI.

**Workflow change** (`.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml`, in the
existing `python-quality` job, immediately after the docs-verify
step):

```yaml
- name: Brand preview drift check
  run: |
    python3 scripts/build_brand_preview.py
    git diff --exit-code BRAND_PALETTE_PREVIEW.html
```

If the freshly-rendered preview differs from the committed copy, the
job fails with a non-zero git-diff exit code. Fix is one-line:
`make brand-preview && git commit -am "..."`.

**Deterministic stamp.** The previous stamp had a UTC wall-clock
timestamp that would have made every CI run fail the drift check.
Swapped it for a 12-char SHA-256 fingerprint of the concatenated
canon docs — so the rendered HTML only changes when the canon
actually does. Re-running `build_brand_preview.py` twice in a row
now produces byte-identical output.

**Files touched.**

* `.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml` — 8-line step inserted into
  the `python-quality` job.
* `scripts/build_brand_preview.py` — replaced `datetime.now()` stamp
  with `hashlib.sha256(canon).hexdigest()[:12]` fingerprint.
* `BRAND_PALETTE_PREVIEW.html` — regenerated with the new stamp.

**Quality gates.** Brand-canon regression suite (`make regression
tests/test_iter_220m_brand_canon.py`) ✓ 10/10. `make docs-verify` ✓
46 docs. `ruff check scripts/` ✓. `python3 -c "import yaml;
yaml.safe_load(...)"` confirms the workflow YAML parses.

## Iter 220m (cont.) — Test-hygiene sprint: 28 → 0 regression failures (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

User asked to run the dedicated test-hygiene sprint to fix the 21
pre-existing real regressions surfaced after the brand-canon work.
Net result: **`make regression` is now 100% green — 828 passed, 15
skipped, 0 failures, 0 errors — across 3 consecutive back-to-back
runs.**

**Stale assertion fixes (9 tests).**

* `test_iter_216h284_activation_checklist` (3 tests) — the live
  `CHECKLIST_KEYS` tuple grew from 6 → 7 (added `stripe_connect_ready`
  between `subscribed` and `compliance_uploaded`). Tests now assert
  against `len(CHECKLIST_KEYS)` so the count auto-tracks future
  additions instead of needing a manual bump each time.
* `test_iter_216h261_engineer_customer_suggest` (4 tests) — the
  `/svc/engineer/customers/lookup` route grew `name` + `site_name`
  `Query()` params. Tests called the route fn directly without
  providing those, so Python used the `Query(default=None, ...)`
  defaults verbatim (Query *object*, not `None`), and the route's
  `(name or "").strip()` crashed. Added explicit `name=None,
  site_name=None` to every direct-call.
* `test_iter_216h259_engineer_lite_crm::test_support_moved_to_top_nav`
  — the Support button moved AGAIN, from EngineerHomeV2's header
  into the EngineerAccountSettings drawer's Help section. Updated
  the assertion to point at the new home + still verify the
  invariant ("Support reachable via navigate('/support')").
* `test_iter_216h260_engineer_customers_csv_history::test_customers_page_has_csv_buttons`
  — CSV import + template-download moved from EngineerCustomers
  into the same settings drawer. Updated assertions to
  `engineer-settings-template-row` / `engineer-settings-import-row`.

**Event-loop cascade fix (12 tests).** Two new autouse fixtures in
`backend/tests/conftest.py`:

1. `_ensure_event_loop` (function-scope) — guarantees every test
   sees a usable thread-default asyncio loop before it runs. On
   Python 3.11+, `asyncio.get_event_loop()` raises `RuntimeError:
   There is no current event loop in thread 'MainThread'` once any
   earlier `asyncio.run(...)` has cleared the thread-default. Was
   producing the cascade of ~13 pseudo-failures: tests that pass
   in isolation but trip the moment they run after another test's
   `asyncio.run`. Fixture creates a fresh loop if `get_event_loop()`
   raises or returns a closed one.

2. `_rebind_motor_to_current_loop` (function-scope) — spins up a
   fresh `AsyncIOMotorClient` per-test and re-publishes it into
   `utils.database.client/db` plus every downstream module that
   imported `db` by value (`routes.partners`,
   `utils.reputation_reports`, `routes.svc.engineer_customers`).
   Motor v3 lazy-binds its connection pool to whichever event loop
   drives the first I/O; the binding survives a `close()` (close
   is permanent). Per-test rebind drops any pool stranded on a
   closed loop and yields a `maxPoolSize=8` client so 800+ tests
   don't exhaust MongoDB's connection ceiling. Teardown restores
   the originals and closes the per-test client.

**Bonus fix — httpx rate-limit cascade.** The existing
`_patch_requests_with_ratelimit_bypass` autouse fixture only patched
`requests`, but the 220k/l/m + 217 + 218 suites all use `httpx.Client`
directly for auth calls. Three consecutive `make regression` runs
were tripping the `/api/auth/login` brute-force guard (5 req / 5 min)
and cascading into 108 setup-errors on the third run. Extended the
fixture to also monkey-patch `httpx.Client.request` with the same
`X-RateLimit-Bypass` header. All three back-to-back runs now green.

**Files touched.**

* `backend/tests/conftest.py` — two new autouse fixtures + httpx
  rate-limit patch.
* `backend/tests/test_iter_216h284_activation_checklist.py` —
  assert vs `len(CHECKLIST_KEYS)` instead of hard-coded `6`.
* `backend/tests/test_iter_216h261_engineer_customer_suggest.py` —
  pass `name=None, site_name=None` to direct route-fn calls.
* `backend/tests/test_iter_216h259_engineer_lite_crm.py` —
  point support-row assertion at EngineerAccountSettings.
* `backend/tests/test_iter_216h260_engineer_customers_csv_history.py` —
  point CSV-button assertion at EngineerAccountSettings.

**Quality gates (all green).** `make regression` ✓ 828 pass × 3
runs. `make docs-verify` ✓ 46 docs. `make brand-preview` ✓.
`ruff check` on every touched file ✓.

* New: `build_brand_preview.py` pins all 10 hexes (5 GymAxis + 5
  Pulse) so silent drift in the renderer fires CI.
* New: rendered `BRAND_PALETTE_PREVIEW.html` contains both brand
  sections + every canonical hex + the DO NOT USE table.

**Quality gates.** `make docs-verify` ✓ 46 docs scanned. `make
brand-preview` ✓ regenerates the HTML. `ruff check` clean on every
file I introduced.

**Heads-up resolution — test isolation hunt.**

Identified the cascading failure pattern and fixed the dominant
class (down 28 → 21 failures):

* Root cause #1 (now fixed): `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(...)`
  pattern across ~70 test files. On Python 3.11+, `get_event_loop()`
  raises once any earlier `asyncio.run(...)` closes the previous loop.
  Added a session-scoped `_shared_event_loop` autouse fixture in
  `tests/conftest.py` that creates ONE shared loop for the whole
  pytest session. That alone eliminated 7 cascading failures.

* Root cause #2 (NOT fixed — flagged for future work): the remaining
  21 failures are **real bugs**, not isolation flakes:
    – `test_iter_216h261_engineer_customer_suggest` (4 tests) — tests
      call FastAPI route fn directly with Pydantic `Query()` defaults
      where the route expects HTTP-resolved strings. Wrong-shaped test.
    – `test_iter_216h284_activation_checklist` (3 tests) — assert 6
      steps but the live builder now returns 7 (product evolved,
      test stale).
    – `test_iter_216h259/260` (2 tests) — assert `data-testid` strings
      that recent JSX refactors removed/renamed.
    – `test_iter_220i_branding_and_email::test_wrap_branded_uses_self_hosted_mark`
      — mark URL pattern changed in iter 220i.
    – `test_iter_220k/l/m` (~11 tests) — motor (async MongoDB driver)
      caches connections to whichever loop runs first; subsequent
      `run_until_complete` calls fail with "Future attached to a
      different loop". Proper fix requires either pytest-asyncio
      adoption or resetting motor clients between tests — bigger
      refactor, out of scope for this iter.

All 21 are pre-existing regressions that were merely *hidden* by the
cascading asyncio cascade. They're now visible and tracked — flagged
in this PRD entry for a dedicated test-hygiene sprint.

## Iter 220m (cont.) — Doc drift guard (May 26, 2026) ✅

Prevents the doc drift problem we just fixed (iters 216h232 → 220m
where 19+ docs accumulated stale "Status — Iter 216h232" banners)
from happening again on the next big sprint.

**New script.** `/app/scripts/docs_verify.py` (~95 lines):

* Reads the canonical current iter from `/app/memory/.current_iter`
  (single line, currently `220m`).
* Scans every shipped `.md` under `/app/memory`, `/app/docs`,
  `/app/*.md`, `/app/marketing/partner_engineer_launch/*.md`.
* Pulls the FIRST status banner from each file (matches both shapes
  we emit: `> **📋 Status — Iter XXX (...)**` and
  `## Iter XXX (...)`).
* Exits 1 with a per-file diff table if any banner doesn't match
  the current iter. Untagged docs are allowed; PRD.md +
  CHANGELOG.md are skiplisted (they're meant to carry historical
  iter labels in their bodies).

**Makefile wiring.**

* New `make docs-verify` target.
* Folded into the existing `make lint` aggregate so every local
  `make lint` invocation now also verifies the docs.
* Help text updated.

**CI wiring.**

* `quality-gate.yml` now runs `python3 scripts/docs_verify.py` as a
  Python-job step between Ruff and Bandit. PRs to `main` that
  touch code without bumping the doc banners (or skiplisting the
  affected files) fail immediately.

**Smoke test result.** 41 docs scanned, 0 stale. Simulated drift
(set `.current_iter` to `999z`) correctly fails with a 25-row diff
table; restoring to `220m` returns to ✓ in a single second.

**Bump workflow for next sprint.** When you cut iter 220n:

1. Edit `/app/memory/.current_iter` → `220n`.
2. Run `make docs-verify` — it'll list every doc still stamped
   `220m`.
3. Either bump the banner in those docs to `220n` (preferred), or
   add them to `_SKIP` in `docs_verify.py` if they're now pure
   changelogs.

## Iter 220m — Monthly Reputation Report email (May 26, 2026) ✅

Turns happy customers into engineer marketing on autopilot, on a
fully automated monthly cadence with zero new operator workload.

**Backend.**

* New `utils/reputation_reports.py`:
    * `build_monthly_report(engineer_user_id, year, month)` —
      aggregates `svc_cases.customer_rating` for the calendar month
      into `{avg, count, distribution[1..5], best_quote,
      prev_avg, prev_count, delta}`. Returns `None` when the
      engineer collected zero ratings (caller skips).
    * `render_monthly_report_html(engineer, report, ratings_url)` —
      branded HTML email with:
        – Big avg in an amber gradient hero card.
        – Star-string render of the avg.
        – Trend pill (▲ +1.67 / ▼ −0.4 / — Stable / First month
          tracked) coloured emerald / rose / indigo / slate.
        – "Quote of the month" pull-quote card (highest-rated, longest
          comment first).
        – Star-distribution histogram with amber bars.
        – Two CTAs side-by-side: **"See every review →"** (deep-link
          to `/svc/engineer/ratings`) and **"Share on LinkedIn"**
          (LinkedIn `sharing/share-offsite` URL pre-filled with
          `⭐ {avg} avg from {count} review(s) this month. Proud
          of the work via @GymAxis…`).
    * `run_monthly_reputation_reports(force_period?)` — one sweep
      over `partner_engineers (status=approved)`. Idempotency via
      `reputation_reports.last_sent_period = "YYYY-MM"`. Without
      `force_period`, the sweep is a no-op unless `today.day == 1`.
    * `run_forever(interval_hours=6)` — async background loop. The
      6-hour interval is a robustness padding so a missed minute
      around midnight UTC on the 1st doesn't skip the entire run.
* New admin endpoint
  `POST /api/partners/admin/{partner_id}/send-reputation-report`
  body `{period?: "YYYY-MM"}` — master-admin-only. Resends on demand;
  defaults to the previous calendar month.
* Loop wired in `server.py` on startup (log: `[reputation-reports]
  loop started (6h)`).

**Testing.**

* `tests/test_iter_220m_reputation_reports.py` — 6 tests, all
  green:
    * Empty period → `None`.
    * Population + delta + best-quote selection logic.
    * Rendered HTML contains the LinkedIn share URL + avg + delta.
    * Idempotency stamp lands on the partner record.
    * Admin trigger endpoint works against the live preview.
    * Non-first-of-month sweep is a no-op (`reason: not_first_of_month`).
* Added to `Makefile::regression`.
* Full iter-220 suite: **103 passed, 3 skipped.** Zero new linter
  warnings.

**Operator notes.**

* The first natural firing happens at the next month-end (1st of
  next month UTC, ~04:00 → 06:00 depending on the loop wake
  cadence). You can dry-run it any time via the admin endpoint by
  passing a `period` of your choice.

## Iter 220k — Release-blocking P0 gates (May 26, 2026) ✅

Following the pre-release journey audit, three real gaps could
strand customers, expose the platform to liability, or admit
non-KYC'd engineers onto gym floors. All three are now closed.

**P0-1 / P0-3 — Compliance-to-claim gate (combined).**

* New `require_engineer_compliance_to_claim` dependency in
  `routes/partners.py`. Layered on top of `require_engineer_app_access`
  so the engineer can still see the dashboard + upload docs, but
  cannot pick up *new* paid work until:
    * `partner.compliance_paused` is **False**, AND
    * at least one of `{dbs, rtw}` has a `file` on record whose
      `expires_at` is either absent or strictly in the future.
* Applied to the only two endpoints that create/claim a paid
  case for a partner engineer:
    * `POST /api/svc/engineer/queue/{case_id}/claim` (queue claim)
    * `POST /api/svc/engineer/jobs/self-create` (self-create)
* Bypass cohorts: `master_admin`, `internal_engineer`,
  `customer_grant` — these engineers aren't on the Partner
  Engineer contract so the compliance gate doesn't apply.
* New `_BLOCK_MESSAGES` entries: `compliance_paused`,
  `compliance_required`. Returned alongside the structured 403
  payload so the frontend can surface a precise reason +
  `required_one_of`.

**P0-2 — Mid-job cancellation recovery.**

New `_handle_partner_loss_of_access(partner_id, reason)` invoked
automatically from `handle_partner_subscription_event` whenever
the partner's Stripe subscription flips to `canceled`,
`unpaid`, or `incomplete_expired`. For every in-flight
`svc_cases` assigned to the engineer (status ∈
`{assigned, en_route, on_site, paused_parts, paused_customer,
repaired, awaiting_sign_off}`):

1. Unassign the engineer (`assigned_engineer_id = null`) and flip
   back to `new` with `needs_reassignment = True` plus a
   structured `needs_reassignment_reason`.
2. Append a `partner_access_lost` audit event so the dispatch
   admin has a paper trail.
3. Email the org's `support_email` (or fallback to the owner) a
   single digest listing every affected case, asking them to
   reassign.

This protects the customer experience — they no longer get
stranded mid-visit by an unrelated billing event between GymAxis
and the engineer.

**Testing.**

* New `tests/test_iter_220k_release_gates.py` (8 tests, all green):
    * `_has_valid_claim_doc` unit tests across edge cases.
    * Direct gate invocations: no docs → 403, paused → 403, dbs
      valid → pass, master_admin → pass, no subscription → 402
      (inheritance from upstream guard).
    * HTTP-level: master admin claim endpoint still 404s on bogus
      case_id (regression — admin support flow not broken).
    * Mid-job recovery: in-flight case → NEW + needs_reassignment;
      closed case untouched; audit event written.
* Added to `Makefile::regression`. Fixed two pre-existing
  `KeyError: 0` bugs in `test_iter_220i_full.py` (mishandled the
  `/svc/engineer/jobs?when=...` `{by_day: {...}}` shape).
* Full iter-220 regression: **87 passed, 2 skipped** (skips are
  graceful "no test data" branches). Zero new linter warnings.

**Operator notes.**

* When deploying, dispatch admins will start receiving "Action
  needed: N job(s) need reassignment" emails the moment a
  subscription cancels. The email uses `org.support_email` if set,
  otherwise the org owner. Configure `support_email` in
  Organisation Settings if you want a shared inbox to receive these.

## Iter 220j — Engineer hamburger attention badge (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

Engineers had no in-app way to know something off-screen needed their
eye — they'd discover a past-due Stripe payment or an expired
insurance cert only when a customer complained or a job got blocked.
This iter adds a single source of truth + visual nudge.

**Backend.**

* New `routes/svc/attention.py` (registered in
  `route_registry/features.py`). Single read-only endpoint
  `GET /api/svc/engineer/attention` aggregates everything that
  needs an approved engineer's eye:
    * Partner application state (pending/rejected/suspended)
    * Stripe subscription (past_due / canceled / inactive)
    * Compliance docs expired or expiring in &lt;14 days (any kind
      under `partner.compliance_docs`)
    * `compliance_paused` flag set by the nightly compliance job
    * Stripe Connect Express not finished (`charges_enabled` false)
* Returns `{count, severity, items[]}` where severity is the highest
  of any item: `red` (blocks paid work) &gt; `amber` (time-sensitive)
  &gt; `green` (nothing).
* Items sort red-first; each carries a stable `key`, label, hint,
  and `cta_to` deep-link.

**Frontend.**

* New hook `pages/ServiceOps/Engineer/hooks/useEngineerAttention.js`
  — fetches the digest, optional 90 s polling, silent fallback on
  network errors (so the menu never shows a spurious dot when the
  API is down).
* `EngineerHomeV2`'s hamburger dot is now unified:
    * **Red, pulsing** (`animate-ping`) when severity = red.
    * **Amber, solid** when severity = amber OR legacy `payouts.ready`
      false.
    * **No dot** otherwise.
* The attention digest is passed into `EngineerAccountSettings` so
  the drawer renders an inline "Needs your attention" card at the
  very top (above the Partner Engineer row), with each item as a
  tap-to-fix button styled red/amber per severity. Closing the
  drawer + navigating happens on a single tap.
* The `onChanged` callback on the drawer now also refreshes the
  attention digest, so resolving an item (e.g. uploading a doc)
  clears the dot the moment they re-open the drawer.

**Testing.**

* New `backend/tests/test_iter_220j_engineer_attention.py` (5 tests):
  default-green, past_due subscription → red, expired+expiring
  compliance, Stripe Connect amber, auth required. All green.
* Added to `Makefile::regression`.
* Full iter-220 suite: **81/81 pass** (up from 76).
* No new ruff / ESLint warnings.

## Iter 220h — Proactive "save new customer" prompt (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

User asked: *"If the engineer types in a customer into new job that
they don't have in their customers, ask if they would like to add to
their database for future use."* (Iter 220f had a passive checkbox at
the bottom of the form — easy to miss.)

**Backend.**

* `GET /api/svc/engineer/customers/lookup` now also matches on
  `?name=…&site_name=…`. Case-insensitive exact name match (no
  fuzzy — the typeahead already covers similar). When email or phone
  also matches, contact-match wins (single source of truth).
* Response now includes `match_via: "contact" | "name"` so the
  frontend can decide whether to suppress the prompt with high
  confidence.

**Frontend.**

* New `NewCustomerPrompt` component in `EngineerNewJob.js`.
* Watches `customer_name` with a 450 ms debounce. The moment the typed
  name returns `{found: false}` from `/lookup`, an inline **amber
  confirm strip** appears between the Customer & site form and the
  saved-customer checkbox:

  **Not now** (dismiss for this session) buttons.

## Iter 220g — Smart scheduling suggestions (P2) (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

User requested: *"Intuitive scheduling, if the engineer already has
jobs booked around the same area as the new job that's being scheduled
recommend this day, but also let them manually book."* Confirmed radius:
10 miles (UK-tight).

**Backend.**

* New module `routes/svc/scheduling_suggestions.py`.
* `GET /api/svc/engineer/scheduling-suggestions?postcode=…&days=14&radius_miles=10`.
* Geocoding via the free public **postcodes.io** API (no key, no auth).
  Results cached in `postcode_cache` so we hit the API at most once per
  postcode per pod lifetime. Misses are cached too (to dodge repeated
  fetches for typos).
* Distance via haversine formula → 10-mile filter.
* Graceful degradation: if geocoder unreachable for either side,
  outward-postcode-code match (e.g. `CV1` ≈ `CV1` → ~3 miles) lets the
  feature still work offline / in tests.
* Returns top 5 dates sorted by `job_count desc, min_distance asc, date asc`.
* Engineer scoped (only sees their own jobs), org-isolated.
* Path is `/svc/engineer/scheduling-suggestions` (NOT nested under
  `/jobs/` — would have collided with `/jobs/{case_id}`).

**Frontend.**

* `EngineerNewJob.js` gained `SmartSchedulingPanel` rendered above the
  *Scheduled for* input.
* 350 ms debounced — fires only once the engineer's postcode is ≥5 chars.
* States:
  * **Loading** — small blue strip with spinner.
  * **No nearby jobs** — muted slate strip, "feel free to pick any date".
  * **Has matches** — amber panel "You already have jobs near here
    within 10 miles" with tappable chips for each suggested date.
* Each chip shows weekday + DD MMM + a job-count badge + the
  minimum-distance mile pill. Tap → pre-fills *Scheduled for* with the
  picked date at 09:00. Tapped chips turn green with a checkmark.
* Manual booking always still works.

## Iter 220f — Customer typeahead on the New Job card (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-requested

User requested: *"The new job card needs to be able to search for
customers, once the customer is selected all fields are populated with
their information, again to save the engineer typing."* Confirmed
source: engineer's saved customers + org-wide customers list.

**Backend.**

* New endpoint `GET /api/svc/engineer/customers/typeahead?q=…&limit=N`
  that merges two data sources, deduped on (name + site):
  1. `svc_engineer_customers` — the saved address book.
     `source="saved"`, sorted by `updated_at desc`.
  2. `svc_cases` distinct `customer_name / customer_email / customer_phone
     / site_name / site_postcode` matches.
     `source="history"`, sorted by `updated_at desc`. Surfaces customers
     captured via the email-parse flow / public intake card that
     haven't been promoted into the saved book yet.
* Returned shape: `[{id, name, email, phone, site_name, site_address,
  site_postcode, last_job_at, source}]`. Saved entries win on dedupe.

**Frontend.**

* `EngineerNewJob.js` gained a `CustomerTypeahead` component above the
  *Customer & site* section:
  * 250 ms debounced search → hits the new typeahead endpoint.
  * Dropdown shows up to 8 results with name + subtitle (site,
    postcode, email, phone).
  * Saved customers get a green check icon. History-only entries get
    an amber history icon + "past job" badge so the engineer knows
    that customer isn't in their book yet.
  * Tap or `Enter` → all 6 customer/site fields are populated in one
    go. Keyboard nav: ↑ ↓ Esc.
  * Green selected-pill at the bottom shows the chosen customer; a
    small X clears the lock.
* `Clear` button at the top-right of the *Customer & site* section
  wipes all 6 fields with a confirm.
* New "Save *<name>* to my customers" tickbox auto-enables when the
  engineer types ≥2 chars in `customer_name` AND no saved customer was
  picked. On successful job creation, POSTs to
  `/api/svc/engineer/customers` so next time the typeahead finds them.
  Non-blocking — a save failure (e.g. duplicate) doesn't abort the

User requested: *"engineers need to be able to write reports against
individual machines… the easiest method to capture detail against
individual machines so the engineer hasn't got to keep typing the same

with Date · Erg type · Serial · Serviced (Y) · Cleaned (Y) · Notes /

## Iter 220c — Engineer App autosave (P0 data-loss bug) (May 26, 2026) ✅ user-reported

User-reported P0: engineer types "Testing 123" in Work summary, switches
to Parts tab to look at fitted parts, comes back — text is GONE. Root
cause: `CompleteTab` is conditionally rendered (only when active tab is
`complete`), so React unmounts it on every tab switch, dropping all
local component state. The fix is two-tier persistence:

**Backend.**

* New collection `svc_engineer_job_drafts` keyed by
  `(organization_id, engineer_id, case_id)` (unique index).
* New endpoints under `/api/svc/engineer/jobs/{case_id}`:
  * `GET /draft` — fetch latest persisted draft.
  * `PUT /draft` — upsert. Body `{draft: {...}}` is opaque; capped at
    32 KB to keep one runaway client from flooding the collection.
  * `DELETE /draft` — clear (called on successful complete).
* `engineer_complete` now deletes the engineer's draft on success so
  re-opening a closed case never shows stale text.

**Frontend.**

* New `useJobDraft(caseId)` hook — localStorage write on every
  keystroke (sync, instant — survives mid-typing tab switches) +
  debounced 1-second backend PUT (durable — survives device loss).
  Reconciles local vs remote on mount: server wins if its `updated_at`
  is newer (cross-device).
* `EngineerJobDetailV2` now lifts the draft state OUT of `CompleteTab`
  so it survives unmount. New `DraftStatusPill` in the header shows
  *Saving… / ● Unsaved / ✓ Saved*.
* `goBack` confirms with the engineer when the draft is dirty
  ("You have unsaved work — leave anyway?"). The draft is still safe
  locally, so accidentally hitting the back button doesn't actually
  lose anything — the dialog is a reassurance + a chance to cancel.
* `window.beforeunload` hooked to show the browser's native
  "unsaved changes" warning when the user reloads / closes the tab.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_iter_220c_engineer_draft_autosave.py`,
6 cases — all green):

* `test_draft_round_trip_persists_and_returns_typed_summary`
* `test_draft_subsequent_put_overwrites_previous_payload`
* `test_draft_delete_clears_storage`
* `test_complete_clears_draft_after_success`
* `test_draft_rejects_payload_larger_than_32_kb`
* `test_draft_404_for_unknown_case`

**testing_agent_v3_fork report** (`/app/test_reports/iteration_220c.json`):
PASS — critical tab-switch persistence verified end-to-end, page-reload
persistence verified, autosave indicator transitions confirmed, back-button
warning fires correctly. 28/28 backend tests (6 iter 220c + 14 iter 220
+ 8 iter 219g). 0 issues found.

## Iter 220b — Asset reading sparkline (trend view) for custom Work Report fields (May 25, 2026) ✅

Now that engineers are capturing structured machine readings on every
visit, surface the drift trend right next to the input so a slow drift
(Drag Factor 122 → 118 → 114) becomes obvious *before* the next call-out.

**Backend.**

* `GET /api/svc/work-report-fields/history/{case_id}?limit=N` returns
  `{series: {key: [{value, captured_at, case_id, case_reference}, ...]}}`,
  oldest-first, scoped to the same `asset_id` (or `asset_name`
  fallback). Default limit=8, range 2-30.
* Only numeric/boolean readings are surfaced — text/date/file values
  are silently skipped because they don't trend; booleans are coerced
  to 0/1 so the sparkline can render them.
* Reuses the same status filter as the last-reading lookup
  (`closed | repaired | awaiting_sign_off | invoiced`).

**Frontend.**

* New `AssetReadingSparkline.js` component — pure SVG, no library.
  Renders the trend, appends the engineer's current input value as a
  highlighted dot, and prints a colour-coded label:
  * 🔻 Trending down (rose)
  * 🟢 Trending up (emerald)
  * — Steady (slate) when the swing is < 5% of the range.
  * Tooltip lists the last 5 values + dates.
* Wired into `WorkReportCustomFields.js` — sparkline appears under
  numeric / checkbox fields when the asset has ≥2 prior readings.
  Text / date / dropdown / file fields stay untouched.

**Tests added** (2 cases, all green — 14/14 now in this file):
