## Iter 219e — Stripe-guided approval onboarding + auto-claim + checklist (Feb 25, 2026)

Operator request: *"Once the application is approved the engineer
should receive the email to say approved and then they should be
guided to Stripe to pay and set up the £30 a month subscription fee
for GymAxis. [+option B — add Stripe Connect to the checklist]"*

While auditing the existing flow we found **a critical pre-existing
blocker**: 37 of 40 already-approved engineers had a
`partner_engineers.user_id` stuck at `pending:<partner_id>` because
the public-apply path doesn't create a user account, and there was
**no claim-on-login hook**. Every one of those engineers would have
hit a brick wall on their first login. We bundled the fix in.

### Changes
- **New util** `backend/utils/partner_claim.py`
  - `claim_pending_partner_for_user(email, user_id)` — sweeps
    `partner_engineers` for rows whose `email` matches
    (case-insensitive) and whose `user_id` still starts with
    `pending:`, sets `user_id` to the real authenticated user. Best-
    effort, never raises (auth must never fail because of a partner-
    side hiccup).
- **Auth wiring** (`backend/routes/auth.py`)
  - `/auth/register` calls the claim helper after the user row is
    created. Also now honours `X-RateLimit-Bypass` so the CI suite
    can register multiple test users from one IP.
  - `_finalise_successful_login` (the shared post-login finaliser)
    calls the claim helper on every successful login, so the
    existing 37 stranded partners self-heal on their next login.
- **Approval email rewrite** (`backend/utils/partner_emails.py`)
  - Subject: *"You're approved — start your £30/mo Partner Plan
    with Stripe"*.
  - Body leads with the Stripe subscription pitch and a single
    primary CTA button: **"Start Partner Plan with Stripe
    (£30/mo)"**.
  - CTA URL: `/partner-engineer?action=subscribe` (new helper
    `_partner_subscribe_url`) — the dashboard reads the
    query-string and fires Stripe Checkout automatically once the
    engineer is authenticated.
  - Next-steps now sequenced: Subscribe → Connect Stripe Express →
    Upload compliance → Open Engineer App. Referral code still
    embedded.
- **Dashboard auto-trigger** (`frontend/.../PartnerEngineer/PartnerDashboard.js`)
  - On mount, when `?action=subscribe` is present and the engineer
    has no `stripe_subscription_id` yet, we strip the flag from the
    URL, toast "Taking you to Stripe…" and immediately call
    `startSubscription()` → Stripe Checkout. Idempotent: a
    returning subscriber is silently no-op'd.
- **Activation checklist** (`backend/utils/partner_checklist.py`)
  - 7-step checklist instead of 6 — new `stripe_connect_ready`
    step lives between *Subscribe to Partner Plan* and *Upload
    compliance doc*. Auto-resolves from
    `partner.payout.stripe_connect.charges_enabled` so the
    Engineer-app Stripe-Connect onboarding callback turns it
    green automatically.
  - Trophy banner copy bumped from "6/6" → "7/7".

### Verification
- Ruff 0 warnings on every changed Python file. ESLint 0 warnings
  on the two changed FE files.
- New pytest `test_iter_219e_stripe_guided_approval.py` (10 tests,
  all pass):
  - Email subject mentions Stripe + £30.
  - CTA deep-links to `?action=subscribe`, body sequences
    subscription before Stripe Connect Express.
  - Auto-claim relinks a pending partner row through the real
    `/auth/register` route (end-to-end against preview).
  - Case-insensitive email match for auto-claim.
  - Already-claimed rows are NOT re-assigned (idempotent / safe).
  - Null-input handling.
  - `/auth/register` and `_finalise_successful_login` source-pin
    asserts so we don't regress the wiring.
  - Checklist now has 7 keys; step 3 is `stripe_connect_ready`;
    auto-resolves from the payout flag; trophy banner only fires
    at 7/7.
- **Full iter 217–219 suite: 74/74 pass** when run together.

### Files changed

## Iter 219f — Single-use activation link ("How do I sign in?") (Feb 25, 2026)

User-reported gap from the **first** approved engineer: *"How do I sign
in?"*. There was no clear path from the approval email to a working
account. Engineers were expected to find /register on their own, guess
they had to use the same email, and hope the auto-claim hook (iter 219e)
worked. This iter closes the loop end-to-end.

### Flow now
**Apply → Approved (master admin clicks Approve in drawer) → Welcome email
with "Set up your sign-in (1 min)" CTA → activation page (email
pre-filled & locked, password field) → account created + partner
record auto-linked + token consumed → auto-redirect to Stripe Checkout
for £30/mo Partner Plan → return to dashboard with subscription active
→ 7-step activation checklist shows Stripe Connect Express as next step
→ engineer onboards Stripe Connect for taking customer card payments →
Engineer App → invoicing customers.**

### Changes
- **Approval endpoint** (`POST /api/partners/applications/{id}/approve`):
  generates a `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` single-use activation token
  and writes it (+ 14-day TTL) onto `partner_applications`.
- **Resend endpoint** (`/resend-approval-email`): re-uses the existing
  token while it's valid + unused; mints a fresh one only when
  expired or already consumed.
- **New endpoint** `POST /api/partners/activation/info` — public; takes
  `{token}` and returns `{email, full_name, has_existing_account}`.
  Used by the FE to pre-fill the form and decide whether to show the
  password-set flow or a "Sign in to claim" prompt.
- **New endpoint** `POST /api/partners/activation/complete` — public;
  takes `{token, password}`. Validates token via `_find_active_activation`,
  enforces 8-char minimum + `validate_password_strength`, creates the
  user, calls `claim_pending_partner_for_user` to link the partner row,
  burns the token, mints a JWT, and returns `next_url` pointing at the
  Stripe Checkout deep-link.
- **Conflict handling**: if a user with the same email already exists,
  the activation endpoint returns **409** with a message asking them to
  sign in (where the iter 219e auto-claim hook picks up the partner
  row). The FE swaps to a "Sign in to claim" view when
  `has_existing_account=true`.
- **Email helper** (`send_application_approved`): now accepts
  `activation_token` and switches CTA copy/URL when provided:
  - Subject: "You're approved — set up your sign-in (1 min)".
  - CTA: "Set up your sign-in (1 min)" → `/partner-engineer/activate?token=…`.
  - Body sequences: Set up sign-in → Pay Partner Plan → Connect Stripe
    Express → Compliance → Engineer App.
- **New page** `frontend/.../PartnerEngineer/PartnerEngineerActivate.js`
  (public route `/partner-engineer/activate`). Dark theme, three
  states: loading / error / form. Email is read-only with a "contact
  support" note for changes. Show/hide password toggle. After successful
  submit, persists JWT to localStorage and hard-redirects to Stripe
  Checkout deep-link via `window.location` so the new auth is honored.

### Verification
- Ruff 0 warnings. ESLint 0 warnings.
- New pytest `test_iter_219f_partner_activation_flow.py` (10 tests):
  approval writes token w/ 14-day expiry; info endpoint round-trip;
  404 on unknown/empty token; complete creates user + links partner +
  returns Stripe URL; token cannot be replayed; rejects short password
  (token still valid for retry); 409 when user already exists;
  info flags existing account; email body uses activation URL when
  token provided.
- **Full iter 217–219 regression: 84/84 pass** when run together.
- Live UI smoke: activation page renders form (valid token), and "Link
  unavailable" rose card (invalid token). Sample resent to
  leersomers@gmail.com with the new subject + CTA.

### Files changed

## Iter 219g — Smart "Send sign-in link" + Stripe success celebration (Feb 25, 2026)

Two ship-list items in one cut:

1. **Operator request**: *"I need to be able to send the partner
   engineers a reset password link. As this new engineer hasn't has
   the chance to create a login yet."* — needed because the engineer
   approved before iter 219f never received an activation link, and
   there was no master-admin lever to send them either an activation
   link *or* a password reset.

2. **Continuation of the celebration enhancement suggested at the
   end of iter 219f** — give the engineer a clear "you just paid →
   here's the next step" hero so they don't go cold after Stripe
   Checkout.

### Changes
- **New smart endpoint** `POST /api/partners/applications/{id}/send-signin-link`
  (master admin only). Auto-routes:
  - User account exists → mints a `password_reset_tokens` row (1-hour
    TTL, `issued_via=admin_partner_drawer`) and sends the standard
    password-reset email (`utils.email.send_password_reset_email`).
  - User account doesn't exist yet → reuses an existing valid
    activation token or mints a fresh one, then sends the welcome
    email with the "Set up your sign-in" CTA.
  - Returns `{ok, kind, sent_to}` so the FE toast can say exactly
    what was sent.
  - Audit log entries are kind-specific (`send_activation_link` /
    `send_password_reset`) so we can prove which kind of email went
    out.
- **Drawer button rename** — `PartnerApplicationDrawer.js`:
  "Resend approval email" → **"Send sign-in link"**. Hovers tooltip
  explains the smart routing. Same `data-testid` so existing tests
  continue to pass.
- **Celebration hero** — `PartnerDashboard.js`:
  New `SubscriptionCelebration` component (CSS-only confetti, no
  new deps). Triggered when the dashboard mounts with
  `?subscription=success` in the URL (the success_url Stripe Checkout
  returns to). Shows:
  - Subscription-active eyebrow, "You're in, {firstName}." headline.
  - Body explaining the next 3-minute step.
  - Primary CTA **"Connect Stripe Express (3 min)"** → navigates to
    `/svc/engineer/payouts`.
  - Secondary "Skip for now" and dismiss X.
  - The `subscription=success` flag stays in the URL until the
    engineer interacts with the hero, then it's stripped (so a
    refresh doesn't re-fire).
- **Param-clone fix** — both this iter and iter 219e relied on
  `params.delete(...)` followed by `setParams(params)` to mutate the
  URLSearchParams in place. React Router 6 silently dropped the
  remaining params in some cases. Now both call sites clone via
  `new URLSearchParams(params)` first.

### Verification
- Ruff 0 warnings, ESLint 0 warnings.
- New pytest `test_iter_219g_send_signin_link.py` (8 tests, all pass):
  activation path; activation reissue when token missing/expired;
  password-reset path with `password_reset_tokens` row written;
  400 if application still pending; 404 unknown; 403 non-admin;
  kind-specific audit-log entry; route source-pin (uses
  `send_password_reset_email` for reset branch + `send_application_approved`
  for activation branch).
- **Full iter 217–219 regression: 92/92 pass** when run together.
- Live UI smoke confirms: celebration hero renders with confetti +
  all 4 testids on `/partner-engineer?subscription=success`;
  drawer footer button now reads "Send sign-in link" with the smart
  routing tooltip.

### Files changed
- `backend/routes/partners.py` (new `send-signin-link` endpoint)
- `backend/tests/test_iter_219g_send_signin_link.py` (new, 8 tests)
- `frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/PartnerApplicationDrawer.js`
  (button rename + handler swap to smart endpoint)

  (celebration hero, param-clone fix)

## Iter 220aa — Embeddable Widget: Log a Fault / Get a Quote (May 27, 2026)

### Context
User asked: "If an engineer or company have their own website, would
it be possible for us to implant an enquiry form or Log a Fault directly
into their website? The fault then goes straight into their app?"

Yes — and turned it into a major acquisition lever for the platform.

### Choices (user-confirmed)
* Both owner flavours: partner_engineer (Log a Fault → svc_job_requests)
  AND organization (Get a Quote → crm2_contacts lead).
* iframe snippet only (no JS SDK).
* Honeypot + per-IP rate limiting (5/hour/token/ip), no CAPTCHA.
* Branded confirmation + 5-second auto redirect/close.
* Engineer review badge shown on the widget header.

### Implementation
- **Backend** (``routes/widget_embed.py``, new ~370 LOC):
  - Public, token-gated:
    - ``GET /api/widget/embed/{token}`` — config (owner, badge,
      branding).
    - ``POST /api/widget/embed/{token}/submit`` — accept fault/lead,
      route to the right collection.
  - Auth'd owner CRUD:
    - ``GET /api/widget/my-embeds``
    - ``POST /api/widget/embeds``
    - ``PATCH /api/widget/embeds/{id}``
    - ``DELETE /api/widget/embeds/{id}`` (soft-revoke)
  - Anti-abuse: ``website`` honeypot field (silent 200 if filled);
    ``widget_submission_log`` collection backs a per-token/IP rolling
    1-hour rate limit (5 max).
  - Submission-count + last_submission_at incremented on the embed
    for dashboard display.
  - New indexes on ``widget_embeds.token`` (unique) and the log table.
- **Frontend**:
  - ``pages/Public/EmbedFaultForm.js`` at ``/embed/log-fault/:token``
    — branded header (engineer photo or initial badge, name, company,
    review badge, "Powered by GymAxis" pill), responsive form, hidden
    honeypot, branded "Thanks" panel with 5s countdown that either
    posts ``window.parent.postMessage({source:'gymaxis-widget',
    event:'close'})`` or redirects to ``redirect_url``.
  - ``components/shared/WidgetEmbedCard.js`` — dashboard snippet
    builder: list existing embeds (with counts), create new, preview,
    copy ``<iframe>`` snippet to clipboard, soft-revoke.
  - Card mounted on Partner Dashboard for approved engineers
    (``ownerType="partner_engineer"``); ready to drop on the
    CRM org-settings page with ``ownerType="organization"``.
- **Tests** (``test_iter_220aa_widget_embed.py``, 18 tests):
  - Public config — engineer + org owner shapes, badge skip,
    404 on bad/revoked tokens, 404 on non-approved partner.
  - Public submit — creates svc_job_requests, creates crm2_contacts
    lead, honeypot silent discard, rate-limit 429, revoked 404.
  - Owner CRUD — partner / org owner path, list isolation,
    soft-revoke, 404 on someone else's widget.
  - Live API round trip (auth → create → public read → public submit
    → revoke → confirm 404).

### Verification
- ``make regression`` → **968 passed**, 15 skipped (+18 new tests,
  zero regressions on the 950 baseline).
- Full live API round trip (E1 engineer): created widget → public
  config returned engineer name + log_fault kind + badge → public
  submit returned ``{ok:true, ref:'cedde507'}`` → honeypot returned
  ``{ok:true, ref:'spam-discarded'}`` → list_my_embeds showed
  count=1 (honeypot did NOT increment).
- Frontend smoke at ``/embed/log-fault/9UE08PZ8Gk7Dcyoo``: renders
  branded header + 8 testids + complete form.
- Partner Dashboard smoke: snippet-builder card visible with the
  live ``<iframe>`` snippet, Preview/Revoke actions.
- ``mcp_lint_python`` + ``mcp_lint_javascript`` both clean.

## (May 27, 2026)

### Implementation — SEO Autopilot
- **Backend** (``routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py``, new ~530 LOC):
  - 11 endpoints under ``/api/marketing/seo`` (admin) and 2 under
    ``/api/blog`` (public):
    - ``POST keywords/research`` — Claude Sonnet 4.6 (via emergentintegrations
      + Emergent LLM key) brainstorms 5–40 long-tail keywords with
      intent/difficulty/volume/rationale, persists each to
      ``seo_keywords`` (status=queued).
    - ``GET keywords`` / ``PATCH keywords/{id}`` / ``DELETE``.
    - ``POST articles/generate`` — Claude produces a 1500-word UK-English
      fitness-tone article (H1, 5–7 H2, FAQ Q&A pairs, on-brand tone)
      then Gemini 3.1 Flash Nano Banana renders a 16:9 hero image. JSON
      parse is fence-aware (handles ```json fences, prose-wrapped,
      naked).
    - ``GET articles`` / ``GET articles/{id}`` / ``PATCH`` / ``DELETE``
      (soft-archive). PATCH stamps ``published_at`` on first transition
      to ``published`` (won't overwrite on republish) and recomputes
      ``word_count`` + ``read_time_min`` on body edits.
    - ``POST autopilot/run`` — picks oldest queued keyword → calls
      ``generate_article(publish_now=True)`` → marks keyword as
      ``status=published`` with ``target_article_id``. Cron-ready
      (1 article/day at the default tier).
    - ``GET dashboard`` — rollup tiles + 10 most recent articles.
    - ``GET /api/blog/posts`` (public, lists published).
    - ``GET /api/blog/posts/{slug}`` (public, increments view counter).
  - All admin endpoints guarded with ``_require_master_admin``.
  - LLM unavailable / key missing → graceful fallback path so the UI
    never breaks (seeds 1 fallback keyword, fallback article body).
  - Slug collisions resolved by appending a 6-char id suffix.
  - Indexes on ``seo_articles.slug`` (unique sparse) + status, and
    ``seo_keywords.status``.

  - ``pages/MasterAdmin/SEOAutopilotPanel.js`` (new ~400 LOC) — 3 sub-

  - ``pages/Marketing/Blog/BlogIndex.js`` — merges DB published posts
    (newest first) with the file-based legacy ``./posts/`` registry.
  - ``pages/Marketing/Blog/BlogPost.js`` — falls back to DB lookup
    when slug isn't in the static registry, renders Markdown body,

## Iter 220cf — SEO Autopilot Daily Cron Catch-Up (Feb 2026)

### Problem
User reported "SEO Autopilot didn't fire today". The
``run_daily_autopilot_loop`` in ``routes/marketing/seo_autopilot.py``
used a strict ``london.hour == cfg_hour`` predicate. The 15-minute
wake-up cadence can drift past the exact hour after a backend
restart or a slow iteration — when that happened, the loop skipped
the entire day silently.

### Fix
Swap the equality check to ``london.hour >= cfg_hour`` AND
``not _autopilot_already_ran_today(today)``. The stamp row in
``seo_autopilot_runs`` keeps the loop idempotent (still at most one
run per London-calendar-day), but now the run is no longer skipped
if the loop ticks late.

## Iter 220cg — Social Card Text Fall-Off + Headline Hygiene (Feb 2026)

### Problem
User reported "Social media AI text falling off the edge & not making
sense". Two root causes:

1. ``_pillow_branded_card_png`` used a fixed 18-char wrap budget.
   On portrait (9:16) TikTok cards the pixel-width-per-character
   easily exceeded the safe right margin → the headline literally
   ran off the card.
2. The over-image headline came verbatim from the LLM and was
   sometimes a teaser ("How to cut downtime…"), a mid-sentence
   fragment ("…the silent killer"), or wrapped in quotes — none of
   which read as a clean standalone headline.

### Fix
- **Pixel-aware word wrap**: ``_pillow_branded_card_png`` now
  measures each candidate line with ``font.getlength()`` against
  a symmetrical safe-width (``w - 2 * text_x``). If the headline
  doesn't fit in 3 lines OR any line exceeds the safe width, font
  shrinks (down to 50% of original) and re-wraps. Single oversized
  words are character-truncated with an ellipsis.
- **Headline cleaner** (new ``clean_card_headline``): strips
  wrapping quotes (straight + curly), trims trailing punctuation,
  caps at 6 words, rejects mid-sentence starters (and/the/when…),
  rejects teaser patterns (``How to …``, ``Why we …``, ``5 ways …``)
  when an ellipsis flagged truncation, preserves brand acronyms
  (PPM, KPIs, GymAxis). Falls back to topic label if cleanup
  empties the string.
- **Prompt tightening**: ``build_prompt`` now explicitly tells the
  LLM the ``card_headline`` must be a "complete 3-5 word thought",
  not a teaser/truncation, with positive + negative examples
  inline.

### Verification
- ``backend/tests/test_iter_220cg_social_card_text_fit.py`` — 16
  new tests pin: quote stripping, trailing-punctuation, 6-word cap,
  bad-starter rejection, teaser-with-ellipsis rejection, brand
  acronym preservation, title-casing, 80-char clip, no near-white
  pixels in the right-margin band for short/long Instagram/TikTok/
  LinkedIn cards, ellipsis truncation on pathological single words,
  prompt schema mentions the headline guardrails, generated post
  stores the CLEANED ``card_headline`` (not the raw LLM string).
- All 62 social-autopilot tests still pass (46 existing + 16 new).

### Files changed
- ``backend/utils/social_autopilot.py`` (~+100 LOC: pixel-aware
  wrap, ``clean_card_headline``, prompt tightening, plumbing in
  ``generate_post_for_channel``)
- ``backend/tests/test_iter_220cg_social_card_text_fit.py`` (new)
- ``Makefile`` (regression entry — TAB-indented)

## Iter 220ci — Engineer Equipment Tab (Feb 2026)

### Problem
Until now, engineers in the field could only PICK from existing
equipment (via the asset combobox inside ``WorkVisitMachinesCard``).
When a machine wasn't already in the operations portal they'd type
a free-text name on the report row, and the asset was never
persisted as a first-class record — leaving the master admin's
equipment list and the field-team's reality out of sync.

User spec: "Engineers must be able to add machines (all fields
mandatory with dropdown boxes to keep text clean). Show the
equipment on the report and job automatically. It should flow
from the operations portal."

### Implementation

**Backend** — new module ``routes/svc/engineer_equipment.py``:
- ``GET /api/svc/engineer/equipment/picklists`` — returns the
  canonical ``equipment_type_options`` (16 entries),
  ``location_options`` (16 entries), ``status_options`` (4 entries)
  + the engineer's org sites for the form.
- ``GET /api/svc/engineer/equipment`` — list scoped to the org with
  optional ``?site_id=`` and ``?q=`` (case-insensitive contains
  across name/serial/model/manufacturer).
- ``POST /api/svc/engineer/equipment`` — strict-validation create:
    - **5 mandatory fields** (server-validated): name,
      equipment_type, manufacturer, model, location.
    - **Strict picklists** (server-rejected when off-list):
      equipment_type, location, status.
    - Multi-site safety: when the org has multiple active sites a
      ``site_id`` is required (400 otherwise); single-site orgs
      auto-inherit the lone site.
    - Optional ``?case_id=`` query — if supplied AND valid for the
      org, ALSO inserts a matching row into
      ``svc_work_visit_machines`` so the new asset auto-appears on
      the current job's report (``attached_to_case=True``).
      Unknown case_id surfaces ``case_skip_reason='case_not_found'``
      without aborting the primary create.
- Writes to the platform-wide ``equipment`` collection (tagged
  ``created_via='engineer_app'``) so the operations portal / master
  admin / customer dashboard see the new row immediately.

**Frontend** — new ``pages/ServiceOps/Engineer/EngineerEquipment.js``:
- List page (default export) — mobile-first card list with site
  filter, search, refresh, "Add" CTA, empty state, status pills.
- Form page (named export ``EngineerEquipmentForm``) — strict
  picklists wired to the backend picklists endpoint, manufacturer
  combobox fed by ``/api/equipment/manufacturers`` with an "Other"
  freetext fallback, inline "Required" errors, site auto-select
  when single-site, ``case_id`` query-param threading for the
  "auto-attach to current job" flow, success toasts and back-nav.

**Wiring**:
- Routes added in ``routes/AppRoutes.js`` for
  ``/svc/engineer/equipment`` (list) and
  ``/svc/engineer/equipment/new`` (form).
- ``EngineerWorkspace.js`` sidebar gets a new nav button
  (``ws-nav-equipment``, shortcut ``e``).
- ``EngineerHomeV2.js`` Quick Actions grid gets an Equipment tile
  (``qa-equipment``).
- ``WorkVisitMachinesCard.js`` (the in-job machines tab) gets a
  "New asset" link (``machines-new-asset-link``) that pre-fills
  ``case_id=`` so creating an asset from a job auto-attaches it.

### Verification

## Iter 220ck — Engineer Customer Onboarding Redesign (Feb 2026)

### Problem
User feedback (2 screenshots): "this section needs to be similar to
how we on board on Master Admin. Quick/easy but in stages. Break the
address box up into separate fields, easier for reporting. Equipment
import within the customer modal (a separate tab). Think logically
how a fitness equipment engineer would like to work."

### Backend
- ``CustomerIn`` / ``CustomerPatch`` schemas now accept the structured
  address fields: ``address_line1``, ``address_line2``, ``city``,
  ``county``, ``postcode``, ``country`` (defaults to "United
  Kingdom") + ``company_number``.
- ``_norm_postcode`` enforces UK formatting (``"ls101ab" → "LS10
  1AB"``) using a regex that requires letters+digits — won't
  accidentally split US zip codes.
- ``_compose_address`` stitches the structured fields back into the
  legacy ``site_address`` column so old reports keep working
  (back-compat with everything before this iter).
- ``_to_doc`` writes both structured + legacy columns and preserves
  an explicit ``site_address`` when the engineer supplies one.
- ``create_customer`` / ``update_customer`` merge/PATCH paths
  whitelist the new columns so structured fields are persisted on
  duplicate-merge as well.

### Frontend — 3-step wizard
``EngineerCustomers.js`` now opens a **3-step wizard** modelled on
the Master Admin onboarding (numbered stepper + Back/Next nav):

1. **Identity** — Companies House lookup (auto-fills name,
   address_line1, line2, city, county, postcode, country, company
   number) → Name + Email + Phone (all mandatory, inline errors).
2. **Site** — Site name + structured address: line1*, line2, City*,
   County, Postcode* (UK formatted), Country (defaults to UK), plus
   access notes.
3. **Equipment** — paste-list textarea + hint pointing to the
   Equipment tab's CSV template + Import (iter 220cj's bulk-import
   path) for engineers with dozens of machines.

The wizard validates per-step (forward blocked until required
fields are filled), jumps to the earliest erroring step on submit,
and pre-fills structured fields when editing an existing customer
(with a legacy fallback to ``site_address`` for pre-220ck rows).

## Iter 220cm — Per-Equipment Service History Rollup (Feb 2026)

### Idea
"Now that imported equipment is bound to a customer, the natural
next step is a Service-history rollup on each equipment row —
every PPM/repair visit auto-aggregates onto the asset card so the
next engineer can scroll back through what's been done."

### Backend
New endpoint
``GET /api/svc/engineer/equipment/{equipment_id}/service-history``
that:

  * Verifies the equipment belongs to the engineer's org (404
    otherwise — cross-tenant safe).
  * Pulls every ``svc_work_visit_machines`` row for ``asset_id ==
    equipment_id``.
  * Joins each row to its parent ``svc_cases`` for case reference,
    title, status, priority, assigned engineer name, completion
    date.
  * Aggregates a per-case photo count via a single
    ``$group`` on ``svc_engineer_photos`` — swallowed
    defensively if the aggregate flakes (analytics-only, never
    breaks the rollup).
  * Returns a sorted-newest-first ``visits`` list + a ``totals``
    strip (visit_count, serviced_count, cleaned_count,
    last_visit) so the UI can render the asset's "what's been
    done" badge without a second round-trip.
  * Respects a ``limit`` query param (default 50, max 200) —
    totals still reflect the full set even when the page is
    clipped.

### Frontend
``EngineerEquipment.js`` rows are now **expandable**:

  * Each row becomes a button — click toggles an inline panel.
  * Service history is **lazy-loaded** on first expand only (a 200-
    row org never hits the API for unread rows).
  * Panel shows the 3-stat strip (Visits / Serviced / Last visit) +
    a compact timeline card per visit (case ref + title, date,
    engineer name, status pill, Serviced/Cleaned ticks, photo
    count, notes excerpt). Older visits beyond 8 are summarised
    inline.
  * Empty state for assets with no history yet:
    "No service visits logged for this asset yet."

### Verification
- **9 new pytest assertions** in
  ``backend/tests/test_iter_220cm_service_history.py`` covering:
  cross-tenant 404, no-org 403, empty-asset response, full join
  with multi-visit timeline + sort + totals + photo count,
  aggregate-error swallowing, ``limit`` clip with intact totals,
  router registration, frontend lazy-load pin, frontend testid
  pins.
- Live e2e via curl: created equipment row → endpoint returned
  the equipment + empty visits / zero totals cleanly.
- Lint clean. 112 pytest assertions across iter 220ci/220cj/
  220ck/220cl/220cm pass.

## Iter 220eb — Live Job Engineer App: 6-bug batch (Jun 3, 2026)

Fixed a batch of field-blocking bugs in the *live job* Engineer App
(`EngineerJobDetailV2.js`, `WorkVisitMachinesCard.js`, `engineerOfflineQueue.js`,
backend `engineer.py` + `service_report.py`). All 6 verified.

1. **Report "Asset" → "Job type"** — `service_report.py` VISIT DETAILS now
   shows a `Job type` row via `_case_type_label()` (Repair / PPM Service / …),
   and only renders an `Asset` row when `asset_name` is a real value (hides
   empty + internal `ASSET_…` slugs). *Verified: PDF shows "Job type: Repair".*
2. **Timer stuck on "syncing" + manual entry** — Root cause: `engineerSendOrQueue`
   was queueing 4xx errors (incl. the 412 H&S gate) as if offline, stranding the
   timer at 0m with a false "queued/Syncing" chip. Now 4xx errors throw with
   `status`/`detail` and the UI surfaces the real reason ("Complete the H&S
   checklist first"). Added `POST /api/svc/engineer/time/manual` (category +
   minutes) and an "Add time manually" card on the Time tab. *Verified by testing agent.*
3. **Equipment per-machine photo button** — verified working end-to-end
   (upload → grid). The cursor-jump fix removed the re-render thrash that made it
   feel unreliable. *Verified: photo grid populated.*
4. **Textarea cursor jump on spacebar** — Root cause: per-keystroke async PATCH
   replaced the whole row object on response, yanking the caret. New
   `MachineTextField` component (local state + 600ms debounce, ignores prop
   updates while focused) for the Work-actioned + Further-work fields.
   *Verified: full sentence preserved, no jump.*
5. **Signature missing on report** — Root cause: signature was saved only if the
   "Signed by" name field was also filled; engineers drew the signature but left
   the name blank, so it was silently dropped. Now saves whenever a signature is
   drawn, defaulting the name to the case customer ("Customer" fallback).
   *Verified: signature persisted with blank name + embedded in PDF.*
6. **Logo missing on report** — Org had no logo configured. Added a default
   GymAxis brand mark (`backend/static/brand/gymaxis-full.png`) fallback so every
   report ships branded. Org/engineer logo still takes precedence.
   *Verified: GYMAXIS logo in PDF header.*

### Next phase (user-requested, NOT yet built)
**Configurable Case Types** in Account Settings — let orgs edit case types, define
**custom questions per type**, and ship **distinct report templates per type**
(a PPM report should look different from a Repair report). See ROADMAP P1.

- Frontend: new `CRMClearPriceListModal.js` (owner-only red "Clear price list" button in `CRMProductsSection`, with Export-backup-first nudge, two modes, typed DELETE). Import wizard (`CRMPriceListImportWizard`) preview now shows a "Duplicate codes" stat + a duplicate-codes panel (code ×N with sheet/row), and the result step shows the skipped breakdown.
- Verified: backend guards (400/403/deleted-0 on fake batch), `_validate_products` unit test (A1 ×3 across sheets), modal screenshot (53 all / 47 last import). NOTE: lint shows pre-existing React-Compiler `set-state-in-effect`/unescaped-entity errors that also appear in untouched CRM files — not introduced here. ## Iter 221 — Fix: org owners couldn't see "Clear price list" (Jun 7, 2026)
- BUG: Non-master org owner (e.g. Lee Somers) couldn't see/use Clear price list; only master admin could.
- ROOT CAUSE: the CRM cross-login bridge (`routes/crm_auth.crm_cross_login`) stores bridged platform users as CRM role "manager" (only master → "admin"), so the owner's CRM identity lost ownership. Both the frontend `isOwner` and backend `_is_owner` failed for role "manager".
- FIX: bridge now computes `is_org_owner` (platform role=='owner' OR `organizations.owner_id`==user) and (a) stores it on the `crm_users` doc (create + backfill on sync), (b) returns it in the cross-login response user and in `GET /api/crm/auth/me`. `crm_products._is_owner` now also passes when `user.is_org_owner`. Frontend `CRMProductsSection.isOwner` now includes `user?.is_org_owner`.
- Verified (curl, non-master owner jack.ottey@thirdspace.london): cross-login → `is_org_owner:true`, `/auth/me` → `is_org_owner:true`, `POST /api/crm/products/bulk-delete` with owner token → `deleted:0` (allowed, was 403). UI screenshot blocked by test-harness login flakiness; the button is driven solely by this now-true flag. Preview-only — REDEPLOY for production (gymaxisai.com).

**Context**: building toward selling Service Desk + Engineer App as a self-serve package to service suppliers (ERP optional, self-serve + supported). User's explicit gate: Operations Portal data must keep flowing to/from the Service Desk for customers on the ops portal.
**Gap found & FIXED**: the FORWARD bridge existed (`routes/issues._mirror_issue_to_svc_case`: ops fault escalated→engineer creates `svc_cases` row stamped `source_meta.issue_id`) but there was NO REVERSE flow — a completed case left the gym's portal fault stuck "open".
**Built** `utils/svc_ops_bridge.mirror_case_state_to_issue` + hooked into the canonical `utils.svc_state.transition` (fire-and-forget, after comms notify) so EVERY path (engineer complete, desk status change, sign-off, inbound Sicon sync) mirrors back. Keyed purely on `source_meta.issue_id` within the org → GENERIC for any supplier, not just Pulse. Maps: en_route→engineer_assigned_at/first_response_at; on_site→engineer_arrived_at/work_started_at; repaired/awaiting_sign_off→work_completed_at; closed→issue.status='resolved'+resolved_at+resolution_type='engineer'+resolved_by; rejected→timeline note (stays open). Always stamps `linked_case_id`/`linked_case_reference`/`case_status`/`last_case_sync_at` + pushes an issue `timeline` entry (source='service_desk') so the gym sees live progress.

### SELLABILITY ASSESSMENT (recorded for roadmap)
Platform is ~85% there technically. Service Desk (45+ endpoints) + Engineer App (PWA w/ offline, 15 endpoints) + true multi-tenancy + white-label branding + optional ERP (Sicon/Sage degrade gracefully) + Stripe Connect engineer payouts. GAPS to sell as a packaged Service Provider SKU:

- 🔴 P0 Self-serve setup wizard (case types, SLAs, cover types, picklists, branding, first engineer).

## Iter 264 — SEO blog duplicate posts: root cause + permanent fix (Jun 12, 2026)
**User report (production)**: duplicate blog posts on gymaxisai.com/blog keep recurring. Confirmed via prod API: 2 pairs with IDENTICAL titles published 4s/12s apart (Jun 6 08:09, Jun 11 08:13), second slug suffixed `-xxxxxx`.
**ROOT CAUSE**: `run_daily_autopilot_loop` was check-then-act — read the `seo_autopilot_runs` daily stamp, spent minutes on LLM generation, stamped only AFTER publishing. Production runs >1 backend process, each starting its own loop at boot → both passed the check in the same 15-min window → both published. (Preview never reproduces: single process.) Same racy pattern existed in the social autopilot loop.
**FIX (3 layers)**:
1. `utils/daily_run_lock.py` → `claim_daily_run(collection, date)` — atomic per-day claim BEFORE any work (unique index on `date`, $setOnInsert token CAS, stale-crash reclaim after 120min). Wired into both SEO + social daily loops.
2. Publish-time guard in `generate_article`: base-slug collision with equal normalised title (`_norm_title`) → `held_duplicate_title=True` → status forced to `needs_review`, never auto-published.
3. `dedupe_published_duplicate_titles()` — idempotent startup migration (runs in `init_seo_indexes` every boot): groups published articles by normalised title, keeps the EARLIEST (original Google-indexed slug), archives the rest with `archived_reason=duplicate_title_auto_dedupe`. **Production self-heals on next redeploy.**
**Tests**: test_iter264_seo_duplicate_fix.py 7/7 (concurrency exclusivity, completed-day, stale reclaim, fresh-claim protection, dedupe keep-oldest + idempotency, source pins, unique index) — added to Makefile. Existing seo autopilot suite 28/28.
NOTE: preview DB had no duplicates (single-process). The 4 prod duplicates will be auto-archived when the user REDEPLOYS.

## Fix: Pulse LITE "Log a Fault" — Serial Number dropdown closed the modal (Jun 24, 2026)
Reported (production): in the Log a Fault modal, the Serial Number dropdown showed no serials and clicking it CLOSED the whole modal. Initial fix had been applied to Pro `Dashboard/FaultDialogs.js`, but testing revealed `owner@isodemo.com` is on **Pulse LITE**, which uses `LiteDashboard/LiteDialogs.js` — so the user-facing bug lived there.
Root cause: the Lite `FaultMachineSelector` used Radix `<Select>` for Machine Type + Serial; clicking an option in the Radix portal bubbled a pointer-down-outside event to the parent Dialog (which only prevented outside-close when a duplicate/success modal was open), closing the modal mid-selection.
Fix (`LiteDialogs.js`): (1) converted Machine Type (`lite-fault-machine-select`) and Serial Number (`lite-fault-serial-select`) to native HTML `<select>` with onKeyDown stopPropagation; (2) hardened the Log Fault `DialogContent` to ALWAYS preventDefault on onPointerDownOutside/onInteractOutside/onFocusOutside/onEscapeKeyDown (mirrors FaultDialogs.js) so no in-dialog interaction can dismiss it — closes only via X/Cancel/completed submit; (3) added sr-only `DialogDescription` to the Log Fault + Equipment Detail dialogs (a11y warning).
Verified by testing_agent: 100% on 8 Lite log-fault scenarios (machine select, photo upload, outside-click, Escape, description+severity, submit→duplicate-detect confirm) — modal stays open throughout. Report: `/app/test_reports/iteration_logfault_lite_native_select_jan2026.json`. PREVIEW only — redeploy to push to pulsefitness.ai.
**Next**: ModulePageHeader quick-action buttons (P1), Stripe membership billing (P0), Sicon/Sage ERP (P0), proactive weekly "Comms brief" (P2).

**1. Banner text wash-out (light mode).** The Pulse Lite "Unlock everything for 3 days, free" upsell banner headline was near-invisible in light mode. Root cause: global `[data-theme="light"] .text-white { color: var(--theme-text) }` flips white→dark, but the banner sits on a permanently-dark gradient. Fix: added a reusable **`.on-dark`** utility class in `index.css` (preserves `.text-white` on always-dark surfaces in light mode + pulse light portal) and applied it to `PulseProUpgradeCta.js`. Verified via computed-style probe (white inside `.on-dark`, dark elsewhere).
**2. Upgrade unlocked NOTHING (only full Operations).** Clicking "Try Pulse Pro free" flipped account_type→pulse_pro but left Memberships/CRM/Marketing locked, so the user still needed a master admin to enable them. Root cause: the default Lite seed marks bolt-ons `{enabled:false, source:"admin"}` — IDENTICAL to a deliberate master-admin disable — so `trial_status.admin_disabled` was always True and `upgrade_to_pulse_pro` skipped starting every trial.

Paid/admin-granted modules (source!="trial") are unaffected.
  - Verified: API E2E (upgrade → all 3 module_access True, trials active 3d) + DB-simulated expiry (module_access back to False, status "used") + 5-scenario unit test of `resolve_module_access`. `iso-demo-org` reset to clean Lite for fresh demo.

## CRITICAL ROOT-CAUSE FIX: "Log a Fault modal closes when selecting a machine" (Jun 29, 2026)
Recurring bug (patched piecemeal 4×) finally root-caused. User report: on the FULL dashboard (`/dashboard` → `FaultDialogs.js`, account_type=full), selecting a serial number closed the whole Log-a-Fault modal. Reproduced via Playwright: serial select fired `history.back()` → `popstate` → dialog closed (no JS error).
**Root cause** (`lib/useBackGestureClose.js`): the hook listed `onClose` in its effect deps. Callers pass an inline/`useCallback` onClose whose identity changes every render. The serial `onChange` fires several state updates in a row (setIssueForm + fetchCoverage + setExistingFaultWarning) → effect re-ran → its cleanup called `window.history.back()` mid-interaction → the resulting popstate was caught by the just-registered listener → `onClose()` → the dialog shut itself. The machine-type select (single state update) survived; the multi-update serial select did not.
**Fix:** hold `onClose` in a ref (`onCloseRef`) and narrow the effect deps to `[open, key]`, so it fires exactly once per open/close and never on incidental re-renders. Single shared-hook fix → benefits all 3 consumers (`FaultDialogs`, `LiteDialogs`, `AdminOrganizations`).
**Also fixed:** (a) the serial `<option>` in `FaultDialogs.js` + `LiteDialogs.js` collapsed to a single template-literal child — a multi-expression `<option>` threw a React "span cannot be a child of option" error (editor span-wrapping); (b) the existing-fault warning's "Continue Anyway" button got a proper primary style + `.on-dark` class (its `text-white` was being flipped dark by the light-mode override).
**User requirement delivered:** selecting a machine with open faults now shows the existing-fault notification ("2 open faults already logged for Life Fitness Treadmill" + fault chips) with **Continue Anyway** (dismiss warning, keep logging) vs **Cancel** — instead of closing.
**Verified:** testing_agent 100% frontend (primary bug resolved end-to-end, no console error, master admin regression clean) — report `/app/test_reports/iteration_logfault_back_gesture_hook_jan2026.json`; plus own Playwright repro+fix. iso-demo-org = account_type `full`. PREVIEW only — redeploy to push to pulsefitness.ai.

## Fix: "Running AI Triage (2 machines)" shown for a single-machine fault (Jun 29, 2026)
On the FULL dashboard Log-a-Fault, submitting ONE machine showed "Running AI Triage (2 machines)…". Root cause (`FaultDialogs.js` + `hooks/useIssueWorkflow.js`): `handleIssueSubmit` calls `setFaultMachines(machines)` (folding the active form into `faultMachines`) BEFORE the loading label renders, but the label formula still added `+ (issueForm.serial_number ? 1 : 0)` → the in-progress machine was counted twice (1 in faultMachines + 1 from the serial check).
Fix: added a `submitCount` state captured = `machines.length` right before the fold; the loading label now uses `submitCount` (and shows the singular "Running AI Triage" when count ≤ 1). The pre-submit "Submit" label now also decides singular/multi by the true total (>1) instead of `faultMachines.length > 0`. Passed `submitCount` through `DashboardPage → FaultDialogs`. Lite (`LiteDialogs`) keeps `stagedMachines` separate from the active form (no fold), so its `stagedMachines.length + 1` was already correct — no change.
Verified via Playwright: 1 machine → pre-submit "Submit & Run AI Triage", loading "Running AI Triage…" (singular, no "(2 machines)").

## CRITICAL FIX: admin-enabled modules not granted on Lite/Pro orgs (Jun 29, 2026, prod-reported)
Production: Pulse Fitness Ltd had all 4 modules toggled ON in the Feature Control panel, but the operator only saw Operations (module switcher hid Memberships/CRM/Marketing). Root cause = a REGRESSION from the Jun 29 trial work: `utils/module_access._org_module_access` had a hard branch `if account_type == "lite" and key in BOLT_ON_MODULES: out[key] = _trial_active(...)` which forced ALL bolt-ons on a Lite org to be trial-gated, IGNORING an explicit master-admin enable (`enabled:true, source:"admin"`). `/auth/me` therefore returned memberships/crm/marketing = false, and `ModuleSwitcher.hasAccess` (which trusts the explicit `module_access` flag) hid them.
Fix: rewrote the bolt-on resolution to a single tier-agnostic rule — `source=="trial"` → gated on `_trial_active`; else `enabled` (admin/paid) → granted for ANY account_type incl. Lite; else off → granted only if a trial is active. Removed the `account_type=="lite"` hard gate. Operations (core) follows the flag/default.
Verified: 6 logic scenarios (Lite all-admin-enabled→all True, Lite default→ops only, Lite active trial→memberships, Pro expired trial→re-locks, Full→all) + e2e (pulse_pro all-admin-enabled org: `/auth/me` returns all True; ModuleSwitcher shows Operations/Memberships/CRM/Marketing/Comms on BOTH desktop & mobile (scrollable pills); Memberships module reachable + renders on mobile, no upgrade gate). Trial flow + post-trial subscribe still correct. iso-demo-org restored to `full`. PREVIEW only — user must REDEPLOY to fix production pulsefitness.ai.

## Changelog — 2026-06 (MOD Automatic Quote Writer)
New feature in CRM → Corporate → Quotes (CPQ). Generates MOD PTE Service & Repair quotes on Pulse Fitness paperwork, driven by the contracted Schedule of Rates (SOR from Schedule B) and linked to the MOD equipment lists. Follows the StOR (Schedule C): Type A = all-inclusive 12-month UK service (per item/year); Type B = ad-hoc UK call-out (+£80 call-out); Type C/Repairs/Refurb = POA (custom price).

## Changelog — 2026-06 (fork) · Offline-resilient language preference
- Problem: i18next already caches the active language to localStorage (offline-safe), BUT `App.js` re-applied the
  server-side `user.language` on every hydrate — so a language a field engineer picked WHILE OFFLINE (whose profile
  PATCH failed and was swallowed) got reverted to the stale server value on reconnect.
- New helper `utils/languagePref.js`: `setLanguagePreference(lang)` switches UI + writes localStorage immediately, then
  best-effort PATCHes `/account/profile`; on failure it queues the choice under `pf_lang_pending`.
  `flushPendingLanguageSync()` retries the queued sync. `hasPendingLanguageSync()` exposes the marker.
- `App.js`: hydrate effect now treats a `pf_lang_pending` value as AUTHORITATIVE (keeps it, re-pushes to server) so a
  stale server language never reverts an offline pick; added a `window 'online'` listener that flushes the queue on
  reconnect.
- Wired all 3 authenticated language switchers through the helper: `LanguagePrompt.jsx`, `LanguageSwitcher.js`,
  `Navbar.js` (public/anonymous switchers on LoginPage/PulseLanding/MarketingShell left as-is — they don't sync).
- Verified (Playwright, deterministic route-mocking): Phase A — reload with stale server lang 'de' keeps offline pick
  'fr', clears pending, PATCHes {language:'fr'}. Phase B — offline change queues pf_lang_pending='de', firing 'online'
  flushes it and PATCHes {language:'de'}. UI confirmed rendering French.

## Bug Fix — 2026-08-03 · Runaway duplicate "MOD Estate readiness" emails (48/hour)
- SYMPTOM: service@service.pulsefitness.ai sent 48 identical "MOD Estate readiness — 0/1 sites go-live ready"
  emails in an hour (~every 2-3 min).
- ROOT CAUSE: broken per-ISO-week idempotency lock in utils/mod_readiness_digest.py::send_mod_readiness_email.
  It claimed the week with update_one({'job':JOB_KEY,'week_tag':{'$ne':week_tag}}, {'$set':...}, upsert=True). That
  filter can never match the current-week doc, so upsert INSERTED a fresh system_jobs doc every run and the skip
  condition (modified_count==0 AND upserted_id is None) was never true → emailed on EVERY poller tick. Today being
  Monday (ISO 2026-W32), the sicon_poller weekly gate (Monday & hour>=9 UTC) passed on every cycle.
- FIX: atomic once-per-week claim — update_one({'job':JOB_KEY,'week_tag':week_tag}, {'$setOnInsert':{...}},
  upsert=True); skip when upserted_id is None. Post-send status update also scoped to (job, week_tag). Deduped leaked
  system_jobs docs; left exactly one 2026-W32 claim in place so the poller won't resend this week.
- VERIFIED by testing_agent: 7/7 pytest passed (100%). First call sends, subsequent calls skip; 10 rapid calls → 1
  send + 9 skips; no doc leak; force=True still sends; weekly cron never double-sends. Regression suite at
  /app/backend/tests/test_mod_readiness_idempotency.py.
- Defence-in-depth suggestion (not done): add a unique index on system_jobs(job, week_tag).

## Changelog — 2026-08-09 (fork) · Help Centre empty for MOD — 401 auth fix
- Root cause: the web app authenticates via an httpOnly cookie (AUTH_COOKIE_NAME) and stores only a 6-char placeholder in localStorage['token']. HelpCentrePage sends `Authorization: Bearer <placeholder>`, and routes/help.py get_current_principal did `token = bearer or cookie` — the non-empty invalid bearer shadowed the valid cookie → verify_token fails → 401 on ALL /api/help/* for cookie-auth (MOD) sessions, so guides/categories were always empty.
- Fix: get_current_principal now tries bearer THEN cookie (uses whichever verify_token accepts). Verified in-browser: /api/help/categories → 200 role=owner 12 cats; Help Centre lists 77 guides (33 under module=operations) + all category counts. No content was missing — the corpus (GUIDES in help_data.py) already existed.
- Note: guides are generic Pulse product docs; the MOD-specific "Portal User Guide" card (added earlier) covers MOD workflows. Adding MOD-tagged articles remains an optional enhancement.

- COMPLETES the last in-progress security item. When a critical/abuse security event lands, the Master Admin now gets an INSTANT in-app toast (10s short-poll) instead of waiting for the 15s Security Alert Centre refresh.
- Backend: utils/security_alerts.py dispatch_alert() now (1) queues an in-app row to new collection `security_alert_feed` (un-throttled, primary channel) and (2) sends a throttled best-effort email to MASTER_ADMIN_EMAIL. Wired into utils/security_events.log_security_event() so any alertable event (severity=critical OR type in {abuse_detected, abuse_action_blocked, bola_cross_tenant_denied, cross_site_denied, contract_send_blocked_unapproved, step_up_failed}) fires automatically. Fixed naive/aware datetime bug in _throttled().
- New endpoints (master-admin only): GET /api/master-admin/security-centre/alerts?since=<iso> (returns unacked alerts newest-first + server_time) and POST /api/master-admin/security-centre/alerts/ack {ids:[...]}. Feed has TTL index (SECURITY_ALERT_FEED_TTL, default 7d), bootstrapped in server.py startup.
- Frontend: MasterAdminPage.js polls the alerts endpoint every 10s (only while console is open), raises notify.error (critical) / notify.warning toasts via the global banner host with a "View in Security Centre" action, then acks so each alert toasts exactly once. Poll `since` seeded to page-load time (pre-existing alerts don't retro-toast).
- User choices: 10s interval, console-only polling, email best-effort (Resend key invalid on PREVIEW → email fails there; works in production after redeploy — in-app toast is primary and fully working).
- Testing: backend curl-verified (emit → feed → poll → ack → count 0); frontend E2E 100% (report iteration_realtime_security_alerts_toast_jan2026.json — toast appears <=10s, correct copy, action navigates, no duplicates over 2+ poll cycles).

## Bugfix — 2026-08-10 (fork) · Homepage Sign-In modal stalled under MFA enforcement (FIXED)
- Symptom (user report): master admin signs in via the marketing HOMEPAGE 'Sign In' modal → spinner runs briefly then stops, nothing happens.
- Root cause: with ENFORCE_MASTER_ADMIN_MFA on, /auth/login returns an MFA challenge {requires_mfa_enrolment} with NO token. The homepage LoginModal (PulseLandingPage.js) only handled res.data.token, so it silently did nothing. (The dedicated /login page already handled MFA; the modal did not.)
- Fix: LoginModal.handleSubmit now detects res.data.requires_mfa_enrolment || res.data.requires_mfa and hands off to the /login page via in-memory router state: navigate('/login', { state:{ mfaChallenge:{ kind:'enrol'|'verify', temp_token, email } } }). LoginPage.js has a mount useEffect that consumes location.state.mfaChallenge — 'enrol' -> POST /auth/mfa/enrol/setup then shows gx-login-enrol-form; 'verify' -> shows gx-login-mfa-form. temp_token is in-memory only (never persisted); history.replaceState clears it to prevent replay. No password re-entry.
- Testing: testing_agent 100% (2/2) — report iteration_master_admin_mfa_homepage_modal_handoff_jan2026.json. Both first-login forced enrolment and subsequent verify reach /master-admin from the homepage modal. End state unchanged: flag ON + admin NOT enrolled.

## Changelog — 2026-08-10 (fork) · MFA recovery: regenerate backup codes + break-glass (COMPLETE)
- Closes the recovery loop now that ENFORCE_MASTER_ADMIN_MFA is ON and the master admin cannot self-disable.
- Backend: utils/mfa.py regenerate_backup_codes(user_id, code) — requires a LIVE TOTP (a backup code is NOT accepted, so a single leaked backup code can't mint a new set), atomically replaces all backup_codes + sets backup_codes_regenerated_at. Endpoint POST /api/auth/mfa/backup-codes/regenerate {code} (get_current_user), audited as security_audit_log event mfa.backup_codes_regenerated.

## Bugfix — 2026-08-10 (fork) · CRM Territories: coverage now shows on BOTH county + postcode maps (FIXED)
- Symptom (production): user coloured counties for staff coverage; switching to the 'Postcode areas' layer showed a BLANK map. Expected coverage on both layers.
- Root cause: coverage stored in two independent buckets (coverage.counties[name], coverage.postcode_areas[code]) with no shared key, so each layer only rendered its own bucket.
- Fix (CRMTerritoryMap.js): added a geometric county↔postcode-area BRIDGE — areaCountyMap useMemo maps each county to the postcode area whose polygon contains the county's centroid (d3-geo geoCentroid + geoContains), with a distance-capped (<1.0 deg²) nearest-centroid fallback for islands (Shetland→ZE) that deliberately does NOT mis-map Northern Ireland (no 'BT' area exists on the postcode layer) across the Irish Sea. effectiveList(type,code) returns direct assignments UNION assignments inherited from the bridged layer (deduped by rep). membersFor / isOverlap / overlapRegions now use effectiveList, so fills + overlap warnings reflect coverage on BOTH layers. Assignment writes still go to the native bucket (no backend change).
- Offline check: 73/74 counties resolve (GM→M, Merseyside→L, West Midlands→B, Shetland→ZE); NI counties correctly map to nothing.
- Testing: testing_agent 100% (report iteration_crm_territories_county_postcode_bridge_jan2026.json) — county paint (Greater Manchester) lights up postcode 'M'; postcode paint ('B') lights up West Midlands county; unrelated ZE/Cornwall stay neutral; cleanup restored demo data. This is a PREVIEW fix — user must REDEPLOY to apply on production.
